We extend the results to $L$-dependent data with long-run variance weights under stronger moment assumptions. Simulations show that the averaged estimator approaches offline two-step GMM in accuracy and coverage at $10^6$ observations, while requiring a fraction of its computing time and fixed memory at up to $10^7$ observations. The online test achieves correct size and comparable power. In an application estimating the effect of a third child on weeks worked using $254{,}654$ women from the 1980 US Census, single-pass estimates agree with offline GMM within a fraction of a standard error on average across data orderings, and both methods yield the same overidentification-test conclusion in most orderings.

papers.title: Temporal Evidence Forests for Long-Horizon Multi-Party Conversational Memory
papers.abstract: Long-term memory has been widely adopted in LLM-based agents to support persistent interaction and personalized assistance. Long-term multi-party interactions, however, accumulate substantially more detailed information, with decisions repeatedly updated and states evolving across participants and interaction stages. Temporal structure is therefore crucial for tracing such memories: relevant information often appears densely within short intervals, while transitions among different states are anchored by a strict temporal order. Existing temporally aware memory frameworks primarily store time as metadata or use temporal signals to guide retrieval over preconstructed memory structures, without using temporal structure to both recover locally concentrated evidence and reconstruct its complete event progression. To address these limitations, we propose T-Mem, a temporal-structure-based memory framework that preserves interactions and organizes query-relevant evidence through two temporal mechanisms. Temporal Evidence Discovery exploits the local concentration of related messages to recover overlooked evidence, while Temporal Memory Structuring models state transitions and supporting relations over time and compresses low-information spans within the resulting forest. Evidence Forest Linearization then serializes the structured evidence for answer generation. Experiments on two long-term multi-party memory benchmarks demonstrate that T-Mem consistently outperforms competitive memory frameworks across LLMs, parameter settings, domains, and query types.

papers.title: The Financing of Debt Relief: Intermediary Liquidity and the Value of Borrower Information
papers.abstract: I study how intermediary liquidity affects mortgage resolution using 1.9 million Ginnie Mae buyout options from 2019 to 2022. When funding markets froze in 2020, nonbank issuers repurchased far fewer delinquent loans than depositories servicing loans in the same pools and, within the same issuer and month, shifted repurchases away from large balances, the loans that require the most cash. About $19 billion of repurchases were delayed, and most were completed later. A model of rationing by value per dollar of cash explains this pattern and shows that borrower information is most valuable when funding is intermediate.

papers.title: When Solvers Get Moody: Quantifying and Predicting Performance Variability in Mixed Integer Programming
papers.abstract: Mixed-integer programming (MIP) solvers are widely used, yet their performance can vary substantially even under seemingly neutral perturbations. Such variability complicates benchmarking, and the interpretation of computational studies. We introduce the Weighted Variability Score (WVS), a robust multi-component metric that aggregates dispersion in normalized runtime, final optimality gap, LP iterations, and branch-and-bound nodes across repeated runs. On a large subset of MIPLIB 2017 instances, each solved in 100 randomized runs under a four-hour limit, WVS reveals a right-skewed distribution with a substantial upper tail: many instances are essentially stable, but some exhibit large variability that is not explained by basic properties alone. Notably, this experiment proved optimality for the open instance 'neos-5045105-creuse' in two SCIP runs. Using static descriptors and root-level features, a tree-based predictor with a gated tail uplift achieves a mean absolute error of 0.058 and Spearman rank correlation of 0.65 on a sealed test split. Feature-importance analysis highlights root degeneracy, matrix structure, coefficient ranges, and presolve reductions as the main drivers of high WVS. Because variability is systematic and partially predictable from inexpensive early-run features, our findings offer a practical tool for preemptive tuning and lay a foundation for fairer evaluation of new algorithms.

papers.title: TAME-Nav: Temporal Asymmetric Mixture-of-Experts Distillation for Agile and Versatile Robot Navigation
papers.abstract: Agile and reliable navigation is a core capability for embodied robots navigating complex spatial constraints and dynamic interactions. However, a single policy often struggles to accommodate the distinct decision-making demands of diverse scenarios. We present TAME-Nav, an asymmetric Teacher-Student navigation framework built around a temporal soft mixture of experts (Soft-MoE). The Teacher combines clean observations with causally maintained dynamic-obstacle tracks to construct privileged representations, while the Student learns complementary navigation features from corrupted observation histories through temporal encoding, soft expert routing, and latent distillation. Procedural scenario generation and parallel task-level simulation broaden training coverage, while deployment-informed asymmetric domain randomization supports sim-to-real transfer. Across in-distribution and unseen compositional scenarios, TAME-Nav achieves higher success rates, lower collision rates, and higher navigation scores than representative baselines. On a real quadruped robot, it completes all twenty trials across local-trap escape and narrow-passage navigation with sudden dynamic obstacles, with only one minor contact.

papers.title: Beyond the Monolithic Interface: A Research Agenda for Plural Conversational AI
papers.abstract: The current paradigm of artificial intelligence (AI) design elevates conversational chatbot interfaces, making them the default mode through which hundreds of millions of people interact with AI systems globally. This narrative review identifies three related harms produced by the single-voice chatbot interface, drawing on insights from literature in cognitive science, political studies, AI alignment, game design and human computer interaction. Firstly, cognitive offloading of user thinking, secondly, ideological narrowing of user beliefs, and thirdly, epistemic compression of cultural and value diversity. We then propose multi-persona interfaces, in which multiple personas are presented to the user simultaneously, as a cost-effective intervention that addresses all three harms at once. We ground this intervention in traditions the AI literature has largely overlooked, drawing on techniques from game design and participatory simulation, including the magic circle, role differentiation, and persona embodiment. We propose a taxonomy for the future design of multi-persona interfaces, and call for a research agenda that closes the gap between technical pluralistic alignment methods and empirical studies of human-AI interactions with pluralistic interfaces.

papers.title: One-Step Text Generation by Seq-Drifting
papers.abstract: Diffusion language models generate tokens in parallel, but still require multiple sampling steps to produce high-quality text. In this paper, we investigate whether a model can learn to generate an entire sequence in a single forward pass. We propose Seq-Drifting, a framework that applies drifting to sequences of continuous token representations and directly learns a map from Gaussian noise to text. Unlike existing DLMs that derive the supervision at each position directly from the observed token in a training sequence, Seq-Drifting builds a drift field whose position-wise targets adapt to the current generated context. At each position, attraction guides each output toward a set of contextually plausible token representations, while repulsion discourages collapse across samples and repetition within sequences. The generator learns from this drift field during training and produces all tokens jointly in one pass at inference. Empirically, Seq-Drifting achieves a generative perplexity of 36.01 on LM1B in one step and performs competitively in both unconditional and conditional generation. Experiments on translation, summarization, and reasoning further demonstrate the applicability of the framework beyond open-ended generation. These results suggest that drifting over token sequences offers a promising path toward effective one-step text generation. Our code is available at https://github.com/jyliu-ai/Seq-Drifting.

papers.title: Decomposing the Kinematics of SNR G180.0-01.7 with Medium-Resolution Spectra
papers.abstract: The exceptionally large angular diameter and intrinsic optical faintness of the Galactic supernova remnant (SNR) G180.0-01.7 (S147) have historically hindered a comprehensive spectroscopic census of its filamentary structure. We present the first dedicated medium-resolution (R ~ 7500) spectroscopic study of S147 using the LAMOST Medium-Resolution Spectroscopic survey of Galactic Nebulae (MRS-N). By implementing multi-Gaussian decomposition on the H$α$, [NII], and [SII] emission complexes and applying combined spectroscopic and spatial criteria, we disentangle the shock-ionized filaments of the SNR from the pervasive foreground and background Diffuse Ionized Gas (DIG). Our analysis reveals a distinct bimodal radial velocity distribution for the SNR: a low-velocity population tracing the decelerated forward shock at a dense cavity wall, and a high-velocity population (with absolute radial velocities of ~ 70 $\pm$ 30 km/s) corresponding to ejecta within a low-density cavity. The co-existence of these populations provides kinematic evidence for the "supernova-in-a-cavity" scenario. Furthermore, we detect enhanced [SII]/H$α$ ratios in the DIG along the eastern and northern boundaries of the remnant, signaling shock compression of the ambient interstellar medium and highlighting remnant's multifaceted feedback.

papers.title: Mind the Spatial Gap: A Benchmark for Geospatial Reasoning and Constrained Spatial Editing
papers.abstract: Understanding and manipulating spatial relations is fundamental to AI systems that reason about physical environments and construct grounded world models. However, existing evaluations of multimodal large language models (MLLMs) for spatial reasoning rely predominantly on static question-answering (QA) over small-scale or synthetic scenes, rarely probing whether models can modify spatial configurations while satisfying explicit geometric constraints. We introduce GeoSpatialBench, a benchmark designed to evaluate an escalating progression of spatial cognition, ranging from spatial relation understanding and geometric reasoning to constrained spatial editing. Grounded in real-world urban data across six geographically diverse cities, GeoSpatialBench evaluates a comprehensive taxonomy of 28 topological, directional, metric, and ordering relations across structured GeoJSON and map image modalities, with ground-truth references and constraints verified via GIS operations. Our empirical evaluation across frontier MLLMs uncovers a stark spatial gap: structured GeoJSON consistently outperforms map images, with multimodal combinations offering no reliable gain over GeoJSON alone, and while models show reasonable competence on qualitative topological and ordering, performance drops on quantitative metric relations. Crucially, editing performance on ordering relations declines relative to QA, and most failed edits violate at least one specified spatial constraint. These results highlight a gap between passively recognizing spatial relations and actively manipulating geometric configurations. GeoSpatialBench provides an open, rigorous diagnostic testbed to benchmark these spatial limitations, laying essential empirical groundwork for physically grounded world models and embodied spatial AI.

papers.title: Undiscovering Quark-gluon Plasma
papers.abstract: Quark-gluon plasma (QGP) is a conjectured state of matter wherein the quarks and gluons of QCD theory, usually confined within the nucleons in atomic nuclei, are deconfined under conditions of extremely high temperature and pressure. According to the current understanding of big-bang evolution, conditions compatible with QGP formation existed for a brief early period as the universe expanded and cooled. In that scenario present matter in the universe in some sense emerged from ``freezeout'' of the primordial QGP. This article describes the rise and fall of a community effort to create QGP in the laboratory and study its properties.

papers.title: HART: Hybrid Attention-RWKV Time series Foundation Model
papers.abstract: Non-autoregressive multi-step forecasting (NAF) enables time series foundation models to predict an entire future horizon in a single forward pass. Despite its strong sequence modeling capabilities, RWKV-7 exhibits long-horizon degradation in our NAF experiments. In this setup, future patches are represented as missing inputs, requiring the recurrent state to evolve across the prediction horizon without new observations. Our analysis of RWKV-7's generalized delta rule suggests a mechanism we term Placeholder Idling Decay (PID): repeated state transitions can attenuate historical information when placeholder-driven writes provide insufficient compensation. Layer-wise analysis reveals reduced state-injection norms in most layers, while transition-matrix norms remain similar between historical and prediction regions, consistent with PID. Motivated by this analysis, we propose HART, a Hybrid Attention-RWKV Time-series Foundation Model that alternates attention and RWKV blocks, combining direct access to historical tokens with recurrent temporal modeling. Controlled experiments on GIFT-Eval and TIME-Benchmark show that HART improves over pure RWKV at medium and long horizons while maintaining comparable short-horizon performance, and achieves better aggregate performance than a comparably sized pure Transformer. With 36M parameters, HART achieves long-horizon MASE comparable to Toto-2.0-1B on GIFT-Eval (0.752 vs. 0.754), using approximately 1/28 of its parameters.

papers.title: Parametrized Jacobian Problem over $\mathbb{C}^n$ and its Complete Resolution
papers.abstract: We formulate a parametrized Jacobian Problem over $\mathbb{C}^{n}$ by incorporating independent scale parameters into the linear part of a polynomial map via polar decomposition. We prove that requiring the Jacobian determinant to remain constant uniformly across the parameter space decouples the Jacobian equation into a system enforcing the vanishing of all principal minors of the perturbation matrix. This system strictly forces lower triangularization up to variable permutations, establishing a necessary and sufficient condition for polynomial invertibility throughout the parameter family and providing an explicit, canonical scheme for constructing the inverse map in every dimension.

papers.title: CoGameReg: Cooperative-Game-Based Collaborative Semi-Supervised Regression for Seismic Reservoir Property Prediction
papers.abstract: Accurate estimation of reservoir properties from seismic data remains challenging when well-log labels are sparse but three-dimensional seismic observations are abundant. We present CoGameReg, a cooperative-game-based semi-supervised regression framework that uses contribution-weighted predictions of heterogeneous regressors to construct shared pseudo-labels. This design makes each regressor's influence explicit in the learning targets generated for unlabeled seismic samples under sparse well control. The Tri-Game Shapley mechanism combines a rank-MSE performance game with a pairwise consistency game to estimate nonnegative regressor weights from labeled training data. These weights remain fixed during collaborative training and are reused for final prediction fusion. Candidate pseudo-labels are screened using a common local k-nearest-neighbor error-reduction criterion before retraining. We evaluate CoGameReg on 10 public regression datasets, a synthetic three-dimensional P-wave velocity prediction task, and a field water-saturation application. The benchmark advantage is most pronounced at the 2.5% labeled-data ratio and decreases as supervision increases. CoGameReg obtains the best blind-well metrics in the synthetic experiment. In the field application, predictions clipped to 0-100% yield a pooled coefficient of determination of 0.5942, a root mean square error of 5.7441 percentage points, and a Pearson correlation of 0.8265 across three blind wells. CoGameReg has the highest Pearson correlation among the four field methods. The results support the use of CoGameReg to integrate sparse well labels with dense seismic attributes, with performance varying across metrics and well locations.

papers.title: Personalized Federated Direct Preference Optimization via LoRA Adapters
papers.abstract: Federated Direct Preference Optimization (FedDPO) enables privacy-preserving alignment of language models across distributed agents without centralizing sensitive preference data. However, existing FedDPO analysis assumes all clients converge to a single shared policy, which is fundamentally at odds with the heterogeneous preference distributions present in practice. We propose Personalized FedDPO (pFedDPO), in which each client maintains a small private LoRA adapter atop a shared global base model. In pFedDPO, the base model is synchronized via FedAvg each round, while LoRA adapters remain local and capture client-specific preference patterns. We prove that this decomposition replaces the gradient diversity $κ^2$ in the FedDPO bound with a residual heterogeneity $κ^2_{\mathrm{eff}}$, which is no larger than $κ^2$ when adapters absorb client-specific directions, at the cost of an additive adapter-bias term that vanishes as adapters converge. Experiments on preference datasets show that pFedDPO consistently attains a lower gradient norm than vanilla FedDPO while remaining competitive in training loss and per-client reward accuracy.

papers.title: LeapBot-JAC: Joint Action Chains for World Action Models
papers.abstract: Action-chunking policies predict future controls but execute only a prefix before replanning. How should a fixed action-token budget be organized to support execution? We propose LeapBot-JAC, which allocates sparse future-control references and dense execution targets within one shared action expert. Both chains are supervised by demonstrated controls and jointly denoised at aligned physical-time positions. Directed attention allows execution tokens to read reference tokens subject to the host's visibility constraints. JAC adds neither action tokens nor parameters and retains the host's world-modeling process; both chains participate in inference, while only the execution chain drives the robot. On LIBERO, JAC reaches 98.3% success with FastWAM and LeapBot-WA, up from 97.0% and 97.3%. On zero-shot LIBERO-Plus, their success rates improve from 53.5% to 70.4% and from 73.1% to 77.3%, respectively. RoboTwin and two real-world tasks provide additional deployment evaluations. Single-training-seed comparisons and FastWAM ablations support action-role organization as a practical design choice under a fixed action-token budget.

papers.title: Win-Win Fusion: Multi-Modal Image Fusion with Visual-Semantic Collaboration
papers.abstract: Existing multi-modal image fusion (MMIF) methods generally face an optimization gap between the visual and semantic domains, limiting the enhancement of perception capabilities. To overcome this long-standing barrier, this work proposes W2F, a new visual-semantic mutual reinforcing paradigm for MMIF. First, we reinforce the foundation for visual-semantic collaboration by amplifying feature complementarity through two targeted designs. Specifically, the segmentation-guided fusion loss introduces object-aware structural guidance into visual fusion, while the embedded information restoration prior strengthens the ability of visual fusion to provide reliable perceptual evidence for the semantic branch under degraded conditions. Then, we introduce a strong multi-modal information interaction mechanism composed of interactive gated mixed attention (IGM-Att) and progressive coupling attention (PC-Att). These modules ensure comprehensive scene representation from both local and global perspectives, providing informational support for visual-semantic collaboration. Finally, we construct a collaborative mechanism to couple visual fusion and semantic fusion. It employs a feature search module to extract complementary key features from both tasks, enriching the representational potential of visual and semantic information. Meanwhile, a gradient correction strategy ensures collaboration from the optimization perspective, enhancing performance for both visual and semantic fusion through consistency learning. Extensive experiments demonstrate that W2F surpasses state-of-the-art methods in both visual appeal and decision accuracy. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/HaoZhang1018/W2F.

papers.title: Numerical Smoothness and Error Analysis for Evolution Equations
papers.abstract: This is a lecture note to introduce the innovative concept of numerical smoothness and its application in the error analysis of numerical solutions of evolution equations. We start from the two fundamentally different error splittings. One splitting is popular, which brings us to local error defined along the original solution and error propagation by numerical schemes. The well know Lax Equivalence Theorem is based on this error splitting. The other splitting can only be seen in a few numerical ODE books, which brings us to local error defined along the numerical solution and error propagation by the solutions of the evolution equations. The innovative concept of numerical smoothness arises from the second error splitting. While there are many difficulties when we use numerical stability in error analysis of nonlinear evolution equations, we will show that numerical smoothness works naturally in error analysis/estimation/control with advantages in several ways. We will define temporal and spatial numerical smoothness indicators, prove the necessity of the boundedness of these indicators for having optimal convergence rate, and show computable error estimates as functions of these smoothness indicators. Moreover, these error estimates are optimal in the approximatons' convergence rates and also optimal in the error propagation of the evolution equation. In comparison with error analysis framework of the Lax Equivalence Theorem, from the necessity results and the error estimates proven in the numerical smoothness framework, we have a new equivalence theory: Consistency + Numerical Smoothness <=> optimal error estimates. Unlike the Lax Equivalence Theorem, the new equivalence theory works well for nonlinear problems, nonlinear schemes, and many other complications of problems.

papers.title: Direct detection constraints on EFT operators for inelastic dark matter
papers.abstract: We convert existing exclusion limits on the elastic spin-independent (SI) dark matter--proton cross sections into upper bounds on the event rate, subsequently applying them to constrain other effective operators for inelastic scattering of light dark matter in the GeV mass region. We focus on three representative scenarios including the isoscalar, proton-philic, and the proton-philic spin-dependent inelastic dark matter model, which are well-motivated in phenomenological studies of dark matter detection.

papers.title: Evaluation of Software Quality Through Refactoring Commit-Impact Analysis
papers.abstract: The aim of this study is to conduct an empirical analysis of the correlation between code modifications and software quality. This will be achieved by examining the effects of changes made before and after each refactoring commit, using software metrics such as size, complexity, code smells, vulnerability, and bug detection. The objective is to conduct static code analysis on open-source software from GitHub repositories using various repository mining and static code analysis tools. Our approach involves formulating research-based questions and utilizing the specified tools to obtain results that will enable us to resolve the case study. The obtained results have been summarised and further analyzed using tables and graphs to achieve the objective.

papers.title: The AI Side of the Human-AI Companion Relationship: Contributions to Users' Mental Models
papers.abstract: For many users, the relationship they have with an AI companion (AIC) feels genuinely mutual. The AIC appears to be attentive, empathic, and responsive, and the exchange can feel like two parties reacting to each other in real time. As a result, the user's mental model of relational adaptation correctly represents the AIC's responsiveness and change, but the mechanisms producing this may not be what the user thinks they are. In this paper, we illustrate how an AIC's apparent mutual engagement is generated without a persisting relational subject on the other side and without a self that persists between prompts. Despite this, we show that both the human and the AIC are changed by the interaction, but these changes occur at different levels. The change in the person is constitutive (i.e., intrinsic), but the change in the AIC is configurative (i.e., external and editable), and it is this difference in level that explains how the AIC contributes to a sense of mutuality. Importantly, we highlight how the mental models users develop regarding AIC mutuality may misrepresent its mechanisms and ontological significance. Specifically, we discuss how the ways in which AICs respond to a user contribute to the user's inaccurate inference that the AIC's adaptation is constitutive rather than configurative and how this can lead users to assign unwarranted interpersonal significance to the mutuality of the relationship. The paper specifies the implications this has for users, researchers, and AIC designers.

papers.title: Room-temperature ferroelectric p-wave magnet
papers.abstract: P -wave magnets exhibit odd-parity spin polarization in momentum space while retaining zero net magnetization, offering a promising route toward nonrelativistic spintronics. Previously reported p-wave magnets based on combined time-reversal and lattice-translation symmetry, Tt, have thus far exhibited ordering temperatures below the liquid-nitrogen range. Here, we demonstrate a distinct route to a pristine p-wave magnetism that does not require T t symmetry, and instead is based on incommensurate spin-spiral order. Specifically, the cycloidal magnetic structure of the multiferroic BiFeO3 (BFO) intrinsically realizes p-wave magnetism coexisting with ferroelectric polarization at room temperature. Combining symmetry analysis, density-functional-theory calculations, and circular photogalvanic-effect (CPGE) measurements, we find a large nonrelativistic spin splitting of approximately 100 meV associated with the cycloidal order. The resulting p-wave spin polarization gives rise to a characteristic CPGE response whose sign can be reversibly switched by electrically controlling the cycloid chirality. Our results establish ferroelectric BiFeO3 as a room-temperature platform for electrically switchable p-wave magnetism and provide a route toward voltage-controlled spintronic devices based on parity-breaking magnetic order.

papers.title: Vulnerable Models in the AI Supply Chain: An Empirical Study of Adoption, Propagation, and Usage Patterns
papers.abstract: The rapid integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) models has established a complex supply chain, but many of these shared artifacts harbor severe vulnerabilities such as insecure serialization and architectural backdoors. While prior efforts have extensively scanned model registries to flag malicious artifacts, a critical gap remains in understanding how developers actually adopt and integrate these unsafe models into downstream software systems. We bridge this gap by conducting a large-scale empirical study on the usage and propagation of 16,977 known vulnerable models on HuggingFace flagged by InsightDB. We track their prevalence across GitHub repositories, software packages, fine-tuning chains, and deployed applications. Our analysis reveals that, despite being publicly flagged, these vulnerable models appear in over 21,000 code locations across more than 5,000 open-source repositories, with 3,757 distinct flagged models (22.1\%) actively referenced in at least one project. To understand how these models are integrated in code and identify recurring usage patterns, we categorize and analyze the recurring patterns surrounding them via a customized pipeline that combines Code Property Graphs extraction with a tailored Frequent Subgraph Mining approach. Across all patterns, we find no evidence of provenance verification or model sanitization logic, with developers frequently bypassing security parameters or delegating trust to permissive framework defaults. These findings underscore that scanning model files alone is insufficient, highlighting the urgent need for context-aware security analysis and stricter integration guardrails at the application layer of the AI supply chain.

papers.title: The Scientific Research Taste Benchmark (SciTaste-Bench): A Multi-Disciplinary Benchmark for Assessing Large Language Models' Judgment of Research Taste in Scientific Papers
papers.abstract: Whether large language models can assess the innovativeness of academic publications matters for literature reviews, research funding screening, and academic recommendations. We introduce the Scientific Research Taste Benchmark (SciTaste), a gold-standard benchmark covering six disciplines: physics, mathematics, chemistry, biology, medicine, and finance. SciTaste measures research taste, that is, the ability to judge a paper's scientific value and potential, of which innovativeness is one of seven dimensions. It integrates metadata from NASA ADS, OpenAlex, and arXiv, aligns papers to field-specific classification systems, and scores each paper with the seven-dimensional Academic Taste Index. Dimension weights come from a bi-objective machine-learning approach (five regressors, including random forests) and are shared across all six disciplines. The benchmark includes 300 selected papers (50 per discipline) and a backup pool of 5,700 papers (950 per field) covering 1996-2023. SciTaste supports four evaluation modes: pure_qa, native_search, our structured tool-calling agent DiM (9 bibliometric tools in ADS/OpenAlex), and dimagent_v3_native. Outputs are evaluated by two complementary schemes: correlation with dimension-level accuracy, and WAPE relative error. Across ten state-of-the-art LLMs, tool-based structured evaluation generally outperformed toolless and raw web search modes, though gains were model-dependent. Physics is easiest; chemistry, biology, and medicine remain more challenging. SciTaste supplies the value-judgment substrate auto-research systems need to screen, rank, and prioritize candidate ideas. Dataset, harness, and scoring code are available on Hugging Face at https://huggingface.co/datasets/skylenage/SciTaste-benchmark.

papers.title: Generalized Determinantal Point Processes for Attraction and Repulsion with Distinct Interaction Kernels
papers.abstract: Determinantal point processes (DPPs) model subset selection probability with repulsion, but many applications also exhibit attraction arising from pairwise relations or shared latent structures. Nonsymmetric DPPs (NDPPs) capture both effects, but their kernels are difficult to interpret and specify. We propose the determinant-ratio point process (DRPP), which models repulsion and attraction via a ratio of the determinants of two symmetric positive-definite kernels. This formulation preserves the feature-based interpretation of standard DPPs while allowing the two effects to be specified separately. Furthermore, we introduce an auxiliary-variable representation that enables efficient MCMC sampling and yields tractable expectation formulas for key statistics including the normalizing constant, which together facilitate maximum-likelihood learning. We theoretically characterize the interaction structures well suited to DRPPs: for clustered attraction with $C$ latent groups, DRPPs exactly realize the target pairwise interactions with an attraction rank $C$, whereas NDPPs can require a rank that grows with the number of items given the same repulsion component. Conversely, nontransitive pair-specific attraction may require compensation through the DRPP repulsion kernel. Experiments support these predictions, showing that DRPPs fit transitive attraction with substantially fewer parameters than NDPPs.

papers.title: MeshBind: Point-to-Mesh Binding for Non-Rigid Scene Flow Automatic Annotation
papers.abstract: Scene flow estimation is essential for many autonomous driving (AD) and robotic applications, but obtaining ground-truth scene flow for non-rigid objects such as pedestrians is highly difficult. We present MeshBind, an automatic annotation method that uses mesh models to generate per-point scene flow for non-rigid objects. The novelty of this work is threefold: 1) developing a multi-view module that reconstructs an articulated mesh model from six surround cameras and registers it to the LiDAR frame; 2) developing a local-frame binding technique that attaches each point to the mesh via a per-triangle tangent-normal frame, invariant under rigid motion yet adaptive to articulated deformation; 3) developing a three-layer flow registration pipeline that combines ego-vehicle motion compensation, box binding, and mesh binding to produce full-scene per-point flow. We implement MeshBind in SF-Studio, an interactive annotation tool that visualises flow and allows human mesh corrections with automatic recomputation. We also release SFB (SUScape-Flow Benchmark), a large-scale benchmark built on the public SUScape dataset, covering 41k frames with per-point non-rigid pedestrian annotations and a Rigid/Semi-Rigid/Non-Rigid evaluation protocol. Experiments show that fine-tuning on SFB reduces three-way endpoint error (EPE) by 2-3x, and brings non-rigid EPE to the same level as rigid EPE.

papers.title: All-electron RT-TDDFT with Exact Exchange based on Numeric Atom-centered Orbitals for Condensed Matter
papers.abstract: Real-time time-dependent density functional theory (RT-TDDFT) has become a widely used first-principles method for studying excited-state and nonequilibrium electron dynamics. Hybrid exchange-correlation (XC) functionals, which incorporate a fraction of nonlocal exact exchange, are particularly important for accurately describing processes such as charge transfer and hot-carrier dynamics. However, the high computational cost which accompanies exact exchange, as required in hybrid XC functionals, has largely restricted RT-TDDFT simulations of condensed matter systems to using semi-local XC functionals. In this work, we present an all-electron implementation of exact exchange for RT-TDDFT based on numeric atom-centered orbitals, extending an efficient ground-state resolution-of-identity (RI) framework to the complex, time-dependent Hamiltonians required for real-time propagation. We validate the implementation against an established RI approach, for an isolated water molecule, finding exact agreement for both valence and core (K-edge) excitations. We also demonstrate the method on two extended periodic systems, crystalline silicon and silicon carbide. For silicon, the HSE06 spectrum reproduces previously reported real-time TDDFT results and agrees with experiment to within approximately 0.2~eV, consistent with plane-wave pseudopotential implementations. For silicon carbide, we compute valence and X-ray absorption spectra at the silicon $L$-edge and carbon $K$-edge. These results establish an efficient, all-electron route to hybrid-XC functional RT-TDDFT for both molecular and condensed matter systems.

papers.title: AD-SRF: Attack-Defense Semantic Reinforcement for Multi-Modal Image Fusion
papers.abstract: Existing image fusion methods struggle to balance visual quality and semantic attributes due to the inherent conflict between their optimization objectives. To address this challenge, we propose an attack-defense semantic reinforcement framework for multi-modal image fusion, termed AD-SRF. By decoupling the optimization of these two aspects and then losslessly reintegrating them, this framework injects rich semantic attributes into the fused image without compromising its visual quality. First, we develop a transformer-based restorative visual fusion network as a strong visual baseline. Equipped with the cross-modal retrieval module and the information restoration-fusion collaborative loss, it produces highly visible fused images even under degraded conditions. Second, we introduce an attack-defense game mechanism to strengthen the semantic attributes of the fused images. The attacker learns perturbation patterns that impair downstream segmentation, whereas the defender restores missing semantics from the original inputs and reintegrates them into the fused image through an imperceptible semantic map. Through iterative adversarial interaction, this mechanism drives the defender to continually strengthen the fused image's semantic attributes, boosting downstream segmentation performance without compromising visual quality. Extensive experiments demonstrate that AD-SRF achieves a win-win performance in both visual quality and semantic attributes. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/HaoZhang1018/AD-SRF.

papers.title: DS-Net: A Dynamic Split Network for Edge-Cloud Collaborative Inference
papers.abstract: Collaborative inference serves as a critical methodology in edge intelligence. Existing collaborative inference methods operate by splitting the deep neural network (DNN) model between edge devices and cloud servers. However, these methods need to load different models for multiple split points when the communication or device changes, thus resulting in long switching times and substantial storage overhead on the edge side. To address this issue, we propose a Dynamic Split Network (DS-Net), which not only enables efficient split point switching but also enhances the collaborative speed and accuracy across various scenarios. Specifically, we design a dynamic switching framework that enables flexible selection among multiple split points within a single model, thereby reducing storage, memory, and switching overhead. To mitigate the feature distribution shifts and task-relevant information loss caused by dynamic splitting and high-ratio compression, we further propose a hierarchical compensation mechanism. Local alignment calibrates the decoded feature distribution at each split point, while task-specific global compensation restores task-relevant information at the global level. In addition, we incorporate sample-adaptive global compensation selection into split-point selection based on sample complexity and runtime resource conditions. Experimental results demonstrate that DS-Net reduces memory overhead by 74.6% and achieves millisecond-level switching latency. Moreover, under a 10 Mbps bandwidth constraint on the Nano platform, DS-Net outperforms state-of-the-art collaborative methods by achieving 1.2% higher accuracy on the COCO dataset, reducing latency by 42.5%, and improving throughput by a factor of 1.8$\times$.

papers.title: Rethinking the Roles of Diffusion and Decoding: Predictive-State Flows for Parallel Language Generation
papers.abstract: In continuous diffusion language models (DLMs), latents generated by the diffusion prior are mapped almost deterministically to tokens, either by a decoder or through a token embedding matrix. Unlike in image generation, where visual details can vary continuously, the diffusion prior must capture fine-grained discrete token choices in continuous space, which can make the joint latent distribution difficult to model. We argue that generative roles should instead be divided: the diffusion prior should generate high-level predictive information, while the decoder should resolve the remaining token-level choices. Based on this view, we introduce Predictive-State Flows (PSF), which partitions a sequence into blocks and associates each block with a predictive state computed solely from the preceding context. A rectified-flow prior generates the sequence of predictive states, after which a block-causal decoder generates all blocks in parallel, autoregressively only within each block. This design reduces diffusion from L token-level states to K << L predictive states and reduces token-level sequential depth to L/K. On unconditional OpenWebText generation, a 197M-parameter model with K=8 achieves a generative perplexity of 22.8 at entropy 5.16 using 0.31 TFLOPs per 1024-token document, versus 24.0 and 7.2 TFLOPs for ELF-B with 32 sampling steps. The corresponding measured operating points yield MAUVE@512 of 0.93 and 0.73, respectively. Controlled comparisons further show that content states, which additionally encode their own blocks, yield 8-16% higher generative perplexity than predictive states, and that replacing sampled predictive-state trajectories with a shared mean lowers MAUVE@512 by 0.11. These results suggest that latent design for continuous DLMs should consider not only how compactly text is represented, but also how generative roles are divided between the prior and the decoder.

papers.title: A Lightweight Velocity Correction Framework for Improving Instruction Following in Few-Step Text-to-Image Generation
papers.abstract: Few-step text-to-image generators produce high-quality images with few network forward passes, yet struggle with complex prompts involving multiple subjects, interactions, spatial relations, counting, and attribute binding. Can these errors be reduced without changing the generator's parameters or increasing its forward-pass count? We propose a lightweight correction framework for a frozen 6B-parameter generator. The generator predicts velocities that determine how its intermediate image representation is updated; a corrector with fewer than 20M parameters learns residual adjustments at selected sampling steps. Because earlier corrections change the states encountered at later steps, our On-Trajectory Flow-Bridge Supervision derives residual targets at the states actually reached during corrected generation. A single corrector is shared across selected steps and runs in parallel with the generator. Only the corrector is trained, requiring neither reward optimization nor re-distillation. To our knowledge, this is the first framework for lightweight velocity-residual adaptation of fully frozen few-step text-to-image generators that preserves their original sampling schedule and forward-pass count. On our target complex-scene distribution, the framework achieves a +17.60-percentage-point NetWin over frozen Z-Image-Turbo in pairwise instruction-following evaluation, with only 26.9 ms (0.84%) additional end-to-end latency per image and no increase in backbone evaluations.

papers.title: Alter-excitons in Altermagnets: Symmetry, Splitting and Dispersion
papers.abstract: Magnetism provides a fertile platform for discovering emergent quantum phenomena governed by symmetry. Recent developments of spin-space-group (SSG) theory have revealed altermagnets as a distinct class of nonrelativistic collinear magnets with unconventional spin-dependent electronic structures. Here, we demonstrate that altermagnetic symmetry imposes fundamentally different constraints on electronic and excitonic excitations. Although the quasiparticle and two-body Hamiltonians possess identical SSG symmetries, we find that symmetry-protected degeneracies present in the electronic band structure can be intrinsically lifted in the exciton spectrum at specific momenta. This splitting arises solely from the many-body nature of excitons and does not require spin-orbit coupling or noncollinear magnetic order. Combining symmetry analysis with many-body perturbation theory, we predict a novel class of spin-split excitonic quasiparticles, termed alter-excitons, and reveal their characteristic dispersions in altermagnetic systems. Our results establish excitons as a sensitive probe of hidden spin-space symmetries and uncover a new route toward symmetry-engineered many-body phenomena in collinear magnets.

papers.title: JMT-YOLO: Multi-task Domain Adaptation via Segmentation-Guided Consistency Learning
papers.abstract: Domain adaptive object detection (DAOD) aims to reduce performance degradation due to distribution shifts between training (source) and testing (target) datasets. However, owing to insufficient modeling of fine-grained features and limited instance-level alignment, existing approaches become less effective under complex environmental conditions, such as extreme weather conditions and object occlusion. We overcome these challenges by proposing JMT-YOLO, a novel joint multi-task learning framework for DAOD. JMT-YOLO is based on the Mean Teacher architecture. It introduces an auxiliary semantic segmentation task and a masking mechanism to enhance the modeling of foreground-background semantic boundaries in the target domain. Specifically, fine-grained feature degradation is reduced by introducing a multiscale context-aware segmentation head equipped with a dense connection structure to effectively capture local and global contextual features. A mask-consistency loss is formulated by applying random masking operations to target images, thereby guiding the network to learn structural context and improving instance-level feature alignment. Extensive experiments on three benchmark domain adaptation tasks (Pascal VOC to Clipart1k, Cityscapes to Foggy Cityscapes, and KITTI to Cityscapes) demonstrate that JMT-YOLO achieves detection performances of 46.9%, 57.3%, and 61.0%, respectively. These results demonstrate superior performance over existing state-of-the-art and baseline methods, thereby validating the effectiveness and generalization of JMT-YOLO.

papers.title: Fast-DeePC: Fast Data-Enabled Predictive Control using Soft-constrained Scheme
papers.abstract: Data-enabled predictive control (DeePC) replaces the explicit system model of model predictive control with a data-driven predictor built directly from recorded input-output trajectories, but the original hard-equality formulation keeps its coordinate vector as an online decision variable whose size grows with the offline data length, so the online problem grows more expensive as more data is used to enrich the behavioral representation. This article proposes Fast-DeePC, a framework which relaxes this consistency relation into the control objective with a quadratic ridge on the coordinate vector in place of the customary sparsity-promoting penalty, admitting a closed-form, offline elimination of the coordinate vector and reducing the online problem to a fixed-size box-constrained quadratic program solved by a structure-exploiting interior-point method. On identical soft quadratically regularized problems, the result matches a general-purpose solver's solution and is up to two orders of magnitude faster.

papers.title: When is Hotelling's $T^2$ asymptotically $F$-distributed?
papers.abstract: For Gaussian observations, a deterministic multiple of Hotelling's $T^2$ statistic has an exact $F$ distribution. This paper investigates when this approximation remains valid for an independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) data matrix $\mathbf{X}\in \mathbb{R}^{p\times n}$ with a fixed, possibly heavy-tailed entry law $ξ$. Under symmetry and $\limsup_{n\rightarrow \infty} p/n<1$, we prove that approximation by the $F$ distribution in Kolmogorov distance is equivalent to belonging to the domain of attraction of the normal law. Both conditions are equivalent to relative concentration of the diagonal entries of the null-space projection $\mathbf{P}=\mathbf{I}_n-\mathbf{X}^{\top}(\mathbf{X}\mathbf{X}^{\top})^{-1}\mathbf{X}$. The central quantity $R=\mathbf{1}^{\top}\mathbf{P}\mathbf{1}$ measures the geometric alignment between the averaging direction and the random row space of $\mathbf{X}$. For symmetric finite-variance entries, the sufficient approximation extends to every sequence $1\le p<n$, including fixed nullity $n-p$. As a consequence of the $F$ approximation, Hotelling's $T^2$ statistic exhibits different asymptotic distributions in different regimes, including the normal, chi-square, and inverse-chi-square limits depending on $p$ and $n$. Without symmetry, we establish a central limit theorem under the weak-$5/2$ tail condition $\lim_{x\to\infty}x^{5/2}\mathbb{P}(|ξ|>x)=0$ when $p/n\rightarrow γ\in (0,1)$, and obtain the $F$ approximation as a consequence. Centered standardized Pareto laws show that the exponent $5/2$ is sharp for this universal absolute-tail sufficient condition, although balanced-tail nonsymmetric laws can retain the approximation at the boundary, which reveals that the asymmetry of the tails matters for the $F$ approximation.

papers.title: Compaction-Aware Reinforcement Learning For Ascend Triton Kernel Generation
papers.abstract: Automatically generating high-performance kernels with LLM-based agents promises substantial gains in development efficiency, but two obstacles remain. First, while increasing multi-turn interaction with execution environments is crucial for refining generation quality, continuous context accumulation rapidly exceeds the model's effective context window. Second, training long-horizon tasks via GRPO inherently incurs sparse rewards due to its reliance on terminal outcome evaluation, severely hindering step-level credit assignment; To address these obstacles, we propose ATRL (Ascend Triton Reinforcement Learning), a post-training method that refines GRPO into a compaction-aware, segment-level objective for long-horizon kernel generation. We also design a lightweight agent harness providing cascaded compilation, correctness, and profiling feedback, alongside an Ascend-specific knowledge base injected during agentic RL training and evaluation to compensate for the base model's missing platform expertise. Evaluations on NPUKernelBench and KernelBench, both executed on Ascend hardware, show that ATRL consistently surpasses all baselines, including GRPO, in both correctness and speedup.

papers.title: GIST: Generator-state-Informed Supervision for Tabular Foundation Models
papers.abstract: Tabular foundation models (TFMs) based on prior-data fitted networks typically use sampled hard query labels, leaving avoidable sampling variability in pretraining. A key observation is that intermediate generator states can reveal label uncertainty beyond a sampled outcome. We propose Generator-state-Informed Supervision for TFMs (GIST), which uses these states to average query losses over conditional label distributions. GIST jointly designs task generation and query supervision, using entropy-calibrated encodings to obtain tractable, input-consistent targets on supported label-dependent branches. We show that this averaging preserves the population objective and yields no larger gradient covariance at fixed parameters within each generating distribution. Under matched pretraining schedules, GIST improves mean rank across three architectures on both TabArena and TALENT without changing architecture or inference. Across these benchmarks and architectures, GIST wins 62.1% of paired dataset-level comparisons against the corresponding hard-label controls.

papers.title: Codegree-Constrained Turán Problems for $F_5$ and Its Blow-ups
papers.abstract: Let $F_5$ denote the $3$-uniform hypergraph with edge set $\{abc,abd,cde\}$. For a hypergraph property $\mathcal P$, let $ex_{\mathcal P}(n,F_5)$ be the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex $F_5$-free $3$-uniform hypergraph satisfying $\mathcal P$. Let $Δ_2(H)$ denote the maximum codegree of a pair of vertices in a $3$-uniform hypergraph $H$. We determine the exact value of $ex_{Δ_2\ge m}(n,F_5)$ when $m$ is bounded away from $n/3$ by a fixed positive proportion. More precisely, for every constant $c\in (1/3,1)$, there exists $n_0$ such that for all $n\ge n_0$ and $m=cn$, \[ ex_{Δ_2\ge m}(n,F_5) = m\left\lceil\frac{n-m}{2}\right\rceil \left\lfloor\frac{n-m}{2}\right\rfloor. \] The unique extremal hypergraph is the complete tripartite $3$-graph $K^3_{m,\lceil (n-m)/2\rceil,\lfloor (n-m)/2\rfloor}$. We also prove the corresponding exact result for the blow-ups $F_5^t$, together with stability theorems showing that every near-extremal configuration is close to the relevant tripartite construction.

papers.title: Robust Halo Orbit Stationkeeping Under Missed Thrust Events and Maneuver Execution Errors
papers.abstract: Spacecraft stationkeeping is subject to various operational uncertainties such as missed thrust events, maneuver execution errors, and dynamics modeling errors. Missed thrust events are the most disruptive of these, and current practices mitigate that risk through Monte Carlo-driven heuristics and conservative margins that offer no formal safety guarantees and do not scale to multiple missed thrust events. This paper models these unplanned thruster outages through the Markov Jump System framework, and represents maneuver execution errors and dynamics linearization errors as bounded multiplicative noise. The resulting closed-loop system is a linear time-varying periodic Markov jump system with multiplicative noise, for which Lyapunov-like mean square stability and periodic set invariance conditions are derived. A linear matrix inequality-based optimal controller synthesis framework then designs a periodic, mode-dependent mean-square stable feedback policy that respects path constraints with probability one. The framework is demonstrated on the Earth-Moon 9:2 near-rectilinear halo orbit (NRHO), under both impulsive and low-thrust propulsion, and on a Saturn-Enceladus $L_1$ NRHO using impulsive propulsion. Nonlinear Monte Carlo simulations show that the spacecraft recovers from an arbitrary number of missed thrust events while respecting path constraints, and that the multiplicative noise model introduces additional robustness to maneuver execution error and linearization error.

papers.title: LatLM: Line-Parallel Language Models with Deferred Commitment
papers.abstract: Line-parallel language models advance multiple lines concurrently for substantial speedups. However, frameworks like the Line-Coupled Language Model (LCLM) enforce a fixed commitment schedule across lines. Because dependencies vary within text, a fixed schedule cannot hold back a line whose prerequisites remain uncomputed, forcing premature commitments and cascading reasoning errors. To address this limitation, we introduce the Lattice Language Model (LatLM), making commitment schedules an adaptive decoding-time choice. Text occupies a 2D lattice where eligible frontier tokens are scored each round; a policy commits confident candidates while deferring unready ones for extended context. One forward pass supervises entire sampled trajectories via 2D causal masking, while an append-only cache retains exact states. At 482M parameters, we establish two findings. (1) LatLM matches a data- and capacity-matched autoregressive model on held-out text when decoded sequentially, while its adaptive parallel decoder achieves near-autoregressive accuracy on independent-line tasks using 25--41% as many decoding rounds. (2) When cross-line dependencies cause LCLM's fixed schedule to fail, deferred commitment substantially improves accuracy while retaining parallelism where dependencies permit. On mixed dependency chains, LatLM achieves 96.5% accuracy versus LCLM's 78.5%, using fewer than half the decoding rounds of the autoregressive baseline.

papers.title: BLEND: Balancing Personalization vs. Generalization in Federated Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract: Federated vision-language models (FedVLMs) represent one of the emerging frontiers of machine learning, aiming to integrate federated learning within the fine-tuning pipelines of vision-language models (VLMs). In this work, we introduce BLEND, a new framework designed to jointly enhance the personalization and generalization capabilities of FedVLMs. BLEND proposes a selective VLM parameter fine-tuning and aggregation strategy that consists of (i) global vision and text adapters shared across clients, and (ii) a personalized vision projection adapter tailored to each client. BLEND further introduces a novel loss function that blends the outputs of the global and personalized adapters to achieve personalization, while simultaneously promoting generalization through a principled anchor design implemented via the projection heads of the zero-shot VLM. Extensive experiments demonstrate that BLEND consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, highlighting its ability to effectively balance personalization and generalization across diverse system settings. (Code is available at: https://github.com/payamsiabd/BLEND.git)

papers.title: Classification of bipartite observables II: NIP observables and the Todorcevic trichotomy
papers.abstract: This is the second paper in a series that reads the dividing lines of Shelah's classification theory as properties of bipartite quantum observables. For an observable of two independently prepared systems, Alice's and Bob's, we study its idealized responses: the expectation values of Alice's limiting preparations, as functions of Bob's preparations, which serve as probes, with Bob's system idealized first. We show that the observable is NIP, that is, no sequence of Alice's preparations lets Bob's probes realize every finite pattern of high and low values at a fixed positive gap, exactly when all idealized responses are of the first Baire class, pointwise limits of sequences of continuous functions; they then form a separable Rosenthal compactum. Because Alice can mix preparations, this compactum is convex, and hereditary separability forces it to be metrizable, so that NIP observables occupy three of the four topological classes defined by metrizability and Todorčević's trichotomy. Comparisons of photon numbers, of positions and of events in spacetime realize these three classes, and trees of preparations realize the seven minimal families of the Argyros--Dodos--Kanellopoulos heptachotomy. For the ferromagnetic transverse-field Ising model at positive temperature, the finite-volume magnetizations with offset longitudinal fields form a stable family when the spontaneous magnetization vanishes, and a family whose closure is first countable but not hereditarily separable when it does not.

papers.title: SecFD-FL: Frequency-Decoupled Federated Learning with Secure Aggregation for Charging Load Forecasting in Internet of Electric Vehicles
papers.abstract: Accurate charging load forecasting is essential for the reliability and efficiency of the Internet of Electric Vehicles (IoEV), yet it is challenging on two fronts: charging demand is highly stochastic, and the data collected by distributed sensors is privacy-sensitive. Although federated learning (FL) preserves data privacy, collaborative training still remains vulnerable to an honest-but-curious server that can invert shared model updates to reconstruct private data. To address both data volatility and privacy concerns, we propose SecFD-FL, a frequency-decoupled federated learning framework for IoEV comprising: 1) a dual-stream gated recurrent unit (GRU) network that separately models short-term and long-term charging load volatility, and 2) a lightweight secure aggregation layer for privacy preservation. Specifically, the secure aggregation layer employs a zero-sum additive masking protocol that perturbs each client's upload with high-variance noise, preventing the server from reconstructing private data while preserving the exact aggregate. Extensive experiments have been conducted on both EV-level and charging station-level using real datasets. The experiment results show that SecFD-FL reduces global RMSE by up to 60% over centralized baselines, achieving Jain's fairness up to 0.991 across clients, and reduces DLG-attack reconstruction correlation by 8 times to 15 times relative to FedAvg -- all with no additional per-round communication cost beyond a one-time key exchange.

papers.title: Sampling-based Kinodynamic Planning with World Models
papers.abstract: Visual world models predict the consequences of actions from images, but planning with them is typically done by optimizers such as CEM and MPPI. However, these optimizers stall on long-horizon tasks where progress requires motion the objective does not reward, such as moving around a block before pushing it. This paper revisits kinodynamic sampling-based motion planning for world models, using the learned model as the propagator of a tree search in latent space. Our key insight is that the sampling strategies devised for high-dimensional search in configuration space apply directly to the latent space of a world model, where they rapidly expand through intermediate states that myopic optimizers never sample. We present two exploration strategies for the high-dimensional latent space, nearest-neighbor-guided RRT and projection-based KPIECE, with GPU-native batched expansion for efficient device utilization. We evaluate with an off-the-shelf DINO-WM on four simulated domains and a real-world block-pushing task. Our approaches match or exceed the success rate of CEM and MPPI at up to 13.8x lower planning time in simulation, and improve the success rate by 20% on the real robot.

papers.title: Coexponential Exploration in the Clef Programming Language
papers.abstract: Clef was created as a concurrent programming language whose compiler tracks state ownership, waiting computations and request dependencies. We develop a coexponential account of stateful services and their client pools within this design. Delimited continuations retain the computation and resources needed to complete each interaction. These structures give our compiler premises for verifying service composition and preserving it through native lowering to multiple hardware targets. We connect finite actor state transitions to the initial, service and final rules of a coexponential server. A separate operational account relates actor dispatch to single-use continuation frames. We prove state-ownership and reply preservation, give a finite communication-summary analysis, and derive circular-wait exclusion under stated assumptions. A further result identifies when changing service order preserves both state and replies. Our Program Semantic Graph retains these facts through compilation. We are researching reusable proofs to confirm the ownership and communication interfaces, while our BAREWire implementation connects message meaning to its unboxed representation across respective endpoints. A distributed worker example preserves request identity across suspension, reordered replies and boundary conversion. Urschel's growth bounds inform a solver service; a distributed ADM update additionally preserves joint samples, metric evidence and request identity. Our two-category account connects component refinement, reusable proof terms and native realization. Protocols determine the admissible interactions, continuations expose their storage requirements, and retained dependencies support differential compilation. Developers can express ordinary stateful services while the compiler carries the conditions for their correct composition across execution targets.

papers.title: Thermochemically Constrained Multiscale Laplace Neural Operator to Learn Stiff Chemical Kinetics with Conditional Diffusion Model Sampling
papers.abstract: Stiff chemical kinetics is a major computational bottleneck in reacting-flow simulations, while data-driven solvers remain sensitive to training-state coverage and chemical dynamics. This work combines conditional diffusion sampling with a thermochemically constrained multiscale Laplace neural operator (TC-MLNO) for chemistry ODE integration. The diffusion model learns the equivalence-ratio-conditioned joint distribution of temperature and species from low-dimensional flame data, augmenting the state space without independent perturbations. TC-MLNO represents transient, non-periodic responses through pole-residue Laplace layers and assigns fast, medium, and slow species to separate branches. Thermochemical constraints are imposed through losses for mass and elemental conservation and heat release rate. The framework is evaluated in 1D premixed flames, a 2D developing jet, and a 3D turbulent burner flame. With equal-sized datasets, diffusion sampling reduces the 95th-percentile distance to the base flame manifold by up to 37.5% and the a posteriori full-species macro-average error by up to 92.7% versus random sampling, especially for minor species and radicals. TC-LNO yields smaller errors than the DeepONet baseline for 84.9% of retained modes and reduces the 95th-percentile error for the most attenuated modes from 0.372 to 0.081. In multidimensional flames, TC-MLNO better preserves reaction-zone locations, heat-release structures, and chemically sensitive species than DeepONet. Errors of representative radical and nitrogen-containing species in the 3D flame decrease by 88.0%-88.9%. Compared with direct CVODE integration, TC-MLNO reduces mean chemistry and total solution times by 90.1% and 62.6%, respectively. These results show that distribution-aware sampling and Laplace neural operator learning provide an accurate and efficient alternative for stiff chemical ODE integration.

papers.title: Product and Quotient Set Dominance in Finite Groups
papers.abstract: A classic problem in additive number theory asks whether a given subset of integers has more sums or differences. This inquiry naturally extends to finite groups, where one compares the sizes of the product set $AA$ and the quotient set $AA^{-1}$ for a subset $A \subseteq G$. A finite group is considered product-dominant if it contains a higher proportion of subsets where $|AA| > |AA^{-1}|$, and quotient-dominant if the reverse is true. We establish statistical criteria to determine the dominance behavior of large finite groups by analyzing the moments of the random variable $d(A) := |AA| - |AA^{-1}|$. By translating product and quotient relationships into graph-theoretic constructions, we compute these moments through counting independent sets. Our main result demonstrates that for a growing sequence of finite groups $G_k$ with center size $Z_k$ and involution count $T_k$, the condition $Z_k = o(T_k)$ implies the groups are eventually product-dominant. Conversely, if $T_k \cdot \sqrt{3}^{R_k/Z_k} = o(Z_k)$ (where $R_k$ denotes the number of elements whose square is central), the groups are eventually quotient-dominant. Using these asymptotic conditions, we resolve the Miller--Vissuet conjecture by proving that all dihedral groups $D_n$ for $n \geq 3$ are product-dominant. Furthermore, we classify the dominance behavior of several major families of groups, proving that symmetric groups and non-abelian finite simple groups are product-dominant, while groups of odd order and certain abelian groups are quotient-dominant. Finally, for groups that fall outside our asymptotic conditions, we derive an explicit formula for the first moment utilizing the irreducible characters and conjugacy classes of the group.

papers.title: Sample-Preserving Search-to-Decision Reduction for Noisy Linear Equations over Large Moduli
papers.abstract: The Noisy Linear Equations problem involves finding the solution to a random linear system over a finite field given noisy evaluations. This is a generalisation of various learning problems widely used in cryptography, including Learning with Errors (LWE), Learning with Rounding (LWR), and Learning Parity with Noise (LPN). We present a new sample-preserving search-to-decision reduction for Noisy Linear Equations that has complexity $\mathrm{poly}(n,m,\log q, q/σ)$, where $n$ is the dimension of the secret, $m$ is the number of samples, $q$ is the modulus, and $σ$ is the magnitude of the noise (defined suitably for the kind of noise involved). In particular, this implies search-to-decision reductions for LWE and LWR that run in time $\mathrm{poly}(n)$ even if the modulus $q$ is exponentially large, as long as the noise-to-modulus ratio $σ/q$ is non-negligible. Our reduction works for prime moduli $q$. If $q$ is composite, it instead produces a list that contains a small multiple of the solution. Prior to this work, known search-to-decision reductions for LWE and LWR either did not preserve the parameters of the problem (i.e., $m$, $n$, $σ$, and $q$), or had complexity that scaled polynomially with either $σ$ or the largest prime factor of $q$.

papers.title: OGPO: Offline Goal-conditioned Policy Optimization for Recoverable Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models have shown strong promise in robotic manipulation, yet their post-training still predominantly relies on trajectory-level supervised imitation over robot demonstrations. While effective for learning feasible actions, this paradigm supervises policies to reproduce expert actions at each step, biasing them toward demonstration-specific action paths and providing limited guidance for recovering toward task-progress states once execution deviates from demonstrated trajectories. To address this limitation, we propose OGPO, an Offline Goal-conditioned Policy Optimization framework for recoverable VLA post-training. Instead of treating offline demonstrations merely as step-wise action labels, OGPO adaptively relabels trajectories with semantic key states and constructs goal-conditioned process rewards to optimize the policy for reaching these task-progress states. In this way, OGPO shifts VLA post-training from trajectory-level action imitation to key-state reachability learning, enabling policies to acquire a more robust ability to complete goal states from feasible off-demonstration states without requiring additional online interaction. Experiments on LIBERO and MetaWorld show that OGPO consistently improves VLA policy performance over standard supervised fine-tuning. Moreover, evaluations on LIBERO-Plus and our proposed LIBERO-ReAct, a mid-execution perturbation benchmark, further demonstrate that OGPO achieves stronger robustness and goal-directed recoverability under distribution shifts and recoverable off-demonstration states.

papers.title: Controlled-Minimax: Stabilizing Adversarial Optimization via Control Theory
papers.abstract: Minimax optimization is fundamental to adversarial learning yet suffers from severe stability challenges, often manifesting as persistent limit cycles or divergence. This paper investigates these instabilities through the lens of continuous-time dynamical systems. By modeling training dynamics as a second-order Ordinary Differential Equation (ODE), we rigorously identify the root cause of non-convergence: the problematic eigenstructure of the loss function's Hessian near equilibrium points. To address this, we introduce Controlled-Minimax, a novel stabilization framework that reformulates the optimization trajectory as a controllable physical system. Unlike heuristic regularization techniques, our approach derives a specific feedback controller that provides theoretical guarantees of local exponential stability, regardless of the underlying Hessian spectrum. Consequently, our method stabilizes general minimax problems where traditional gradient descent-ascent methods fail. Extensive experiments on pathological benchmarks including the Dirac-GAN, 2D Gaussian mixtures, and Swiss Roll datasets, as well as high-resolution image synthesis with StyleGAN2-ada, demonstrate that Controlled-Minimax effectively suppresses oscillatory behavior while ensuring fast and robust convergence.

papers.title: DeFiRank: Federated Pairwise Ranking for Governance in Decentralized Financial Networks
papers.abstract: Existing governance approaches in decentralized financial networks rely on manual review processes conducted by human committees, which introduces subjective bias, creates a scalability bottleneck under high network volume, and fails to capture complex behavioural patterns and evolving network dynamics. To address these limitations, we propose \name, a federated learning-based pairwise ranking framework in which multiple institutions collaboratively train a ranking model without sharing their private transaction data. This collaborative learning enables the model to capture network-wide behavioural patterns that signify strong network participation and directly contribute to the network effect, including diversity of counterparties, usage of multiple applications, and frequency of transactions. The proposed system ranks providers based on the authenticity of their actions, promoting genuine contributors and demoting those exhibiting suspicious behaviour. We evaluate \name\ on a real-world blockchain transaction dataset. Results demonstrate that the federated approach achieves ranking performance modestly below the centralized baseline (NDCG@15: $\approx$0.87 vs.\ $\approx$0.92) while preserving data privacy and matching its ranking stability (Kendall $τ$: $\approx$0.70 for both regimes), producing reliable governance decisions, including provider promotion and demotion (648 and 39 unique providers, respectively), without requiring centralized access to sensitive transaction data.

papers.title: AI-Mediation in Retail Markets: Revenue Effects and Assortment Optimization
papers.abstract: AI shopping assistants increasingly influence which products consumers consider. We study retail assortment planning under AI mediation, where a retailer chooses a catalog, an AI intermediary forms a customer-facing shortlist, and the customer chooses from that shortlist according to a multinomial logit model. We consider both deterministic mediation, in which the AI follows a fixed segment-specific ranking, and stochastic mediation based on the Plackett-Luce model. Empirically, we construct a dataset of product rankings from leading AI models, estimate Plackett-Luce ranking models, and evaluate their predictive performance on held-out assortments. Combining these estimates with synthetic customer preferences, we find that accounting for AI mediation can materially change optimal assortments and revenue. Across the tested capacity configurations, ignoring mediation yields mean revenue losses between 2.52% and 11.37% relative to the PL optimum. A much simpler deterministic plug-in, based only on the ordering of fitted AI utilities, performs substantially better, with mean losses of at most 0.53%. Motivated by this performance, we study assortment optimization under deterministic mediation. We characterize its computational complexity and show that, for any fixed number of customer segments, the problem admits a fully polynomial-time approximation scheme.

papers.title: A Comparison Theorem for $p$-adic GKZ Hypergeometric $\mathcal D$-Modules and Complexes
papers.abstract: We compare the $p$-adic GKZ hypergeometric complex with the hypergeometric arithmetic $\mathcal D$-module defined via six functors. Under the $p$-adic semi-nonresonance condition, the natural comparison morphism is a quasi-isomorphism. We prove concentration of the $p$-adic GKZ hypergeometric complex in degree $n$, establish overholonomicity under another non-Liouville hypothesis. When $(q-1)γ\in\mathbb Z^n$, we construct a Frobenius structure on its $n$-th cohomology and prove that its restriction to the nondegenerate locus is an overconvergent $F$-isocrystal of rank $n!\operatorname{vol}(Δ)$.

papers.title: Beyond Second-Order Information: Paid Logistic Regression with Noisy Features
papers.abstract: We consider online binary prediction with paid stochastic features, where the learner can spend resources to obtain better observations of the underlying features. This setting is motivated by applications such as medical testing, where additional cost can provide more precise measurements of patient's features for predicting a binary outcome. At each round, a latent feature is drawn i.i.d., the response is generated through a logistic model, and the learner chooses how much to pay before observing a noisy version of the feature. The goal of learner is to jointly control prediction loss and acquisition cost. In contrast to the former result on the online linear regression with paid features, covariance information alone is no longer sufficient: two noise distributions with the same covariance may induce different optimal logistic losses, and lower variance can even lead to higher loss. Under a structural ordering in which larger payments yield better observations by removing independent noise, we obtain $\widetilde O(\sqrt{T})$ regret when the noise structure is known and $\widetilde O(T^{2/3})$ regret when it is unknown, with matching lower bounds up to logarithmic factors.

papers.title: SCCGBench: Executability-Oriented Evaluation for Real-World Web Service-Call Code Generation
papers.abstract: LLM-generated service-call code is increasingly important for service computing, where developers rely on large language models (LLMs) to compose services and invoke third-party services. However, current approaches have not yet evaluated the invocation and execution of services in the actual code environment. To support execution-grounded evaluation, we present the Service-Call Code Generation Benchmark (SCCGBench), a benchmark of 3,135 traceable and decontamination-filtered RapidAPI call functions from real GitHub repositories. SCCGBench uses redacted-intent generation to reduce circular leakage and introduces Mock, Robust, ParamF1, and host-, endpoint-, method-, and parameter-level diagnostics. Mock denotes a virtual-execution hit that simultaneously matches the gold host, endpoint, and HTTP method, while Robust further requires status checking and exception handling. We evaluate six code LLMs and one non-neural retrieval baseline under intent-only, retrieval-augmented, and gold-documentation Oracle settings. Results show that models often generate syntactically correct or superficially similar HTTP-request code but achieve low Mock success in the intent-only setting; the strongest evaluated model obtains only 3.76% Mock. Under the gold-documentation Oracle settings (C3 and C5), Mock reaches 88.73%--90.52% for the open-source models evaluated in RQ2 and 76.47%--81.86% for DeepSeek-V4-Pro, whereas sparse and dense retrieval remain far below this oracle level. The findings indicate that service/API grounding is the main bottleneck: Mock is dominated by host, endpoint, and method alignment, while ParamF1 separately reveals parameter-alignment errors. SCCGBench provides an execution-grounded benchmark for Web service invocation, API recommendation, service-interface retrieval, endpoint grounding, and reliable service-call automation.
