Overall, this study suggests that robust accent classification evaluation should simultaneously include speaker-disjoint evaluation and cross-corpus testing.

papers.title: Deformation cones of 2-cubical combinatorial zonotopes
papers.abstract: We prove that the dimension of the deformation cone of any polytope combinatorially equivalent to a 2-cubical zonotope is bounded above by the number of generators of the zonotope. This bound is tight, and we show that it cannot be improved to an identity. We further extend our results to any 2-cubical polytope whose normal fan is combinatorially isomorphic to a pseudohyperplane arrangement, but we show that it cannot be extended to arbitrary 2-cubical polytopes.

papers.title: Learning by Compression: Risk Estimates Attain the Law-of-Large-Numbers Rate
papers.abstract: Compression schemes provide a general framework for deriving data-dependent risk bounds for learning algorithms. For learning rules based on preferent compression, existing results upper-bound the risk in terms of a sample-dependent complexity $\boldsymbol{k}$, defined as the cardinality of the compression augmented by the training examples on which the reconstructed hypothesis is inappropriate. These results, however, yield a margin of order $O(\sqrt{\ln N/N})$ above $\boldsymbol{k}/N$. In this paper, we establish that the logarithmic factor is not intrinsic. We prove that, for every fixed confidence level $1-δ$, the risk is bounded with probability at least $1-δ$ by $$ \frac{\boldsymbol{k}}{N} + O\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{N}}\right), $$ uniformly over all possible values of $\boldsymbol{k}$. Thus, risk estimates for learning algorithms based on preferent compression attain the same law-of-large-numbers rate as the empirical estimate of the probability of a fixed event. We also show that the leading term $\boldsymbol{k}/N$ is necessary and investigate its relation to the empirical risk. In particular, we identify regimes in which the empirical risk retains the $O(1/\sqrt{N})$ convergence rate, as well as regimes in which it converges more slowly or ceases to be consistent, while the complexity-based estimator preserves the $O(1/\sqrt{N})$ rate.

papers.title: Suppressing Multiple GNSS Interferers with Local-Gradient Adaptive Notch Filtering
papers.abstract: Adaptive notch filters (ANFs) based on the normalized least mean squares (NLMS) algorithm are an established technique for suppressing narrowband interference in GNSS receivers. The traditional solution for multiple interferers is simply cascading the NLMS-ANF into multiple stages but this solution degrades performance when multiple chirp jammers of similar power are present. We propose a low-complexity modification to the cascaded NLMS-ANF update rule to resolve this: a local gradient (LG) formulation: LG-ANF. The LG-ANF forms a locally bandlimited gradient signal by translating the input to baseband around the current frequency estimate, low-pass filtering it, and translating it back, thereby attenuating competing interferers before adaptation. The modification generalizes the traditional NLMS-ANF to handle the similar-power multiple interferer problem, using just one additional parameter. We characterize the gradient-averaging failure analytically and visually, demonstrate independent chirp tracking in the worst-case two-chirp scenarios, and evaluate statistical suppression performance by sweeping amplitude ratio against a standard NLMS-ANF, a frequency-locked-loop (FLL)-based ANF and a per-sample oracle upper bound. We further characterize the LG advantage over various ANF parameters and chirp conditions. Simulations show that the LG-ANF reduces to the standard NLMS-ANF outside the pathological multi-chirp regime, while recovering up to 4dB of in-band suppression around pathological amplitude ratios under per-condition optimization of the local bandwidth, and up to 13dB for selected edge-case parameter combinations. These optimized results represent an upper bound on the achievable LG gain. In a hardware experiment using a fixed alpha_lp=0.5, the LG-ANF extends position-lock survival by 24s relative to the standard ANF.

papers.title: Magnetic-field-induced detwinning of orientational domains in altermagnet $α$-MnTe: A single-crystal neutron diffraction study
papers.abstract: Altermagnets combine compensated magnetic order with momentum-dependent spin splitting, which makes them promising for future spintronic and magnonic applications, but their macroscopic responses can be strongly reduced by domain averaging. In hexagonal $α$-MnTe, three symmetry-related in-plane Néel-vector orientations and their time-reversal counterparts form six magnetic domain states, complicating both magnetic structure determination and measurements of the chiral magnon response. Using single-crystal neutron diffraction, we show that an in-plane field applied along the $[-1,1,0]$ direction produces a common magnetic domain orientation that saturates near $μ_0H=2$ T. A constrained refinement of 61 nuclear and magnetic reflections collected at 2 K and 2 T yields $\mathbf{M}\parallel[1,1,0]$, an ordered moment of $4.62(8)~μ_\mathrm{B}$ per Mn, and an orientational domain population at $r_A:r_B:r_C=0.97:0.03(5):0$ that is compatible with a nearly complete alignment of orientational domains. Furthermore, an abnormal behaviour in the temperature dependence of the selected reflections is observed in 60-88 K, its microscopic origin is discussed within the context of possible intrinsic piezomagnetic or magnetoelastic effects. Because unpolarized diffraction neither distinguishes domain repopulation from continuous Néel-vector rotation nor resolves time-reversal antiphase domains, the field-prepared state is a near-single-orientation state rather than a truly single-domain state. This non-contact domain control provides a practical complement to strain and field-cooling approaches for preparing well-defined magnetic states in bulk $α$-MnTe.

papers.title: HoldLight: Making Indoor Climbing More Accessible for Blind and Low-Vision Climbers through Layered Route Preview and Real-Time Next-Hold Guidance
papers.abstract: Indoor climbing creates access barriers for blind and low-vision (BLV) climbers because route understanding and in-climb next-hold localization are typically visually mediated and socially dependent. We present HoldLight, a workflow-centered accessibility system combining layered pre-climb route preview, concise real-time next-hold cueing, and explicit fallback under uncertainty. We grounded the design through formative inquiry with BLV climbers, refined the interaction via pilot testing, and conducted a controlled within-subjects evaluation comparing HoldLight with a controlled on-demand human-support condition derived from current support practices. Findings provide initial evidence that structured support can improve pre-climb route understanding, support recovery from next-hold uncertainty, and reduce immediate human re-entry for routine route-information clarification under controlled conditions. HoldLight contributes a bounded accessibility workflow, demonstrating where structured route-information is helpful, where explicit fallback is necessary, and how technical assistance can integrate with retained human safety oversight.

papers.title: Realized Tail-Risk Conditional Autoregressive Expectile Models: Accurate and Stable Forecasting Performance
papers.abstract: A realized tail-risk conditional autoregressive expectile (RTCARE) model is proposed for joint forecasting of value-at-risk (VaR) and expected shortfall (ES). Realized tail measures such as the realized quantile and the realized ES, constructed from intraday high-frequency returns, are incorporated into the dynamics and measurement equations of the conditional expectile, allowing information about lower-tail risk to enter the forecasts. The parameters are estimated by Markov chain Monte Carlo, and we evaluate the resulting VaR-ES forecasts in numerical examples and in an empirical application using U.S. stock-return data. Across the considered tail levels, the RTCARE models deliver competitive and often superior forecasting performance relative to existing alternatives, with stable results across Monte Carlo replications and rolling forecast evaluations.

papers.title: Oído: Real-Time Open-Vocabulary Speech Recognition on a $5 Microcontroller without a Neural Accelerator
papers.abstract: Speech recognition on low-cost microcontrollers is, in practice, limited to keyword spotting or a fixed list of commands. We present Oído, an inference engine and a family of models that run open-vocabulary English speech recognition entirely on an ESP32-S3 (240 MHz Xtensa LX7, 8 MB of PSRAM, 16 MB of flash, no neural accelerator) faster than real time on one core. Version 1 of this work ran a 13 M-parameter Conformer-CTC at 1.97x the duration of the audio. We measured on the board that the bound was memory traffic and per-frame cost, not arithmetic: external memory reads at 89 MB/s (PSRAM) and 32 MB/s (flash), and a streaming recognizer re-reads every weight for every chunk. Version 2 combines a model built for that memory system (80 ms frame stacking, a 64-channel front end, 12 or 16 blocks, int4 weights that mostly fit in PSRAM, fine-tuned from the version 1 model) with engine changes that overlap the weight stream with compute (an asynchronous data-cache preload), keep work buffers in SRAM and make the decoder cheap. On a physical board the streaming real-time factor falls from 1.77 to 0.54 (variant B) and 0.72 (variant A), the final text appears 259 ms (B) or 431 ms (A) after the end of speech with audio fed at real-time speed, and the host build and the firmware produce identical transcripts. Variant A reaches 7.1%/16.4% word error rate on LibriSpeech test-clean/test-other in streaming mode with 0.64 s chunks and the on-chip language model (4.6%/10.7% with full context). Code, models and the raw board measurements are released.

papers.title: Adaptive Incentive Design for Linear-Quadratic Dynamic Games: No-Regret Social Coordination
papers.abstract: Incentives can align private interests with collective goals, but their design becomes intertwined with learning when agents' preferences are unknown. This paper develops an adaptive incentive-design framework for multi-agent linear-quadratic dynamic games, where a system planner can simultaneously learn agents' private preferences and steer their strategic behavior towards the social optimum. To this end, we first characterize the complete family of affine incentives that implement the social optimum as the unique open-loop Nash equilibrium while ensuring exact budget balance. When agents' preferences are unknown, we develop an online algorithm to estimate their preference parameters and establish strong consistency of the estimates under a weak trajectory-dependent excitation condition, without requiring persistent excitation or i.i.d. trajectories. We then integrate this estimator into an active-learning incentive mechanism that combines certainty-equivalent coordination with decaying random probing. We prove that the probing generates sufficient information through the agents' equilibrium responses and the system dynamics, ensuring consistent preference learning from the resulting closed-loop trajectories. We show that the induced trajectories converge almost surely to their socially optimal counterparts, while cumulative social-cost regret relative to the full-information oracle and cumulative net-budget imbalance grow sublinearly. Simulations of a transboundary pollution game demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework.

papers.title: Constrained coupled-cluster computations yield negative-parity rotational bands
papers.abstract: Many deformed nuclei exhibit low-lying rotational bands with negative parity. In mean-field calculations, such bands follow from symmetry restoration when the variational solution spontaneously breaks parity. However, they can also be computed in cases where the breaking of parity is not spontaneous but rather enforced by an octupole constraint. In this paper, we extend these techniques to coupled-cluster computations. We introduce octupole-constrained coupled-cluster theory, which explicitly breaks the parity of the correlated intrinsic state and restores parity and angular momentum as good quantum numbers by projection after variation. We perform coupled-cluster singles-and-doubles (CCSD) computations for $^{20}$Ne using two- and three-nucleon forces from chiral effective field theory. The energies of the positive-parity ground-state rotational band are close to data and depend only weakly on the constrained octupole moment and the Hartree--Fock reference. In contrast, the energies of the negative-parity rotational band are more sensitive to these auxiliary quantities.

papers.title: A complex associated to a family of ideals and applications to subspace arrangements
papers.abstract: We reprove and generalize a result of Derksen describing the Hilbert polynomial of the vanishing ideal of a transversal subspace arrangement in projective space. When the subspaces have all codimension 2, we describe explicitly the local cohomology modules of the corresponding defining ideal. This is achieved via a complex naturally associated to the subspace arrangement, whose basic properties are also investigated.

papers.title: An Optimal Control Approach to Finite-Time Stabilization of Linear Systems
papers.abstract: This paper presents a finite-time stabilization method for the integrator chain via optimal control techniques by introducing a tailored cost function. We analyze key properties of the resulting value function to derive the corresponding Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation. Numerical simulations illustrate the effectiveness of the approach.

papers.title: Deterministic Girth Approximation in Weighted Undirected Graphs
papers.abstract: We give deterministic algorithms for approximating the girth~$g$ of an undirected graph with $n$ vertices, $m$ edges, and nonnegative real edge lengths. For every integer $k\geq2$, our algorithm returns a cycle of length at most $\frac{2k}{3}g$ in $O((m+n^{1+2/k})k\log n)$ worst-case time. For every constant~$k$, this matches the stretch and the expected running time of the randomized algorithms of Kadria, Roditty, Sidford, Vassilevska Williams, and Zwick [SODA'23, SICOMP'26] and Kadria, Roditty, and Vassilevska Williams [ESA'26]. In general, it loses only a factor of $O(\min\{k,\log n\})$ in the term that depends on~$m$. The best previous deterministic trade-off, of Kadria, Roditty, Sidford, Vassilevska Williams, and Zwick [SODA'22], has stretch~$k$ instead of $\frac{2k}{3}$ at the same exponent (for even~$k$) and requires integer edge lengths. In particular, for $k=3$ we obtain a deterministic $2$-approximation in $O((m+n^{5/3})\log n)$ time for real edge lengths, whereas the deterministic algorithm of Ducoffe [SIDMA'21] for real lengths has stretch $2+\varepsilon$. Our main technical idea is that a deterministic construction of the Thorup--Zwick hierarchy used by these algorithms may stop exploring as soon as it finds a cycle: the approximation analysis only needs clusters truncated at half the best cycle certificate found, so balls stopped in this way need not be hit. Together with a degree-weighted selection rule, this bounds the work of each level by its number of edges and stored ball entries. More generally, a ball need not be hit whenever the analysis only uses clusters up to a radius bounded by a certificate that the algorithm has already found.

papers.title: IceCube data for astrophysical neutrinos exhibit q-statistical behavior
papers.abstract: Relevant IceCube recent data for astrophysical neutrinos are analyzed. Similarly to cosmic rays and proton-proton LHC collisions, the corresponding spectra are satisfactorily described, for the entire interval of measured energies, through $q$-Gaussians. This fact reinforces the already available evidence that nonadditive entropies (either of the $S_q$ class or of the $S_δ$ one, or even alternative ones) appear to play a crucial role in systems such as black holes and related cosmological phenomena (e.g., dark energy). The IceCube data yield high values for the momenta-distribution nonadditive index ($q \simeq 1.6$, hence $q_{energy} \simeq 1.3$), to be compared with the cosmic rays values ($q_{energy} \simeq 1.2$) and the LHC values ($q_{energy} \simeq 1.1$). This fact neatly indicates very-long-ranged space-time correlations. The detailed associated physical mechanisms remain, at the present stage, as an instigating open issue.

papers.title: Reflect-VLA: Internalizing Reflective Guidance via Dual-Path On-Policy Self-Distillation for Autonomous Driving
papers.abstract: Reinforcement Learning (RL) substantially improves planning performance in autonomous-driving Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models. However, existing RL methods rely on scalar trajectory rewards that measure overall quality but fail to identify specific planning errors or provide actionable correction signals. In long-tail scenarios, errors in scene understanding, behavior selection, and trajectory execution are compressed into a single score. We observe that Reflective Guidance turns trajectory evaluation into explicit diagnoses and corrective instructions, substantially improving planning accuracy. Yet such guidance requires an initial prediction and its evaluation results, making it unavailable for direct single-pass inference. We propose Reflect-VLA, which treats Reflective Guidance as training-time privileged information and internalizes its planning benefits through Dual-Path On-Policy Self-Distillation (Dual-OPSD). Unlike scalar-reward optimization, Dual-OPSD uses the driving score only to route student-generated trajectories. It distills dense token-level corrective distributions from the teacher for risky trajectories while applying self-imitation to preserve reliable ones. To provide reliable corrective distributions on student rollouts, the teacher is progressively constructed through Driving-Knowledge Pretraining, Planning-and-Refinement SFT, and Self-Refinement Rejection Sampling. At inference time, Reflect-VLA generates trajectories in a single pass without explicit guidance or iterative refinement. Experiments on NAVSIM v1/v2 and Bench2Drive demonstrate competitive planning performance while reducing training time by over 90% compared with RL.

papers.title: Utility-Based Recovery Risk Measures: Redundancy and Approximation for Portfolio Optimization
papers.abstract: Recovery risk measures incorporate explicit liability-recovery requirements into asset-liability risk assessment. We study their specialization to optimized certainty equivalents (OCEs), allowing the underlying utility specification to vary across recovery levels and encompassing Recovery Average Value at Risk (RecAV@R) as a special case. For finite recovery specifications, we use the dual penalty representation to characterize redundant recovery regimes and derive position-independent screening conditions. For a subfamily of the Cressie-Read power-divergence family, including entropic and truncated-quadratic specifications, we obtain an exact characterization on atomless probability spaces: universal redundancy is equivalent to a two-dimensional convex-hull condition involving recovery levels and divergence-scale parameters. On such spaces, universal redundancy for RecAV@R reduces to pairwise dominance, whereas for power-divergence OCEs it can arise from the joint effect of several recovery regimes. For nonlinear OCE utilities, we develop a certified piecewise-linear approximation framework for portfolio optimization. In finite-scenario models, the approximating problems are finite-dimensional linear programs, while utility approximation errors transfer directly to the Recovery OCE, yielding explicit error bounds and convergence rates. Uniform approximation over the portfolio domain further implies convergence of optimal values and stability of optimal solutions. A numerical asset-liability study illustrates the effects of recovery-dependent risk preferences and the accuracy and convergence of the approximation.

papers.title: Agentic Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have taken the world by storm. Their ability to communicate with us in our own language, and to reason about our world, has made them a favorite tool for writing, answering questions, and much more. Their answers already influence our decisions and our actions. What would happen if LLMs themselves could act in the world directly? What would happen if LLMs could interact with each other? Agentic LLMs combine the power of large language models with the ability to act in the real world. In this book we will discuss how agentic LLMs work, how they act, how they interact, and what this means for us, as users.

papers.title: Towards Enriching Design-Time Models with Evidence from Simulation and Operational Activities
papers.abstract: Cyber-Physical Systems are developed through multiple model based activities, comprising several stages of development. As the development progresses through simulation, experimentation, and operation, observations of system execution may reveal missing, uncertain, or invalid design knowledge. The path from execution results to persistent design-time enrichment, however, is often implicit. This paper addresses this challenge by proposing an evidence driven workflow for systematically transferring knowledge produced during simulation and operation back into design-time models. We demonstrate the workflow using an Influence Model, a design-time artefact used to represent how design artefacts and environmental factors jointly affect system response properties, using a sign-following robot use case. We show how simulation evidence can enrich Influence Models by supporting participant pruning decisions, interaction characterisation, influence-function abstraction, and validity-scope information. The application demonstrates the feasibility of the workflow for simulation-based evidence and its potential benefits to improve design-time reasoning and feedback in subsequent development iterations.

papers.title: The binormal flow: a toy model for turbulence
papers.abstract: These notes summarize the content of a one-week course given by Luis Vega on the binormal flow model applied to describe the dynamics of three-dimensional vortex filaments in incompressible fluids following the Euler equations. This topic touches connections between the binormal flow, the Schrödinger map and the 1d cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation, providing a rich casuistry linked to the physical and numerical phenomenology. This course was part of the $2^{\text{nd}}$ Advanced Summer School held at the Institut d'Etudes Scientifiques de Cargèse (IESC), at Cargèse (Corsica), from $20^{\text{th}}$ to $30^{\text{th}}$ June 2023. These notes have been written and completed by two of its attendees, Elena Danesi and Pablo Merino.

papers.title: The DP color function of joins and vertex-gluing of hypergraphs
papers.abstract: The DP color function $P_{DP}(\mathcal{H}, k)$ of a hypergraph $\mathcal{H}$ is defined as the minimum possible value of $P_{DP}(\mathcal{H}, \mathcal{F})$ taken over all $k$-fold covers $\mathcal{F}$ of $\mathcal{H}$. It serves as an extension of the classical chromatic polynomial. In this paper, we investigate the DP color function for two constructions: the join of a hypergraph with a complete graph and vertex-gluings of certain hypergraphs. Both constructions extend some results of Becker et al.

papers.title: A functional mixed-effects model for the joint analysis of amplitude and phase variations in function-valued traits
papers.abstract: Quantitative genetics is the study of continuous traits and the statistical analysis of phenotypic variation, that is, the observable differences in physical traits among individuals within a population. If family relationships between individuals are known, phenotypic variation can be partitioned into genetic and environmental components. Some traits, such as growth trajectories, can be described as a function of a continuous index and are known as function-valued traits. However, function-valued traits from different individuals often vary not only in their shape (amplitude) but also in the speed at which the biological process develops (phase). In this work, we present and compare two approaches to account for amplitude and phase variations in estimating the additive genetic and environmental components. The first one follows from a conventional framework where warping functions remove phase variations, and then the aligned curves are analysed. The second approach adopts the perspective of looking at the aligned curve and the warping function as a joint functional object. In both cases, we propose a functional mixed-effects framework that uses functional principal components as the data-driven basis for genetically correlated data. The proposed procedure is applied to simulations and a real-case study of Tribolium castaneum growth trajectories.

papers.title: Brown's loss function and estimation of the scale parameter and the entropy in scale mixture models with unknown location
papers.abstract: This paper deals with the problems of decision theoretic estimation of the scale parameter, $σ$, and the entropy (Shannon or Renyi) in general scale mixture models with unknown location. Employing Kubokawa's approach, under convexity of the loss $L(t)$ either in $t$ or in $lnt$, improved estimators of $σ$ are derived. If $L(t)$ satisfies an additional condition, the problem reduces to estimating $σ$ in the degenerate (scale mixture) model. As the entropy is a linear translation of $lnσ$, its estimation under a loss $L_0(u)$ amounts to estimating $σ$ under $L(t)=L_0(lnt)$, with the quadratic loss $L_0(u)=u^2$ and Brown's loss $L(t)=(lnt)^2$ being a typical case. Thus, in the case that $L_0(u)$ is convex improved estimators of the entropy are directly obtained from respective estimators of $σ$. The results are applied to scale mixtures of normal and exponential distributions, including the multivariate $t$ and multivariate Lomax distributions.

papers.title: SqueezeBench: Saturation-Resilient Evaluation of Mathematical Capability
papers.abstract: AI systems are making rapid progress in mathematics, but this progress is hard to measure. Benchmarks of solved problems saturate, and in benchmarks of open problems each problem can be resolved for the first time only once. We present SqueezeBench, a benchmark that is resilient to saturation: a success raises the bar instead of removing the problem. Each problem fixes an integer function $f(n)$ whose values are known only for small $n$, and the benchmark keeps a lower and an upper record on it. A record is a computable Lean function with a machine-checked proof that it bounds $f$. A submission proposes a new function and proves that it bounds $f$, that it is no worse than the current record at any $n$, and that it is strictly better at some $n$. Once accepted, it becomes the record that the next submission has to beat. The system thus chooses the bound as well as its proof, and it may improve the record at a single $n$ or its growth rate. At every $n$, the gap between the two records shows how far the certified bounds are from determining $f(n)$. Every proof is checked by two independent Lean kernels, so no referee needs to check the mathematics. The checks also reject a function that computes $f$ by exhaustive search at small $n$, and a maintainer only reads the submitter's report and looks for such a search at larger $n$. We release ten problems from extremal combinatorics with twenty proved initial records and the admission tools. As a baseline, agents based on a frontier language model, with at most one hour per record, had 82 submissions accepted and improved every record, without going beyond the published literature. Agents based on two newer models then started from these records, had 60 more submissions accepted and improved 19 of the 20 records again. For eight of the ten problems, at least one record is still asymptotically behind the best published bound.

papers.title: OC-AND: A Citation-Enriched Benchmark for Author Name Disambiguation
papers.abstract: Author Name Disambiguation benchmarks are predominantly derived from closed infrastructures that may not reflect conditions in open bibliographic environments. We present OC-AND, an open citation-enriched benchmark for AND constructed by remapping the WhoIsWho dataset with bibliographic and citation metadata from OpenCitations. The dataset is produced through a reproducible five-stage pipeline involving DOI verification, metadata validation, OpenCitations enrichment, and author-centric transformation. OC-AND retains the WhoIsWho ground-truth files and partition structure unchanged, while its publication files are restricted to publications that could be matched to a validated DOI and an OpenCitations record. It introduces realistic characteristics of open environments: heterogeneous metadata completeness, absent abstracts and affiliations, asymmetric citation coverage, and sparse graph connectivity. The dataset contains author records with associated citations, enabling evaluation of AND methods in settings closer to real-world open scholarly infrastructure scenarios. OC-AND is released as open data with complete provenance documentation and pipeline code, supporting reproducible research and the development of citation-aware disambiguation approaches.

papers.title: Exact rational certificates and a Lean formalization of the eleven-variable Vasc inequality
papers.abstract: We prove that the cyclic sum $\sum_{i=0}^{10}(x_i-x_{i+1})/(x_{i+1}+x_{i+2})$ is nonnegative for every strictly positive real eleven-tuple, with indices taken modulo eleven. Clearing denominators reduces the problem to a homogeneous polynomial. Subtracting the smallest coordinate then separates the proof into nonnegativity of a common-translation derivative and nonnegativity on a full boundary face. We supply exact rational polynomial certificates in Gram-matrix form for both statements. The derivative certificate uses a linear multiplier, centered monomials and cyclic averaging; the boundary certificate uses a strictly positive quadratic multiplier and uncentered monomials. Their verification requires 6,069 cyclic coefficient comparisons and 34,304 literal coefficient comparisons. All 606 certificate matrices are certified by integer congruences with strictly diagonally dominant images. A Lean 4 development formally verifies the certificate checks and their connection to the original inequality. The exact certificate data, replay programs, and formal sources are publicly available.

papers.title: Gaussian BROJA Partial Information Decomposition in Closed Form
papers.abstract: The BROJA partial information decomposition provides an operationally motivated way to separate the information that two sources carry about a target into unique, redundant, and synergistic components. For continuous and high-dimensional variables, however, computing the BROJA decomposition requires solving a difficult optimization problem. Previous work showed that, when each source-target pair is jointly Gaussian, the problem can be reduced to finite-dimensional numerical optimization. Here, we derive a closed-form solution to this optimization problem, enabling direct computation of the BROJA decomposition in the general multivariate Gaussian setting. The resulting closed-form expression enables speedups exceeding two orders of magnitude for high-dimensional Gaussian BROJA PID. Code is available at https://github.com/brainsandmachines/Eigen_PID.

papers.title: When MLLMs miss what humans read: diagnosing and learning to read squint text
papers.abstract: Multimodal LLMs can fail to read text embedded in an image's coarse structure (text a human recovers by squinting) and report that no text is present. We name this class Squint Text and study it as a recognition deficiency, motivated by cases from a production moderation pipeline. We introduce SquintBench, comprising 1076 production-derived moderation images, and SquintCtrl, a controlled synthetic suite for mechanism diagnosis. Frozen-weight analysis shows that hidden text leaves a coarse signal while glyph identity is weakly represented; identity becomes substantially more accessible when the correct spatial regions are supplied, implicating spatial selection as a major bottleneck. Suppressing high-frequency content also improves reading at a fixed visual-token budget, while visual token count may also contribute. These findings motivate Squint OPSD: a frozen teacher receives a downscaled view and the ground-truth transcription as privileged context, and its token-level distributions supervise a student along on-policy trajectories. At inference, the student reads the original image alone. Squint OPSD reaches 88.61 ANLS on SquintBench, versus 26.50 for the unadapted backbone, 24.44 for the best general-purpose model on the original view, and 68.60 at best for an off-the-shelf model under a downscaled view. These results substantially narrow the gap between available visual evidence and its generated read-out without auxiliary views at inference.

papers.title: A Real-World CAD Segmentation Benchmark: Comparing Rule-Based and Learning-Based Approaches through Hole Detection
papers.abstract: CAD segmentation datasets are predominantly synthetic or automatically labelled, leaving it unclear how well existing methods transfer to real-world engineering tasks. Fastener-relevant hole detection represents one such task, requiring human annotation and exhibiting greater geometric complexity than commonly used benchmarks. We address this gap through three main contributions. First, we develop two task-specific rule-based methods, one graph-wire-search and one multi-view based, and complement them with a human-annotated benchmark dataset derived from engineering CAD data that also enables training of UV-Net and AAGNet, representative learning-based approaches for B-Rep segmentation. Second, we conduct an extensive experimental study including parameter optimisation, evaluation on our benchmark dataset, cross-domain generalisation on a synthetic dataset, and an assessment of the feasibility of the approaches at varying dataset sizes and IoU thresholds. Third, we provide evidence-based insights into the strengths and limitations of different approaches: rule-based methods generalise well without training data, with the graph-wire-search method favouring recall and the multi-view method favouring precision, whereas learning-based methods achieve strong performance with sufficient annotations but exhibit reduced robustness under domain shift. These findings highlight trade-offs between data requirements, and robustness, and provide guidance not only for hole detection, but more broadly for real-world CAD segmentation tasks.

papers.title: A Multi-Dimensional Score for Detecting Lesser-Known Points of Interest in Mountain Regions
papers.abstract: Overtourism concentrates visitor demand on few iconic sites, while other points of interest (POIs) in the same area often remain known only to a narrower public. This imbalance is especially critical in mountain environments, where limited infrastructure amplifies environmental pressures. Discovering lesser-known POIs is relevant for redistributing tourism demand spatially, valuing underrepresented heritage, and temporally, easing high seasonality pressures on popular POIs. Across the literature, definitions of lesser-known POIs or hidden gems remain scattered, and existing scoring approaches remain incomplete, relying on narrow indicators (e.g., number of photos, reviews, likes) which fail to characterize mountain POIs holistically. These approaches are further constrained by their reliance on commercial proprietary sources, or by questionnaires that are subject to memory bias. To address these gaps, we introduce a novel multi-dimensional metric, the Obscurity Score, that groups fragmented literature into four key dimensions (International Awareness, Attractiveness, Promotion, and Accessibility) to systematically detect and characterize lesser-known POIs and enable their promotion as a first step toward mitigating overtourism. To operationalize this score, we develop a generic pipeline mapping open data sources onto these four dimensions. Preliminary results from a web-based prototype demonstrate the practical relevance of the proposed approach.

papers.title: Sharp Bounds for Limits of $N$-Point Correlation
papers.abstract: We consider the question which functions $f$ may appear as limiting functions of the $N$-point correlation. We obtain sharp point-wise lower and upper bounds. The explicit examples constructed to show the sharpness of the bounds are based on van der Corput sequences.

papers.title: Quillen's local parameter conjecture in dimension four
papers.abstract: Let $R$ be a Noetherian regular local ring of mixed characteristic and dimension four, and let $r$ be a member of a regular system of parameters. We prove that every finitely generated projective module over $R[1/r]$ is free. We also prove that $\mathrm{Sp}_4(R[1/r])$ acts transitively on unimodular columns of length four and that every determinant orientation of a rank-two projective module is induced by a basis. The argument reduces freeness to two vanishing results: the degree-three Zariski cohomology of the naive degree-four Milnor--Witt sheaf and the alternating Witt group of $R[1/r]$. We establish these results using integral degree-two algebraic $K$-theory, supported hermitian $K$-theory, and local motivic cohomology. A finite-rank symplectic comparison relates the image of the completion obstruction to Milnor--Witt multiplication and yields the required symplectic frames.

papers.title: GraftOOD: Grafting Out-of-Distribution Exemplars into Advantage-Weighted Rectification for Video Reward Optimization
papers.abstract: Video reward optimization can increase proxy rewards while reducing video dynamics, a mismatch we identify as \emph{motion collapse}, including under a video-level motion-quality reward. We propose \textbf{GraftOOD}, which replaces part of the online rollouts in selected prompt groups with out-of-distribution video exemplars. A shared velocity-regression objective combines group-relative reward rectification with sequence-level exemplar supervision, requiring neither exemplar generation trajectories nor an additional supervised-loss coefficient. We characterize its pointwise optimal field as a source-posterior-weighted combination of the two source-specific target fields. We construct \textbf{GraftSet-Video}, containing 9,588 format-matched exemplars for 2,397 prompts, to supply external supervision. On Wan2.1-1.3B, GraftOOD raises Dynamic Degree from 4.86 to 44.41 relative to reward-only FlowAWR, while HPSv3 decreases from 8.10 to 7.32 and VisionReward remains close. At the main setting, GraftOOD leads nine of ten metrics among three exemplar-augmented methods. Ablations of exemplar frequency and within-group count reveal dynamics--reward trade-offs rather than uniform gains from increasing exemplar usage. These results support external exemplar supervision as a complement to scalar reward feedback, without equating higher measured dynamics with coherent, visually plausible motion in the generated videos. Code is available at \href{https://github.com/Fuzm7/FlowAWR}{GraftOOD}.

papers.title: Conserved amount, negotiable placement. Prompting perturbs one architecture, an AI reviewer both
papers.abstract: Tesler's conservation law holds that a problem carries an irreducible amount of complexity. Brooks separates that essential part from the accidental part a solution adds. If the essential part is fixed, architecture is placement rather than quantity, and the question is which levers move placement. An AI agent implements sixty accumulating change requests on one REST endpoint under two architectures, a mutative Spring controller and an additive OfficeFloor pipeline, under five conditions, ten runs per cell, model fixed. Four are external controls, from a bare change request to the disclosed structural cost function. The fifth is different in kind. A second agent reviews each change and reasons about cohesion itself. Amount is steady. Across all ten cells the finished complexity varies by 7% to 20% over four operationalisations, and the complexity the sixty rules added by 21% to 29% within an architecture. Placement is not. Under the four external controls the plasticity ratio between the architectures is near 1 on six amount metrics (five of six intervals contain 1) against 2.7 to 10.0 on eleven placement metrics (ten of eleven above 1). The mutative architecture moves, the additive one does not, and the disclosed formula brings it to the additive arm's untouched placement. The AI reviewer is the one lever that moves the additive arm, on one family only. It consolidates the pipeline, raising change- and mass-concentration on every such metric, interval excluding zero, while leaving coupling, file count and per-node complexity untouched. The price is reported in full. Strict correctness fell in most comparisons though each rule was implemented correctly in over 99% of checkpoints, and all three outcome measures favour the concentrated codebase. The contribution is a measurable property of an architecture and its lever, not a verdict on either.

papers.title: Two Cosmological Histories in a New Exponential Infrared $f(T)$ Teleparallel Gravity: Implications for the Hubble Tension and the Low-$\ell$ Planck TT--EE Tension
papers.abstract: We investigate a particular case of the New Exponential Infrared $f(T)$ teleparallel gravity model with the same number of free parameters as the standard $Λ$CDM model. Remarkably, due to the two real branches of the Lambert function $W$, the model admits two distinct cosmological solutions, denoted by $f^{(I)}$CDM and $f^{(II)}$CDM. The former exhibits a late-time phantom crossing, whereas the latter predicts an effective dark-energy density evolving from negative to positive values. Using a Markov Chain Monte Carlo analysis of the Planck CMB, DESI BAO, and Type Ia supernova data, we find that the $f^{(II)}$CDM branch develops a bimodal posterior distribution in the primordial parameters $A_s$ and $τ_{ reio}$ for the Planck-only dataset. We show that this bimodality originates from the tension between the low-$\ell$ TT and EE likelihoods, which becomes pronounced in models exhibiting a significantly enhanced late ISW contribution relative to the $Λ$CDM model. Moreover, the inclusion of background observations drives this branch toward cosmologically unacceptable parameter values, rendering it observationally unviable. The $f^{(I)}$CDM branch, on the other hand, remains observationally viable, yielding $H_0=73.43\pm0.69~\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$ for the Planck-only dataset and $H_0=72.55\pm0.32~\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$ after including DESI, substantially alleviating the Hubble tension. Although this branch provides a slightly better fit than $Λ$CDM for Planck-only data, the addition of background observations reverses this preference in favor of the standard $Λ$CDM model. These results show that the cosmological viability of this model critically depends on the choice of the Lambert $W$ branch, with only the $f^{(I)}$CDM solution remaining compatible with current cosmological observations.

papers.title: REMBGO for Evaluation-Limited Optimization: CEC2022 Benchmarking and EAF-STATCOM Generalization
papers.abstract: Metaheuristic comparisons are often reported at evaluation budgets far larger than an expensive engineering simulation can afford. This paper presents REMBGO, an evaluation-budget-aware refinement of EMBGO. Its contribution is not any single operator: it is the integration of population preservation, scale-normalized exploration and recovery mechanisms whose parent-relative benefit is concentrated under restricted function-evaluation budgets. REMBGO is evaluated on CEC2022 at a primary, application-aligned budget of 1040 function evaluations, with a surrounding budget ladder reported descriptively to characterise budget dependence rather than as a family of controlled hypotheses. A component-removal study finds no individual mechanism whose removal survives multiplicity correction, consistent with an integrated rather than a single-operator contribution. The algorithm is then applied to EAF--STATCOM controller tuning, and the resulting frozen gain vectors are transferred without retuning to twenty pre-specified unseen stochastic arc realizations ($210$ fixed-gain simulations, all feasible). The selected gain-vector main effect accounts for only $3.6$--$5.8\%$ of the crossed validation variation, against approximately $61.4\%$ for interaction plus residual, and the matched REMBGO--EMBGO paired differences are controller-dependent in sign and not statistically significant. REMBGO is therefore presented as a resource-aware refinement whose benefit must be stated together with the evaluation budget, not as a universally superior optimizer.

papers.title: How Many Significant LISA?: A multiple testing correction
papers.abstract: In spatial data analysis, global measures of spatial correlation provide useful insights into the general spatial patterns, but fail to capture local variations. Local Indicators of Spatial Association (LISA) address this limitation by identifying local clusters and spatial outliers, offering valuable applications in many fields of research such as public health, urban planning and environmental monitoring, to name only a few. However, the application of LISA tools in hypothesis testing is undermined by the presence of the multiple testing problem which dramatically increases the risk of committing Type I errors especially when dealing with very large datasets. Standard corrections procedure (like, e. g., Bonferroni and Benjamini-Hochberg procedures) fail to consider the spatial dependence among the various LISA tests and, furthermore, they are overly conservative. This paper proposes an adjustment that, by incorporating the notion of the "effective sample size", improves statistical inference balancing false discovery rate control and statistical power.

papers.title: Breaking Two Barriers for Dynamic Planar Reachability
papers.abstract: We consider the reachability problem in fully dynamic directed planar graphs: the graph undergoes edge updates (insertions and deletions) and we receive queries asking if one vertex is reachable from another. The current-best online algorithm for dynamic planar reachability spends worst-case time $\widetilde{O}(n^{2/3})$ per query/update [Subramanian, ESA '93]. This can be improved to $\widetilde{O}(n^{1/2})$ in the offline setting or when the embedding is fixed [Diks and Sankowski, ESA '07]. Our contribution is twofold: 1. We present the first algorithm that breaks the square-root barrier for dynamic planar reachability in the offline setting, obtaining time ${O}(n^{0.49})$ per query/update. This shows that the problem is easier than answering distance queries in a dynamic undirected planar graph, for which a conditional lower bound of $n^{1/2 - o(1)}$ is known [Abboud and Dahlgaard, FOCS '16]. Notably, this lower bound applies to both online and offline algorithms. 2. Second, in the general online setting we design a randomized data structure with amortized update and query time ${O}(n^{0.664})$. This is the first improvement upon the exponent $2/3$ in over three decades. The main engine behind our theorems is a new sparsification framework aimed at maintaining information about reachability. Specifically, we study digraphs through the lens of VC dimensionality of certain set systems. First, we design sparse reachability emulators for planar digraphs that preserve the VC dimension. Second, we utilize orderings with a low ``stabbing number'' [Chazelle and Welzl, Discrete Comput. Geom. '89] to compute subquadratic reachability emulators in subquadratic time whenever the VC dimension is bounded.

papers.title: CompileMask: Bridging the Gap Between Expressiveness and Efficiency in Attention Masking
papers.abstract: Modern attention workloads require diverse masking patterns whose boundaries depend on runtime metadata, yet efficient attention kernels natively support only a small set of patterns. Existing methods for supporting custom masks in these kernels face an expressiveness-efficiency trade-off. Predicate-based methods are expressive but incur substantial preprocessing and execution overhead, whereas interval-based methods execute efficiently but restrict expressiveness through a predefined interval count. We present CompileMask, which addresses this trade-off by connecting expressive mask specifications with efficient attention execution. We design a compiler that analyzes visibility rules during the offline stage and generates a mask-specific preprocess kernel. We further propose MaskSpec, a region-based DSL that lets users express these rules. During the online stage, the generated kernel reads batch metadata and produces a compact Execution Descriptor that lets the attention kernel efficiently check visibility by comparing element indices against precomputed endpoints. Experiments show that CompileMask achieves up to $3.8\times$ speedup over state-of-the-art methods.

papers.title: Each simplex in $\mathbb{R}^4$ has a point with at least $14$ emanating normals to its boundary
papers.abstract: We prove that each simplex in $\mathbb{R}^4$ contains a point with at least $14$ emanating normals to the boundary. Earlier, the authors proved that each generic simple polytope in $\mathbb{R}^4$ contains a point with at least $12$ emanating normals to the boundary. This problem belongs to a piecewise linear counterpart of a longstanding problem concerning normals to smooth convex bodies.

papers.title: A Better Metric Will Not Save You: What You Compare Beats How You Compare It
papers.abstract: Representational similarity measures (RSA, CKA, Procrustes) are chosen for the transformations they treat as irrelevant, and all of them take the set of conditions as given. That set is fixed by two decisions, which inputs are admitted and how they are grouped, both taken before the matrix a measure operates on exists: no invariance property reaches them. We measure what they are worth where the arrangement the conditions ought to have is known independently of the systems compared, the acoustic organisation of vowels, across fifteen languages and twenty-seven representations. Changing which categories are compared, at a fixed number of them, moves the gap between two representations by more than twice the effect being measured, while changing how many moves it not at all. In this setting rankings of models are identified under these choices, and rankings across languages are not.

papers.title: Harmonic analysis and circuit approximation of Sobolev functions on quantum input spaces
papers.abstract: We derive approximation rates for Sobolev functions defined on the complex unit sphere and complex projective space, representing quantum states, and on the special and projective unitary groups, representing quantum unitary operations. By using harmonic analysis on compact groups and compact homogeneous spaces, we characterize the corresponding Peter--Weyl decompositions and Sobolev spaces via irreducible representations and the Laplace--Beltrami operator. Combining spectral truncation with finite-depth quantum-circuit approximation, invoking the Solovay--Kitaev theorem, we establish quantitative rates that separate the spectral truncation error from the circuit approximation error.

papers.title: On physical implementability of reinforcement-learning-driven reasoning
papers.abstract: In the machine learning community, the reinforcement-learning-driven reasoning process has been intensively studied since around 2025. In this article, we present a negative result on the hardware implementation of this reinforcement-learning-driven reasoning process in a physical neural network model in the presence of a reward external potential energy for a given reward. In this hardware implementation, the existence of a chain of thought in dynamics contradicts the Lyapunov stability of the system.

papers.title: Complex Monge-Amp{è}re equations with boundary values: a variational approach
papers.abstract: Let $Ω$ ___ C n be a bounded hyperconvex domain and $Φ$\,: $Ω$ $\rightarrow$ R a maximal plurisubharmonic function in $Ω$ (possibly unbounded). We introduce a new class E 1 $Φ$ ($Ω$) of plurisubharmonic functions with boundary values equal to $Φ$ in the sense of Cegrell and finite $Φ$-energy on $Ω$. Then given a Borel measure $μ$ on $Ω$, we apply a variational approach to prove that $μ$ is the Monge-Amp{è}re measure of a function u $\in$ E 1 $Φ$ ($Ω$) if and only if it satisfies the integrability condition We also establish a quantitative version of this condition extending previous results of Cegrell and others. Using a logarithmic transformation, we obtain analogous results for the real Monge-Amp{è}re equations with (unbounded) boundary data.

papers.title: A Local Agentic AI Framework to Generate Edge Case Scenarios for Safety Assurance
papers.abstract: Generating edge case scenarios is crucial for training, testing and safety assuring autonomous systems. This identifies hazardous failures to increase system reliability and robustness, ensures the system can still function safely on the boundaries of its operational design domain and learns the expected system behaviour for these edge cases. The rapid advancement in the generation and analysis capabilities of language models (LMs) has expanded their applicability and recent work has investigated LM scenario generation. However, many recent approaches rely on human-in-the-loop or rule-based strategies. This restricts the LM's ability to generate diverse and edge case scenarios; the long tail of the distribution. Our work uses local LMs in a laptop-based agentic AI framework for adaptive scenario generation. This is cheap, fully-controlled, ensures data privacy and security. It uses think, act, observe, update, and continue loops with lightweight JSON encoding to generate scenarios. We use the system requirements, system description and environment description as knowledge bases in contextual prompts for an LM to ensure scenario realism. A second, independent LM critiques each scenario using domain specific criteria so it can be refined. The refined scenarios are run in simulation and evaluation metrics collected. These metric scores are analysed and similar scenarios are created for edge cases (exploitation) or novel scenarios are generated to explore the scenario space. Post-hoc clustering using metric scores and thematic-type analysis of the rich-text scenario descriptions produced by the LM pinpoints functional gaps and their triggering conditions. This creates traceable evidence for the safety assurance case. Our work highlights the potential of a flexible and adaptive local agentic AI framework for automating edge case generation and producing traceable safety assurance evidence.

papers.title: A Scalable Learned Iterative Solver for Nonlinear MPC via Temporal Decomposition
papers.abstract: Nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) can be applied to large nonlinear systems with complex objectives while enforcing constraints, but the cost of solving the underlying optimization problems limits real-time application for systems with fast dynamics or many states. Neural networks can reduce this online cost by approximating the control law, but may violate constraints and typically require many precomputed optimizer solutions for training. The learning-based iterative solver for constrained optimization (LISCO) instead learns to predict primal-dual steps toward satisfaction of the Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) conditions through self-supervised training without precomputed solutions, but its dense, monolithic architecture grows with the prediction horizon. We remove this horizon dependence by exploiting the temporal structure of the problem in the solver architecture, which makes the network size independent of the horizon while leaving the training loss and the solver iteration unchanged. A closed-loop resampling strategy further aligns the training distribution with closed-loop operation at no additional sampling cost. On an economic NMPC benchmark of a CSTR cascade, the proposed solver scales to larger problems than monolithic LISCO and achieves median speedups of up to a factor of four over IPOPT. In closed loop, it achieves comparable control performance to IPOPT with no observed constraint violations.

papers.title: Branching On-Policy Distillation
papers.abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) provides teacher supervision on student-generated trajectories, but a single trajectory realizes only one continuation at each decision, limiting supervision coverage under a finite sampling budget. We propose BranchOPD (Branching On-Policy Distillation), which selects informative decision points using student uncertainty and teacher-student disagreement, resamples student-policy continuations from shared prefixes, and applies token-level teacher supervision to both main trajectories and branches. BranchOPD operates at token-level decisions in mathematics and within-turn decisions in agent tasks. Shared-prefix reuse reduces student-generated token costs by approximately 19% on ALFWorld and 31% on WebShop relative to seven independent trajectories. We also introduce protocol-boundary repair (PBR), which uses targeted supervision under protocol constraints to mitigate repetition and wasted generation. BranchOPD outperforms Vanilla OPD and Multi-Rollout OPD (n=7) across all evaluated benchmarks, with gains over Vanilla OPD of 18.55 percentage points in mean mathematics accuracy over 16 sampled answers (avg@16) and 13.8 points in mean ALFWorld ID/OOD success. Mechanistic analyses and selection ablations show that branching at uncertain decisions expands subsequent behavior coverage and outperforms random selection and turn-initial branching.

papers.title: Unveiling the Influence of Graphitic Nanocarbon Structures, Defects, and Surface Functional Groups on Supercapacitive Performance in LiTFSI Electrolyte
papers.abstract: When investigating the performance of supercapacitors (SCs), it was found that they offer high-power density and long life but are limited in capacity and energy density. Water-in-salt electrolytes, i.e., 21___m lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl) imide (LiTFSI), offer a solution by expanding the electrochemical window compared to a diluted aqueous environment. While significant research has been dedicated to improving these electrolytes, the impact of carbon properties on energy storage remains relatively underexplored. This study investigated the influence of carbon structures, defects, and surface functional groups on supercapacitive performance in LiTFSI electrolytes. For this purpose, a series of carbon materials, including carbon nano-onions and porous conductive carbon black (ENSACO), were synthesized and systematically modified by oxidative and reductive thermal treatments. Our results indicated that higher specific surface area and active surface area improve the ion adsorption and capacitance, while specific oxygen functionalities, such as carboxylic and anhydride groups, were found to significantly enhance capacitance. Furthermore, crystallinity and graphitic characteristics play a role in capacitance, with smaller graphene domains and greater disorder promoting ion storage. The study demonstrates a direct correlation between carbon microstructure and electrochemical behavior, providing insights into the rational design of carbon electrodes in high-performance SCs.

papers.title: Regularisation and Parameter Choice Rules for Composite Linear Inverse Problems
papers.abstract: In this paper we propose a novel regularisation strategy for structured linear inverse problems of the form $Ax=F \circ G x = z$. Instead of using the operator $A$ or a complex scheme involving both $F$ and $G$ simultaneously, combining already existing and simpler regularisations for $F$ and $G$ allows the use of established and optimised programs for high-speed computations. As classical parameter choice rules fail in the scenario when no source conditions are known because intermediate error bounds may be unavailable, we provide both a-priori and a-posteriori rules with a convergence speed analysis given source conditions. We test the proposed method on the pre-clinical medical imaging technique of magnetic particle imaging with different choices of regularisation and on a convolution problem for an analysis of the convergence speed.

papers.title: BKT transition for $\mathsf{Sine}_β$
papers.abstract: We prove the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) phase transition in the large-distance behaviour of the two-point correlation function of the $\mathsf{Sine}_β$ point process for all $β>0$, confirming the first term of an asymptotic expansion predicted by Forrester.

papers.title: Proactive Agentic Orchestration
papers.abstract: Agentic orchestration delegates tasks to sub-agents with independent contexts, providing a key path to extending the effective execution horizon of large language model agents. However, existing orchestration methods face two limitations: in execution, current methods fix sub-agents' goals and harnesses at creation time, limiting their adaptability to dynamic real-world environments; in optimization, sparse and delayed feedback constrains effective learning of the orchestration policy. To address these limitations, we introduce POrchestra, an on-the-fly proactive agentic orchestration framework. It allows sub-agents to proactively communicate with the orchestrator at any logical point to request harness adjustments while maintaining continuity of local execution. This mechanism not only enables sub-agents to adapt seamlessly to dynamic environments but also naturally inspires On-Policy Orchestration Distillation (OPOD) based on hindsight feedback. OPOD attributes sub-agents' proactive revision requests back to preceding orchestration decisions to derive targeted improvement signals, and leverages these signals as process supervision alongside the final reward to optimize the orchestration policy. We evaluate POrchestra on three long-horizon agent benchmarks spanning deep research, dynamic digital assistance, and software engineering. POrchestra improves task success by an average of 9.1% relative to the strongest baseline; combined with OPOD, it improves small-orchestrator success by an average of 10.0% relative to existing training baselines. POrchestra also achieves a more favorable cost-performance trade-off. Our code is publicly available at https://github.com/XueyangFeng/POrchestra.

papers.title: Weighted Liouville Theorems and A Priori Bounds for Indefinite Superlinear Equations with Pucci's Maximal Operator
papers.abstract: Consider \begin{equation*}\ \left\{ \begin{aligned} -\mathcal_{λ,Λ}^{+}(D^{2}u)&=μu+a(x)u^{p}\quad\text{in}~Ω,\\ u&=0\quad\text{on}~~\partialΩ, \end{aligned} \right. \end{equation*} where $ \ Omega$ is a smooth bounded domain, $a$ is a continuous function which is allowed to change sign. Moreover, the set of zeros of $a$ may have a non-empty interior. The main objective of this article is to establish a uniform bound on the set of positive solutions of the above problem. This approach requires a suitable Liouville-type theorem. We first prove the Liouville-type theorem for $-\mathcal_{λ,Λ}^{+}(D^{2}v)=h(x_{1})f(v),$ where \(h\) is a strictly increasing one-dimensional weight and \(f\) is positive and nondecreasing.

papers.title: On the probability that a random Latin square is all-even
papers.abstract: In a Latin square, every row can be interpreted as a permutation, and therefore has a parity (even or odd). We prove that in a uniformly random $n\times n$ Latin square, the probability that all rows are even is of the form $2^{-n+o(n)}$. This fills a gap left by recent work of Kwan, Petrova and Sawhney: they proved that the row parities behave like a sequence of independent coin flips in a variety of different senses, but they were not able to lower-bound the all-even probability, as their approach had a small number of "exceptional rows" whose parities they could not control. In fact, we prove a more general theorem on the probability of any possible prescription of row parities, column parities and symbol parities. Our approach extends the ideas of Kwan, Petrova and Sawhney, introducing a new way to "bootstrap" intercalate switchings to control more complex switching operations.

papers.title: Neural Block-wise Auto-exposure for Single-Shot High Dynamic Range Imaging
papers.abstract: Block-wise varying exposures are effective for cap- turing appearance of a real-world high dynamic range (HDR) scene via a single-shot. However, brightness order reversal (BOR) artifacts, blocking artifacts and loss of details in highlight/shadow regions are possible issues for block-wise varying exposures. In this paper, a novel neural block-wise auto-exposure algorithm is proposed to address the issues. The proposed algorithm maps a temporary image and its exposure time to the exposure times of all non-overlapping 16 X 16 blocks. The temporary image can be either an sRGB or a raw image. Although the sRGB image is widely adopted in existing auto-exposure algorithms, exposure times of blocks in the highlight and shadow regions might not be accurately learned due to the limited radiance measurement capability of the sRGB image. This paper thus also explores the feasibility of temporary image as a raw image. Due to the better radiance measurement capability of the raw image, the exposure times of blocks are learned more accurately, and more details in the highlight/shadow regions of the real-world HDR scene are captured by the resultant HDR imaging system. Experiment results validate the proposed neural block-wise auto-exposure algorithm.

papers.title: Reconstruction of graphs and surfaces from derived categories
papers.abstract: A pair of topological spaces $X$ and $Y$ is a \emph{Fourier--Mukai (FM) pair} if there is an equivalence of $\infty$-categories of derived sheaves of abelian groups \[\operatorname{Shv}(X;\mathrm D(\mathbb Z))\simeq \operatorname{Shv}(Y;\mathrm D(\mathbb Z)).\] An FM pair $(X,Y)$ is \emph{non-trivial} if $X$ and $Y$ are not homeomorphic. We consider the question of whether non-trivial FM pairs $(X,Y)$ exist for which $X$ and $Y$ are both "nice" spaces, which in this article means admitting a triangulation. We show that the answer is no if $X$ is second-countable and either (i) one-dimensional, (ii) a surface, or (iii) the 3-sphere. In order to prove this, we define two invariants of dualizable categories. The first invariant is an extension of \emph{Tate--Hochschild cohomology} (aka singular Hochschild cohomology) to a class of dualizable categories satisfying a countability assumption. For a homology manifold $X$, we relate the Tate--Hochschild cohomology of $\operatorname{Shv}(X;\mathrm D(\mathbb Z))$ to the homology at infinity of $X$ (in the sense of proper homotopy theory). The second invariant takes the form of a subcategory $\mathcal D_{\mathrm{Gor}}\subseteq\mathcal D$ called the \emph{Gorenstein locus}, defined for every dualizable stable category $\mathcal D$. For a triangularizable space $X$ and a field $k$, we show that the Gorenstein locus of $\operatorname{Shv}(X;\mathrm D(k))$ is equal to the full subcategory of sheaves supported on the $k$-homology manifold locus of $X$.

papers.title: Estimating ratio of variance components in a balanced one-way random effect model
papers.abstract: This paper considers the problem of estimating the ratio of variance components of a balanced one-way random effects model. Existing estimators of ratio of variance, such as the ANOVA and maximum likelihood estimators, can take negative values and are inadmissible under quadratic loss. We therefore study the problem under a general class of scale-invariant loss functions. We characterize the class of scale-equivariant estimators of ratio of variance and obtain the best equivariant estimator. We then derive a class of estimators that dominate the BEE and extend this class to obtain further improved estimators. We propose a smooth improved estimator of ratio of variance. For interval estimation of ratio of variance, we derive an asymptotic confidence interval, bootstrap confidence intervals, a generalized confidence interval and a highest posterior density credible interval. The performance of the proposed improved point estimators and confidence interval procedures is assessed through an extensive simulation study. Finally, we provide a real data analysis for implementation purposes.

papers.title: Quasinormal and hyponormal operators in the $β(H)$-class
papers.abstract: Following \cite{BR} we study hyponormal operators in the strictly larger class $β(H)$ of operators whose restriction to every non-zero reducing subspace is norm attaining. The Weyl-type characterization of positive operators via the essential spectrum used in the absolutely norm attaining case is replaced by a well-ordering condition on the eigenvalues (Theorem~\ref{thm:positive}). We prove a transfinite, block-diagonal representation $T=\bigoplus_iλ_iS_i$ (with isometries $S_i$) for the $β(H)$-operators whose $|T|$-eigenspaces are reducing, equivalently the quasinormal operators with $|T|\inβ(H)$, and we show by examples that hyponormality alone does not give such a decomposition. For normal operators we obtain a complete representation, and for hyponormal $β(H)$-operators we show that normality is equivalent to the spectrum having planar Lebesgue measure zero. An analogous area-zero criterion for normality is proved for hyponormal operators attaining the minimum modulus on every non-zero reducing subspace.

papers.title: EviRepair: Evidence-Driven Agents for Reliable Vulnerability Repair
papers.abstract: Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have enabled agent-based approaches for repository-level automated vulnerability repair (AVR), showing promising repair capabilities. However, an important issue has received limited attention: how can we ensure that the evidence generated during the repair process is reliable enough to support accurate vulnerability understanding and patch generation? In this paper, we propose EviRepair, an evidence-driven multi-agent framework for repository-level AVR. EviRepair introduces evidence review into the repair process by enabling agents to collaboratively collect vulnerability evidence, verify evidence consistency, and construct a reviewed vulnerability model for patch synthesis and validation. Extensive experiments on PatchEval and SecBench benchmarks with multiple agent frameworks and LLMs demonstrate that EviRepair consistently outperforms existing agent-based baselines, achieving average improvements of 16.37% and 40.33% in resolved rates on PatchEval and SecBench, respectively. Codes are available at https://github.com/lly-s/EviRepair

papers.title: An empirical calibration of the spectral resolution of JWST NIRSpec PRISM
papers.abstract: We present an empirical calibration of the effective spectral resolution of the JWST NIRSpec PRISM disperser based on a large sample of galaxies drawn from archival observations. Our sample spans a wide redshift range, $0.5 \lesssim z \lesssim 10$, enabling a wavelength-dependent characterization of the PRISM resolving power across the full bandpass using the [O III]$λ\lambda4959,5007$ doublets. To ensure robust measurements, we impose strict signal-to-noise requirements on both continuum and emission-line detections. Emission-line profiles are fitted with multi-Gaussian models, and the full width at half maximum (FWHM) is measured for each source. The derived empirical resolution curve shows a systematic offset from the nominal pre-launch estimate, lying between the tabulated instrumental resolution and the point-source shutter limit. We also discuss how source size affects the final spectral resolution, and provide an analytical formula that combines wavelength and morphology dependence in a root-sum-square framework. This work delivers a population-averaged, statistically robust calibration of the effective PRISM spectral resolution for typical galaxy observations. The resulting calibration is directly applicable to statistical analyses of galaxy spectra obtained with NIRSpec PRISM. Our empirical calibration exceeds the pre-launch JDox values by a factor of 1.03 to 1.63, depending on source morphology, and provides the first wavelength and morphology dependent calibration of the NIRSpec PRISM spectral resolution.

papers.title: Controlling the Atomic Reconstruction in Twisted MoSe$_2$/WSe$_2$ with a Monolayer hBN Spacer
papers.abstract: Twisted van der Waals heterobilayers are a promising material platform for studying collective exciton many-body phenomena, but near-aligned structures often exhibit a local, anisotropic atomic reconstruction that compromises lateral homogeneity. The present study describes how atomic-scale rearrangement in adjacent regions of hBN-encapsulated, near-aligned MoSe$_2$/WSe$_2$ heterobilayers is controlled by the presence of a mono- or bilayer hBN spacer between the two monolayers. High-angle annular dark-field STEM directly resolves the atomic alignment in both layers and shows that the spacer suppresses the reconstruction and strongly increases the structural uniformity of the heterobilayers. 4D-STEM quantitatively maps local rotation, dilation, and heterostrain, revealing that the separated regions remain consistent with rigid moiré superlattice simulations, whereas without the spacer the structural parameters have two to three times broader distributions. By suppressing reconstruction, ultrathin hBN spacers therefore provide an effective route to enhance lattice homogeneity in MoSe$_2$/WSe$_2$ heterobilayers targeting collective excitonic and optoelectronic phenomena.

papers.title: Humanize MLE Agents: Multi-Agent Session Alternation Beyond Single-Agent Limits
papers.abstract: Existing LLM-based agent approaches for long-horizon machine learning engineering (MLE) often use context engineering, implemented through custom harnesses that manage tools, skills, and accumulated experience. However, we find that as single-session execution lengthens, the agent's reasoning intensity declines alongside slowing progress, summarized as long-horizon deceleration, and the benefits of these custom harnesses vanish as the underlying model improves, summarized as harness staleness. These findings suggest that their benefits may not persist across versions, which motivates a workflow-level approach in which agents build on one another's work across sessions. We model these alternating agent sessions as a context-reset semi-Markov decision process (CR-SMDP) and establish sufficient conditions for alternation to exceed single-agent reference limits, derive an explicit experiment-budget bound, and characterize when session caps preserve this advantage. Guided by this analysis, we introduce Humanize MLE Agents (HMA), which alternates two agents on a shared workspace, limits each session to at most k experiments and resets the context between sessions, without additional task-specific harness or prior knowledge supplements. Across 75 Kaggle tasks in MLE-bench, HMA reaches a state-of-the-art any-medal rate of 78.2%, exceeding the strongest open-source baseline by 8.0 points with a quarter of its time budget. Moreover, among six configurations spanning five heterogeneous agent pairs, HMA improves any-medal rate over the constituent baselines by 6.4 points on average, demonstrating cross-pair generality. A supplementary case on kernel optimization reaches 878 cycles, within 1.6% of the community leaderboard leader, demonstrating applicability beyond MLE.

papers.title: Hierarchical Graph Neural Network for Probabilistic Power Flow with Grid Topology Contingencies
papers.abstract: Data-driven surrogates reduce the nonlinear solves required for probabilistic power flow (PPF), but models tied to a fixed bus--branch graph often generalize poorly when outages change electrical coupling. This paper proposes a topology-decomposition-driven hierarchical bidirectional graph neural network (TDD--HBGNN) for PPF under unseen topologies. For each realized topology, the network is decomposed into fundamental topological units (FTUs), dynamically homogeneous voltage clusters (DHVCs), and a core backbone sub-grid (CBSG), with equivalent-admittance representations preserving electrical ports between units. A sensitivity-based linear prior captures the first-order voltage-magnitude and phase-angle response, while the HBGNN learns topology-dependent nonlinear residuals. Impedance- and uncertainty-aware bottom-up aggregation condenses local perturbations, while mode-modulated top-down broadcasting restores system context at buses. We evaluate our approach on the IEEE 118-bus and Polish 2746-bus systems under unseen N--1 and N--2 contingencies against six baseline methods. Compared with these methods, TDD--HBGNN achieves 2.47--4.20-fold lower all-bus phase-angle errors and lower phase-angle errors in every held-out event. Its voltage-magnitude advantage is concentrated near the outaged branches, where paired error ratios reach 1.75--2.58 on the IEEE system and 1.87--1.97 in Polish N--2 events. All system--contingency--baseline comparisons favor TDD--HBGNN in joint voltage--angle error. Moreover, shared hierarchical operators keep the model size at 0.658 million parameters across both grids and yield 0.161--1.793~ms forward latency per probabilistic case. These results demonstrate system-wide angular accuracy, outage-local voltage accuracy, and parameter-efficient scaling across unseen topologies.

papers.title: A new device for live cell imaging of biological samples under in-plane shear
papers.abstract: The effect of mechanical stresses and deformations upon the behavior and properties of cells and tissues is a topic of paramount interest in the field of biophysics. Its understanding is essential for deepening our comprehension of cellular responses to environmental stimuli, with implications in fields ranging from embryogenesis to tumor development. For boosting the understanding in this field, it is important to develop devices for the application of simple deformations in order to probe the cellular response to the basic mechanical transformations. While a number of stretching devices have been developed, in-plane shearing deformation has been little investigated. Here, a new device is introduced that allows the application of homogeneous in-plane shear upon a cell monolayer while imaging the sample with a commercial optical microscope. A description of the faced experimental challenges is reported and a full characterization is presented. It is demonstrated the capability of the device to apply reproducible, controlled and homogeneous shear of both single cells and confluent cellular monolayers.

papers.title: Blocking of bistable front propagation: Application to Wolbachia population replacement
