papers.abstract: In order to control epidemics of mosquito-borne diseases such as dengue, for which there is still no vaccine available, several strategies aim to directly target the mosquito population. One technique involves introducing a symbiotic bacterium called Wolbachia into the population, which blocks the transmission of pathogens. A mathematical model of the introduction of this bacterium and the replacement of the mosquito population with a population carrying this bacterium has been developed, proving that in a homogeneous environment, there is spatial propagation of the replacement. The objective of this paper is to study the blocking of this propagation in cases where the environment is not homogeneous. In particular, we are considering scenarios where the environmental carrying capacity varies significantly across different regions of the spatial domain. To achieve this objective, we first reduce the original 2x2 reaction-diffusion system to a single closed equation, providing a simplified framework for studying the dynamics of Wolbachia propagation. We then investigate the blocking of the propagation in the population replacement process, focusing on the effects of spatial variations in the environmental carrying capacity. Numerical simulations have been performed to validate the theoretical results.

papers.title: A Hybrid and Hierarchical Ray Tracing Method for Efficient 3D Gaussian Rendering
papers.abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) is a powerful representation for real-time neural reconstruction and rendering. While existing 3DGS systems rely on rasterization for efficiency, recent work explores ray tracing to enable secondary lighting, highly distorted cameras, and depth-of-field effects. However, compared with rasterization, ray-traced 3DGS introduces three major challenges: (1) the highly non-uniform spatial distribution of massive numbers of Gaussian primitives creates severe load imbalance; (2) neighboring pixels often generate rays with highly similar traversal paths, leading to substantial redundant traversal overhead; and (3) supporting both Gaussian and triangle primitives yields heterogeneous intersection workloads that are not well matched to existing GPU architectures. We present H2-Ray, a hybrid and hierarchical ray tracing architecture for efficient 3D Gaussian rendering. H2-Ray introduces three techniques. Load-Balanced Spatial BVH (LB-SBVH) partitions the scene into uniform grids and uses density-aware representations to convert an imbalanced global workload into balanced local traversal units. Ray-Cluster Path Reuse (RCPR) lets a proxy ray share traversal state with neighboring rays to amortize redundant traversal. The Unified Intersection Engine (UIE) supports mixed Gaussian and triangle intersections through a mode-multiplexed datapath that shares 40% of its floating-point units across both primitive types. Across 8 scenes, H2-Ray achieves a geometric-mean speedup of 3.77x and a maximum speedup of 9.26x over RaySplats on the NVIDIA RTX A5000, combining a cycle-accurate model of the modified RT Core with measured CUDA timings.

papers.title: The effects of non-stoichiometric lattice structure and secondary phase α-Fe2O3 on modifying the magnetic, electrical, and magneto-electric properties of Eu doped BaFe12O19 hexaferrite
papers.abstract: The Ba-atoms in BaFe12O19 were substituted by Eu-atoms to prepare the material of composition Ba1-xEuyFe12O19. The Eu atoms occupied at the sites of Fe atoms. The atomic ratio of Eu/Ba were varied from 0 to 0.33 to control the secondary phase (hematite) and M-type hexaferrite. Raman spectra provided complimentary support for a systematic increase of the hematite phase on increasing the Eu/Ba ratio. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy informed the presence of oxygen deficiency and surface defects, and charge state of Ba and Fe/Eu ions close to +2 and +3, respectively. The material showed direct optical transitions with band gap in the range of 2.25-3.09 eV. The increase of Eu/Ba ratio systematically increased the saturation magnetization from 84.44 emu g-1 to 57.68 emu g-1 at 3 K and 67.09 emu g-1 to 43.42 emu g-1 at 300 K, along with remarkable enhancement of the coercivity (914- 3656 Oe at 3 K and 1996-4862 Oe at 300 K). Electrical conductivity increased from 10-11-10-10 Sm-1 at 30 K to 10-5 -10-4 Sm-1 at 300 K. The electrical conductivity analysis reveals the Efros-Shklovsky-type variable-range hopping mechanism at the low-temperature region, whereas the Mott variable range hopping mechanism is applicable near to room temperature. The analysis of current-voltage characteristics provided electrode to sample interfacial barrier height of 0.27-0.74 eV. The material exhibited novel magneto-electronic properties (bi-stable electronic switching and its transformation in the temperature scale, magnetoresistance and magnetoelectric coupling) which are highly useful for spintronic devices. This work demonstrates that controlled Eu/Ba atomic ratio in the stoichiometric and non-stoichiometric lattice structure could be an effective strategy to widely tune the magnetic, optical and magneto-electronic properties in M-type Ba hexaferrite material.

papers.title: Phonology-Aware Speaker Extraction Frontend for Audio LLMs
papers.abstract: Target speaker extraction (TSE) is a key frontend for enabling audio large language models (LLMs) to recognize and understand a designated speaker in overlapping speech. However, multilingual mixtures exhibit heterogeneous extraction demands, causing fixed-depth systems to either under-process challenging inputs or waste computation on inputs that have already converged. Existing TSE frontends generally apply uniform computation, while Audio-LLM adaptation methods neither explicitly model language-conditioned extraction demands nor preserve plug-and-play compatibility with frozen downstream models. We therefore propose LATTE, a lightweight 5.2M-parameter frontend that combines an acoustic Difficulty Estimator, a task-adaptive phonology-informed prior learned from multi-depth TSE gains, and an Adaptive Hourglass Extractor to route each mixture without requiring language identity at inference. On PolyExtract, LATTE achieves a macro SI-SNRi of 15.07 dB at 0.30 GFLOPs, retaining performance within 0.09 dB of a 0.53-GFLOP fixed-depth model while reducing computation by 43.4%, and lowers the average WER from 16.8% to 14.6% relative to TF-GridNet. By jointly modeling sample-level extraction demands and phonological structure, LATTE provides a practical framework for quality-aware, compute-efficient multilingual TSE and offers a scalable path toward robust Audio-LLM deployment.

papers.title: Integrable auxiliary field sigma model and the metric approach to $T\bar{T}$-like deformations
papers.abstract: We describe a family of two-dimensional metric deformations that preserve integrability. The seeds are (classically) conformal integrable field theories and the deformations are directly related to different classes of auxiliary field sigma models. We introduce a master action connecting deformations by Lie-algebra-valued auxiliary fields, the so-called $ν$-frame, to deformations by two Lorentz-charged scalars. These auxiliary scalar fields can be identified as Beltrami differentials of an auxiliary two-dimensional metric, providing a direct connection with the metric approach to $T\bar{T}$-like deformations. For Weyl-invariant seed matter theories, the auxiliary metric sector is described by a reduced gravitational potential. We show that the resulting framework preserves classical Lax integrability whenever the seed matter theory admits a Lax representation of its equations of motion on a generic curved two-dimensional spacetime. Finally, within the Lorentz-invariant family and the zweibein deformations of conformal matter theories considered here, we identify $T\bar{T}$ as the only deformation that can be interpreted as a field-dependent coordinate transformation.

papers.title: Stride: Scale-Aware Multi-Agent Evolutionary Refinement for Infographic Generation
papers.abstract: Infographic generation challenges text-to-image models because a single image must satisfy numerous visual, textual, and semantic constraints. Iterative agentic refinement with a multimodal verifier is a natural remedy, but existing methods face a scale mismatch: local edits cannot correct global composition errors, while full regeneration may destroy already-correct regions. We introduce Stride, a constraint-grounded multi-agent framework that treats refinement over any frozen generator as a history-aware evolution strategy. Stride separates constraint evaluation - whether each requirement is satisfied - from visual grounding - where and how it is violated. It then routes global revisions to a composer subagent and local corrections to a retoucher subagent. Each subagent conducts internal planning and generates multiple candidates, while Stride accepts a candidate only when it improves the verifier score, reducing regression across iterations. Because stochastic generators and imperfect verifiers make any single step unreliable, it is this combination of scale-aware routing, per-step redundancy, and monotonic acceptance that yields stable improvement across iterations. With fully open-weight generator-verifier systems, Stride outperforms proprietary systems including Nano-Banana-2.0 and Seedream-5.0-Pro on BizGenEval, matches GPT-Image-2.0 and surpasses Seedream-5.0-Pro on IGenBench, and achieves a new state-of-the-art score on WISE, while substantially outperforming existing agentic methods across all evaluated benchmarks.

papers.title: SplatQ: Interaction-Aware Pruning of 3D Gaussian Splatting via Quadratic Selection
papers.abstract: Existing 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) pruning methods primarily rely on global Top-K selection based on independent importance scores, lacking regional budget control and ignoring joint deletion effects. Consequently, they cannot ensure balanced reconstruction quality across a scene. We propose SplatQ, a combinatorial pruning algorithm that coordinates regional budget allocation and joint Gaussian selection under a fixed budget. SplatQ partitions Gaussians by spatial proximity and appearance similarity into size-limited blocks, decomposing global selection into subproblems of a specific size. It then smooths importance-based block retention quotas to prevent excessive budget concentration. Finally, it constructs a quadratic approximation of joint deletion effects using the responses of representative pixel colors to changes in Gaussian opacity. Individual responses, pairwise interactions, and quota penalties are incorporated into a quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) objective, solved using simulated annealing (SA) or a coherent Ising machine (CIM) to jointly select Gaussians. Experiments on 5 benchmarks demonstrate that SplatQ outperforms state-of-the-art pruning methods in aggregate reconstruction quality, spatial quality balance, and rendering speed. Ablations confirm that budget smoothing improves local detail reconstruction, while interaction modeling improves Gaussian selection quality under a fixed budget.

papers.title: Beyond Temporal Proximity: Explanatory World Models for Credit Assignment in Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Generative Recommenders increasingly use Reinforcement Learning (RL) to optimize outcomes that may appear hundreds or thousands of interactions after a decision. Standard RL propagates reward according to temporal proximity rather than explicit relevance, attenuating the signal assigned to distant but important actions and creating a source of sample inefficiency. We introduce Explanatory World Models (EWM), an attribution framework that uses explanations to identify the earlier events that plausibly contributed to a realized outcome. We instantiate EWM with a frontier language model and use its explanations as learning signals using a conservative hierarchical operator that recursively redistributes reward while preserving the undiscounted episode return. To investigate what constitutes a useful explanation, we operationalize three complementary variants inspired by Halpern's actual causation, Lombrozo's explanatory simplicity, and Deutsch's hard-to-vary explanations. We evaluate EWM on two controlled long-horizon RL benchmarks, a public sequential-recommendation benchmark, and an industry-scale generative recommender. On Crafter and WordCraft, EWM substantially outperforms PPO and LaRe, with its largest gains when rewards are most delayed. On KuaiRand, EWM outperforms SFT and LaRe offline and A2C online. Finally, in an offline evaluation of an industry generative recommender, EWM considerably improves Recall and increases behavioral proxies. These results suggest that explanations can provide structured and reusable credit for learning from delayed outcomes.

papers.title: Graph-theoretic framework for semi-Markov networks: transient and stationary occupation probabilities, hitting times and weak ergodicity breaking
papers.abstract: We show that finite semi-Markov networks admit explicit combinatorial representations of their Laplace-transformed occupation probabilities and hitting-time distributions as sums over weighted spanning trees and forests of an augmented graph, generalizing the previously developed graph-theoretic framework for Markov networks. These representations yield asymptotic results, including the long-time scaling of hitting-time survival probabilities in the presence of infinite-mean sojourn times. They also extend recently derived combinatorial formulas for hitting-time moments to the semi-Markov setting, where non-Markovian corrections appear in higher moments. For finite-mean sojourn times, the framework recovers the known stationary distribution through a generalization of the Markov Chain Tree Theorem, with transition rates replaced by pseudo-rates. In particular, the mean hitting-time formula coincides with that of a Markov network with the corresponding pseudo-rates, which also yields a short graph-theoretic proof of the previously established constancy of Kemeny's constant for finite-mean semi-Markov networks. Finally, we use the same framework to extend established results on weak ergodicity breaking for time-additive state observables that are nonconstant on the support of the limiting distribution in heavy-tailed semi-Markov networks, allowing for generally heterogeneous, transition-dependent waiting-time distributions.

papers.title: Lossless Inference Acceleration for ASR via EAGLE-Style Speculative Decoding
papers.abstract: Autoregressive Transformer and Conformer models have achieved state-of-the-art performance in automatic speech recognition (ASR). However, their sequential token generation mechanism imposes a significant bottleneck during decoding, resulting in substantial inference latency. While speculative decoding has emerged as a promising lossless acceleration technique, existing ASR-oriented approaches either suffer from low draft acceptance rates due to suboptimal draft quality or rely on specially designed external draft models, which limit their generality and practicality. To overcome these limitations, we propose EAGLE-ASR, a novel framework that accelerates ASR inference via EAGLE-style speculative decoding while strictly preserving lossless output quality. Specifically, we introduce Speech-Draft, a lightweight autoregressive module that serves as a universal draft model by jointly leveraging encoder acoustic features and hierarchical decoder representations from the target ASR model. Furthermore, we adopt a multi-step generation strategy with self-distilled data to train the Speech-Draft, enabling it to better approximate the target model's output distribution and maintain causal consistency during multi-token generation. Extensive experiments on representative Whisper and Conformer AED models demonstrate that EAGLE-ASR achieves significant lossless speedups of up to $1.9\times$ and $2.4\times$, respectively, consistently outperforming existing speculative decoding baselines for ASR. Our proposed framework further generalizes effectively to multilingual ASR and speech translation tasks, establishing EAGLE-ASR as a practical and universally applicable solution for accelerating modern ASR systems without compromising recognition accuracy.

papers.title: Compactly supported instability of Riemannian Schwarzschild--Tangherlini metrics
papers.abstract: On the Riemannian Schwarzschild--Tangherlini metric of dimension $n\geq 4$, we show that the destabilizing TT tensor of Ozuch lies in the image of the ``TT-tensor machine''. By continuity, it can then be approximated, in suitable weighted Sobolev spaces, by smooth compactly supported TT tensors, on which the stability quadratic form is still negative. This proves instability in the usual sense for noncompact manifolds. To our knowledge, no exact smooth compactly supported destabilizing TT tensor was known before, even in 4D.

papers.title: FedPCD: Priority-Constrained Federated Aggregation
papers.abstract: Federated learning (FL) seeks to optimize a shared global model from decentralized client data. While effective for average performance, this process can produce unfair performance across clients, particularly under statistically heterogeneous data distributions. Existing fairness-aware and multi-objective FL methods address this through client re-weighting, gradient correction, or common-descent formulations, but often change the global optimization direction or treat client objectives symmetrically. We propose FedPCD, a priority-constrained federated optimization framework that separates the global optimization objective from client protection. FedPCD preserves the conventional federated aggregate as the primary objective, while allowing only the minimum correction necessary to meet client performance constraints. Across heterogeneous FL benchmarks, FedPCD consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, achieving the highest global accuracy across all configurations and leading worst-10% client accuracy in nearly all. FedPCD further preserves competitive trade-offs between global accuracy and client performance variability. Beyond this trade-off, FedPCD demonstrates faster empirical convergence, reaching matching or superior performance in substantially fewer communication rounds.

papers.title: Energy-dependent trapping of backscattered helium during magnetron sputtering growth: A molecular dynamics study
papers.abstract: Helium incorporation during magnetron sputtering can strongly affect thin film growth and lead to the formation of gas/solid nanocomposites and nanoporous structures. Here, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations are used to investigate the trapping mechanism of helium atoms (He) and the subsequent formation of He bubbles during the sputter deposition of aluminum (Al) and titanium (Ti) thin films. The simulations account for the kinetic energy distributions of sputtered metal atoms and backscattered gas species. Results indicate that He is efficiently incorporated into the growing films, leading to the formation of high-pressure, dense He bubbles, with a much higher He-to-metal atomic ratio in Ti ($\sim$ 60%) than in Al ($\sim$ 12%). More importantly, the simulations reveal a clear energy dependence of He trapping in Ti: background He atoms at thermal energies are essentially not incorporated, whereas efficient trapping starts at an incident energy of approximately 20 eV and increases up to a saturation regime near 100 eV. Simulated thermal desorption spectroscopy (TDS) further reveals distinct release mechanisms in the two investigated metals: He desorption from Al occurs at higher temperatures and is preceded by the removal of surface Al atoms, whereas He and Ti atom desorption starts continuously around 950 K, leading to a porous structure. Comparative simulations with argon (Ar) demonstrate negligible trapping even at comparable kinetic energy or momentum, showing that neither parameter alone accounts for the strong He incorporation observed in Ti. The above results are in very good agreement with what is reported in literature for low-kinetic energy He ion implantation in metal surfaces, suggesting similar insertion mechanisms. They clarify the atomistic conditions governing noble gas trapping during film growth and provide a basis for controlling He incorporation and porosity in films synthesized by magnetron sputtering.

papers.title: Retrieval-Augmented Multimodal Language Model with Heterogeneous Evidence Integration for Clinical Prognosis
papers.abstract: Clinical prognosis requires integrating structured measurements, physiological waveforms, longitudinal history, and population context. We introduce PRISM (Population-Retrieved Inference for Structured Multimodal Prognosis), a multimodal language model that combines per-feature numerical tokenization, recency-weighted aggregation of longitudinal ECGs, and a dual-modality population memory bank. Retrieval operates in representation space: the model receives mean-pooled embeddings of similar training-cohort encounters, while no individual retrieved record enters the prompt. On the 1,443-task MDS-ED benchmark, PRISM achieves AUROCs of 86.2% for diagnosis, 93.1% for deterioration, 91.8% for ICU admission, and 92.8% for mortality. These results use a 96-hour pre-arrival window unavailable to reported baselines. With benchmark-window inputs only, PRISM reaches 0.8895 AUROC, compared with 0.8937 for UniPACT and 0.8889 for MDS-ED. A matched-input compact fusion model using the same five evidence streams and frozen encoders reaches 0.7652 AUROC, versus 0.9092 for PRISM. Replacing numerical EHR encoding with text serialization reduces AUROC by 3.66 points; removing pre-arrival history reduces it by 1.97 points; and zeroing retrieval reduces it by 0.99 points. Genuine retrieval outperforms random-neighbor retrieval by 0.97 macro-average points, although a paired task-level sign test does not establish a uniform advantage (p=0.067). On the external MC-MED cohort, supervised fine-tuning reaches 0.8611 AUROC, compared with 0.8227 for locally trained gradient boosting and 0.7841 for source-only PRISM. These results support structure-aware multimodal integration and supervised external adaptation.

papers.title: Finite Quantum Engineering Thermodynamics
papers.abstract: A useful thermodynamic model predicts what a device will do without tracking its full microscopic state. For a finite quantum working medium, the difficult question is which quantities should actually be measured. We develop a task-based method that keeps exact energy accounting separate from calibrated macroscopic prediction. Operator geometry identifies what a measured record determines and bounds what remains uncertain. We then compare direct measurements of dynamical observables with earlier measurements of the same coarse record, selecting the representation together with its measurement cost. A Bose--Hubbard example yields a compact response table tested over a continuous operating region and on unseen microscopic trajectories. A driven Ising chain shows why history is not always the cheaper choice. The result is a way to turn detailed quantum dynamics into a small, reusable, and explicitly qualified thermodynamic description.

papers.title: Construction of isoscattering non-isospectral quantum graphs using the concept of a germ graph
papers.abstract: The recently developed concept of germ graphs (P. Kurasov {\it et al.}, Phys. Rev. Research {\bf 7}, L022071 (2025)) is employed to construct families of isocattering, non-isospectral graphs that exhibit dissipation. More specifically, a new pair of isoscattering non-isospectral graphs is constructed by connecting the existing isoscattering non-isospectral graphs, so called attachments, to the different contact vertices of the germ graph. The existing isoscattering non-isospectral graphs contained a two-loop graph labelled $Γ_{A2}$ and a three-loop graph labelled $Γ_{A3}$. These graphs have an equal total metric length, but different topologies. The resulting graphs $Γ_3$ and $Γ_4$ are verified as non-isospectral using their Euler characteristics, while their isoscattering properties are investigated by calculating the one-port scattering matrices numerically.

papers.title: Short scale asymptotics in nonlocal spectral problems
papers.abstract: We study the asymptotic behavior of eigenvalues of nonlocal convolution-type operators $$L_\varepsilonρ=-\frac{1}{\varepsilon^{d}}\int_ΩJ\left({\frac{|x-y|^2}{\varepsilon^2}}\right)ρ(y)dy+a(x)ρ(x),$$ (with a continuous sufficiently fast decaying at infinity function $J\geq 0$) when the scaling parameter $\varepsilon>0$ tends to zero. Assuming that the minimum of the function $a(x)$ is attained at a point $x_0\in \overlineΩ\subset \mathbb{R}^d$ and is non-degenerate, we establish several terms in the asymptotic expansion of the first eigenvalues $λ_\varepsilon^{(k)}$ of $L_\varepsilon$. If $x_0$ is an interior point of the domain $Ω$, we show that $λ_\varepsilon^{(k)}=a(x_0)-1+\varepsilonμ^{(k)}+\overline{o}(\varepsilon)$, where $μ^{(k)}$ are eigenvalues of a harmonic oscillator (obtained by the blow up analysis), the corresponding eigenfunctions of $\mathcal{L}_\varepsilon$ are concentrated near $x_0$ on the scale $\varepsilon^{1/2}$. If $x_0\in\partial Ω$ then the asymptotic expansion of the eigenvalues of $L_\varepsilon$ has the form $λ_\varepsilon^{(k)}=a(x_0)-1+\varepsilon^{2/3}Λ_0+\varepsilon(μ^{(k)}+αp_0)+\overline{o}(\varepsilon)$. The corresponding eigenfunctions are represented as the product of a function depending on the distance to $\partialΩ$ and concentrated on the scale $\varepsilon^{2/3}$, and functions localized on the scale $\varepsilon^{1/2}$ and asymptotically independent of the distance to $\partialΩ$. The latter functions converge (after rescaling) to eigenfunctions of a harmonic oscillator (in tangential variables), $μ^{(k)}$ being their eigenvalues. The former function is given, to the leading term, by the scaled Airy function, and $Λ_0$, $α$ and $p_0$ depend on $J(|x|^2)$ and $a(x)$.

papers.title: The School on Gravity: from motion to commotion
papers.abstract: Understanding the gravitational interaction is one of the great scientific endeavors of the 21st century. The Nobel Prize-winning discovery of gravitational waves in 2015, and subsequent detections by the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA Collaboration, have marked a revolutionary step forward in physics and astrophysics by opening an entirely new window for exploring the Universe. Future upgrades to these detectors, along with upcoming facilities such as LISA, the Einstein Telescope, and radio and optical instruments, promise other breakthrough discoveries that the next generation of scientists will need to interpret. The School on Gravity (22--26 June 2026, Copenhagen) aimed to introduce junior scientists--graduate students and advanced undergraduates with a background in general relativity--to a wide range of foundational topics in the exciting new field of gravitational-wave physics. Topics spanned from the theory of motion, to new challenges introduced by quantum physics, to the astrophysics of black holes and source modeling for gravitational-wave detectors. The School on Gravity took place at the legendary Auditorium A of the Niels Bohr Institute, inviting students and lecturers to challenge current paradigms in gravitational physics in the spirit of the quantum revolution that unfolded in this very room. These lecture notes aim at opening up those new ideas presented in Auditorium A to the rest of the scientific community.

papers.title: On the weak invariance principle for strictly stationary sequences in some Besov spaces
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the weak invariance principle in some Besov spaces for strictly stationary sequences. In particular, we provide sufficient conditions on the moments and the dependence of a strictly stationary sequence to guaranty the weak invariance principle in these Besov spaces. Several dependence structures are considered, including projective conditions, $α$-dependent, $ρ$-mixing, and $τ$ -dependent conditions. The main tools in the proofs are martingale approximation and deviation inequalities for weakly dependent sequences. Our results cover a large range of strictly stationary sequences that were not treated previously in the literature. Moreover, the presented conditions are sharp.

papers.title: RESCUE: Is This Alarm Worth Acting On? Counterfactual Evaluation of VLA Runtime Monitors
papers.abstract: Runtime failure monitors for robot policies are typically evaluated by how accurately they distinguish failed from successful executions. Yet an accurate alarm may arrive too late for recovery, while an unnecessary intervention may disrupt an execution that would otherwise succeed. We introduce RESCUE, a counterfactual framework for evaluating whether a monitor's alarms enable useful interventions. By restoring simulator and policy states at execution checkpoints, RESCUE compares alternative actions, identifies the latest checkpoint satisfying a specified recovery criterion, and evaluates whether acting on alarms reduces expected task-completion cost. We evaluate RESCUE with OpenVLA-OFT and $π_{0.5}$ over LIBERO-Spatial and LIBERO-Plus using 128,340 counterfactual branches. Recoverability depends on the state--intervention pair rather than on robot state alone: at $τ=0.5$, 14 of 66 OpenVLA-OFT/LIBERO-Plus failures contain a recoverable checkpoint under continuation, compared with 34 of 66 under continuation or scripted recovery, while recovery reduces recoverability in other conditions. On the primary strong-policy conditions, favourable detection scores do not establish lower intervention cost. Under the evaluated stop-and-reset model, even an idealised detector can afford only a 2.0--3.3% false-alarm rate before unnecessary resets outweigh the savings from stopping failures early. These results show that monitor value depends jointly on the intervention available and the workload in which it is deployed.

papers.title: The Hydrological Cycle and Circulation of Tidally-Locked Planets with a Finite Moisture Inventory
papers.abstract: Tidally-locked planets express a range of climate regimes distinct from those found in our solar system. Their atmospheres are often dominated by planetary-wide overturning circulations and super- rotating jets. In this paper we explore the hydrological cycle of such planets and how it might depend on the total inventory of condensate. To this end we use a set of idealised GCM simulations to probe the response of the hydrological cycle to the surface moisture budget in their atmospheres. We find that for low moisture inventories the climate quickly develops a barren day side and a moist night side where the moisture is trapped, as might be expected. For higher moisture inventories the drying of the day side is significantly delayed by the development of a substellar lake just east of the substellar point, which is sustained by the presence of a local thunderstorm-like convective system that persists even after the lake disappears. The timescales for the lake to disappear are millennia, suggesting that even a weak transfer of moisture through surface processes could maintain a moist day side. We also find that adjusting the threshold at which the evaporative rate becomes constrained by the remaining surface liquid depth modifies the longevity of the lake and surrounding day side conditions. These findings have implications for understanding a diverse range of planetary climates and habitability, given the distribution of moisture and presence of a substellar lake.

papers.title: Asymptotic Analysis of Discrete-Time Self-Attention Dynamics in Transformers
papers.abstract: In machine learning, a self-attention dynamics describes the attention mechanism of transformers, and is obtained treating the layer index of a transformer as time index. Even though naturally discrete-time, this dynamical system is most often studied in continuous-time. Scope of this paper is to provide a thorough investigation of the discrete-time version of the self-attention dynamics: a complete classification of its equilibria is given, and their stability properties are studied, in both the single-head and the multihead case. We show that in both cases the main attractor of the dynamics is a consensus equilibrium aligned with the principal eigenvector of the value matrix (in the single-head case, a corresponding matrix of weights in the multihead case), even though other locally asymptotically stable bipartite equilibria can be show to exist at least in the single-head situation. The behavior is confirmed by looking at the learned weight matrices of a real transformer.

papers.title: TrustPaper for forged PDF with Issuer Fingerprints
papers.abstract: Sick leave certificates are increasingly delivered as PDF files by online teleconsultation platforms, and can be altered in minutes with free editors. Generic PDF scanners report how a file was built, but cannot tell whether that construction is legitimate: an incremental update, an embedded font or a given producer string is normal for one issuer and anomalous for another. We present TrustPaper solution, an issuer aware forensic approach that combines three elements: the claimed issuer of the document, a reference fingerprint learned beforehand from genuine documents of that issuer, and an explainable combination of evidence from several forensic modules. Fingerprints are stored as versioned declarative profiles, and every anomaly keeps its observed value, expected value and triggering rule. We formalize the threat model, the fingerprint and the scoring model, and evaluate the open-source prototype on a controlled corpus documents from two issuers and six forgery techniques. With the issuer fingerprint, all forgeries made by opportunistic and metadata-aware attackers are flagged with no false positive on genuine test documents.

papers.title: A Stochastic Analysis Perspective on Diffusion Models
papers.abstract: Generative modelling involves two complementary tasks: learning a probabilistic approximation of an unknown data distribution from observations, and designing a tractable mechanism for sampling from this approximation. We present a stochastic-analysis perspective on score-based generative models, connecting ideas from classical sampling theory, score estimation, and diffusion time reversal. We first explain how score functions link Langevin sampling with score matching, and how Gaussian smoothing leads to denoising score matching and multiscale sampling methods. We then emphasize the distinction between dynamics preserving a fixed distribution and dynamics transporting a prescribed family of marginals. This motivates a path-space treatment of diffusion time reversal. Finally, we connect the ideal reverse diffusion with practical generative algorithms.

papers.title: Latin squares as a model of perfect mixing of high-entropy alloys
papers.abstract: The structure of high-entropy alloys, which include 5 or more components in equimolar proportions, is proposed to be described in the mathematical language of Latin squares. This model is fundamentally discrete and allows for a quantitative description of ideal mixing, in which any given alloy element is guaranteed not to have an identical element as its nearest neighbor. For the two-dimensional case, the model possesses four axes of translational symmetry, which makes it possible to tile the plane with a single Latin square and, based on the properties of this square, describe the properties of macroscopic material samples. The model makes it possible to make quantitative estimates of the suitability of a particular atomic structure (configuration) for implementation in a perfectly mixed high-entropy alloy with maximum mixing entropy. A condition has been obtained for acceptable fluctuations in the concentration of components at which the thermodynamic stability of the alloy is maintained. The possibility of identifying superstructures in high-entropy alloys based on group theory, as applied to the description and construction of Latin squares, is discussed. Based on the proposed model, the probability of forming a multicomponent alloy with ideal mixing is estimated. For a five-component alloy, this probability is no more than 2.6*10^{-10}.

papers.title: Causal Effect Identifiability in Causal Abstractions: A Strict Hierarchy of Criteria
papers.abstract: Identifying causal effects from observational data typically requires a fully specified causal graph, an assumption that is often unrealistic in complex or high-dimensional settings. Causal abstractions address this limitation by retaining only partial causal information, thereby defining equivalence classes of compatible causal graphs. In this paper, we study causal effect identifiability directly at the level of these graph collections, rather than at the level of individual causal diagrams. We formalize several notions of identifiability in this setting and organize them into a hierarchy that clarifies their relationships and differences. In particular, we establish that a causal effect may be identified over a collection of graphs without admitting a single causal derivation that holds uniformly across all compatible graphs. These results help reveal gaps and clarify ambiguities in the existing literature.

papers.title: Beyond Domain-Routed Supervision: Cross-Teacher Guarding for Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation
papers.abstract: Multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD) extends on-policy distillation (OPD) by routing domain-specific data to specialized teachers, integrating their capabilities through dense token-level supervision on student-generated trajectories. However, domain routing only distinguishes the supervision sources for different domains; updates from all domains still act on shared parameters. When teachers differ substantially in response style and domain expertise, supervision that is effective in isolation may still lead to persistent gradient conflicts and capability degradation during joint optimization. To address this challenge, we propose Cross-Teacher Guarding for MOPD (Road MOPD), which introduces non-routed teachers as auxiliary cross-domain critics on the same student trajectories and coordinates multi-teacher supervision through token-level credit assignment and gradient updates. Specifically, cross-teacher-guided credit assignment uses teacher agreement to strengthen token-level corrections jointly supported by the teachers and attenuate conflicting signals; preventive multi-teacher gradient projection uses auxiliary gradients from the same trajectories to constrain potentially conflicting updates and adaptively controls projection strength to retain target-domain learning signals. In experiments, Road MOPD mitigates degradation in the disadvantaged domain, gains over 5 percentage points under high conflict, and improves overall performance in low-conflict and three-domain settings.

papers.title: Exploring Representation Autoencoders for Text-to-Audio Generation
papers.abstract: Representation autoencoders (RAE), created by pairing a frozen pretrained self-supervised learning (SSL) encoder with a trained decoder, have recently demonstrated state-of-the-art performance on image generation. Their use in the audio domain, however, remains limited: text-to-audio (TTA) models are typically trained in the latent space of dedicated autoencoders where the encoder and the decoder are trained jointly with reconstruction objectives. This paper presents a study on audio representation autoencoders (AuRA) and their applicability to general audio TTA. We train decoders for two pretrained SSL audio encoders and evaluate their reconstruction quality against autoencoders used by recent TTA systems. After obtaining decoders for the SSL representations, we also train rectified flow models in the SSL and baseline latent spaces to isolate the autoencoder's effect on generation. We find that generation in SSL spaces achieves comparable or superior performance to generation in the baseline spaces, despite differences in reconstruction performance. These results highlight that reconstruction quality alone is not a sufficient proxy for generative performance.

papers.title: Beyond Successful Robot Demonstrations: Learning from Human Interactions and Modeling Failure Dynamics
papers.abstract: Action-conditioned world models offer a promising foundation for generalist robotic intelligence by predicting the consequences of actions. However, existing robotic datasets provide limited coverage of the diverse interaction dynamics required for generalizable world modeling. Large-scale egocentric human videos offer complementary interaction experience, yet the embodiment gap between human hands and robotic manipulators hinders effective cross-embodiment learning. Meanwhile, the predominance of successful demonstrations leaves failure dynamics substantially underrepresented, limiting the ability of world models to anticipate unsuccessful executions. To address these limitations, we introduce HF-WM, an action-conditioned world model that combines Human interaction learning with Failure-aware post-training. To bridge the embodiment gap, we develop a dual-branch framework that couples video generation with auxiliary pointflow prediction, using stabilized pointflow as a unified motion representation across human and robot interactions while suppressing egocentric camera motion. To improve failure modeling, we further perform Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) post-training on perturbed actions derived from successful demonstrations, guided by action alignment and physical plausibility rewards, enabling the model to learn plausible failure dynamics without paired ground-truth videos. Extensive experiments demonstrate that HF-WM achieves state-of-the-art performance in action-conditioned video generation and exhibits strong utility for policy evaluation in downstream robotic tasks.

papers.title: How Fluctuations Control Chiral Symmetry Breaking in Reacting Mixtures of Chiral Molecules
papers.abstract: The pronounced chiral asymmetry of biomolecules is a defining feature of living systems, yet the mechanisms by which such asymmetry emerged remain unresolved. Chiral symmetry breaking may have occurred under prebiotic conditions in systems with sufficiently small molecular populations for intrinsic fluctuations to play an important role. Here, we investigate how finite-population fluctuations affect chiral-state selection, the characteristic time for symmetry breaking, and stochastic switching between chiral states in a system driven by autocatalysis and mutual antagonism. We determine how these dynamical processes scale with particle number and derive an analytical expression for the probability of selecting either chiral state as a function of the initial enantiomeric bias. We further calculate the mean selection time for different initial biases and show that, for weak mutual antagonism, fluctuations can induce transitions between opposite chiral states. These results characterize how finite-population fluctuations control both the emergence and stability of molecular chirality in autocatalytic chemical systems.

papers.title: A Machine Learning Approach to Finslerian Cosmological Dark Energy Model
papers.abstract: Modified extensions of the standard cosmological models often introduce complex parameter degeneracies that severely impact sampling convergence of the parameter space while analyzing the model observationally. In this work, we present an accelerated Bayesian inference technique using a Heteroscedastic Deep Ensemble with Monte Carlo Dropout incorporating distance-gated local residual corrections to emulate complex likelihood surfaces and avoid extrapolation beyond the trained region. We demonstrate this methodology on a unified dark energy cosmological model equipped with Finsler geometry. The model is studied using the recent observational datasets, including Cosmic Chronometers (CC), Pantheon$+$SH$0$ES, and DESI DR$2$ BAO measurements. While the conventional sampling procedure struggles with slow mixing of parameter chains ($τ_{max}=1578.3$), the neural network, specially trained densely in high likelihood regions, yields converged and highly resolved posterior distributions of the model parameters without significantly compromising the minimum chi-square value. We further discuss the results for physical inferences and also compare the present dark energy model with $Λ\text{CDM}$ statistically using AIC and BIC.

papers.title: Simulating Training Spikes of Deep Neural Networks by Layer-wise Random Feature Models
papers.abstract: Intermittent ``spikes'' in loss, during the pre-training of Large Language Models (LLMs), remains a mysterious phenomenon both theoretically and empirically. In this paper, we show that simple quadratic models with heavy-tailed, power-law distributed inputs can replicate these spikes. We introduce a theoretical framework and simulation algorithm to model per-layer training dynamics of Deep Neural Networks (DNNs), using such quadratic models. In a case study on an Adam hyperparameter configuration (where $β_2$ is set close to $1$) known to induce spikes in Transformer LMs, our simulation successfully predicts bumps indicating spiky behavior from a given checkpoint. Furthermore, we derive an appropriate $β_2$ schedule from observed metrics, which empirically improves performance.

papers.title: Null-controllable data for cascade heat equations: almost sharp spectral spaces and modal critical times
papers.abstract: We study one-dimensional cascades of heat equations controlled through their last component. For a fixed time $T>0$, we consider the Hilbert space $\mathcal{C}_T$ of all initial data that can be steered exactly to zero at time $T$, endowed with the norm of the minimal $L^2$ control. This space can be strongly anisotropic: in explicit examples, it is incomparable with every isotropic spectral Sobolev or sub-Gaussian Gevrey scale associated with an adapted basis. For two equations, under the block Fattorini--Hautus condition, we give an almost sharp spectral description of $\mathcal{C}_T$. More precisely, in an adapted Riesz basis of generalized eigenvectors we define an explicit increasing scale $(\mathcal{V}_τ)_{τ\in\R}$ of Hilbert spaces such that $\mathcal{V}_{T-\varepsilon}\hookrightarrow\mathcal{C}_T\hookrightarrow\mathcal{V}_T$ for every $\varepsilon>0$. The weights of $\mathcal{V}_T$ combine heat dissipation with the loss of observation inside each double generalized eigenspace. When the coupling and control regions are disjoint, this recovers the known minimal null-control time $T^\star$ and identifies it as a transition time for controllable data: for $TT^\star$, the natural state space is properly contained in $\mathcal{C}_T$. We extend the analysis to arbitrary finite upper triangular heat cascades. The observation losses of the different directions in each spectral block may have distinct exponential orders, leading to a hierarchy of critical times rather than a single threshold. This hierarchy describes successive gains of null controllability on adapted modal subspaces and accounts for the interactions and cancellations between different coupling paths.

papers.title: UV Fluorescence Sensing of Medical-Chemical-and- Biological Analytes by an AlGaN/Si-on-Sapphire Optoelectronic Chip
papers.abstract: This paper proposes and analyzes a compact fluorescence-photometer lab-on-a-chip that is simpler than a fluorescence spectrometer, and that does not require spectrum reconstruction by a computer. An on-chip AlGaN VCSEL lasing at 280 nm, or at 310 nm, pumps an on-chip sample in the form of liquid or solid or tissue, thereby exciting signature fluorescence in the 300 to 540 nm wavelength range. This emission signal is detected and read out by an on-chip UV-enhanced Silicon photodiode. The 2 cm x 5 cm chip consists of C-plane (0001) Sapphire, and no lenses, prisms, or mirrors are utilized in the photometer. The chip is opto-electronic and features co-packaged electronics using tiny electronic chiplets that are bonded to the sapphire. These consist of an LD driver and transimpedance amplifier for the UV photonics, together with ASICs, ADC, microcontroller, micro-battery and RF-wireless or Ethernet chiplets. The mission of this self-contained cost-effective chip is sensing targeted medical-chemical-biological (MCB) agents in a local or network setting. Eight significant MCB applications are detailed here.

papers.title: On the Alignment Between Spectral Efficiency and Positioning Accuracy in Multi-LEO Clusters
papers.abstract: Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite constellations are expected to play a key role in future 6G Non-Terrestrial Networks (NTNs), where dense deployments enable cooperative multi-satellite processing for communication and positioning. While existing works have addressed communication and localization objectives separately, the correlation and alignment between these objectives remain largely unexplored. In this paper, we investigate the correlation between Spectral Efficiency (SE) and positioning accuracy in cooperative multi-LEO satellite clusters. We consider an uplink direct-to-device scenario in which multiple satellites jointly process user signals and evaluate cluster performance using SE and Position Error Bound (PEB) metrics. We derive Time-of-Arrival (TOA)-based and Doppler-based PEBs, while communication performance is quantified through the achievable SE under joint signal processing. Using realistic LEO constellation simulations, we demonstrate that for clusters of seven satellites, SE exhibits a strong negative correlation with Doppler-based PEB (correlation coefficient of $-0.72$). In contrast, its correlation with TOA-based PEB is notably weaker, ranging between $-0.55$ and $-0.37$. These findings suggest that communication-oriented LEO clusters are largely compatible with Doppler-based positioning, but not necessarily with TOA-based positioning.

papers.title: S-Space: Exploring Spatial Workspace in Multimodal Language Models
papers.abstract: Multimodal language models (MLLMs) exhibit promising spatial reasoning capabilities, yet the internal mechanisms supporting them remain poorly understood. We uncover S-Space, a linear representation subspace in which object-token representations encode continuous coordinates along horizontal, vertical, and distance axes. Although we identify these axes by differentiating spatial-answer scores with respect to object-token activations, S-Space is intrinsic rather than induced by specific data or prompts, remaining readable under non-spatial questions. We show that S-Space functions as an internal spatial workspace of MLLMs. Perception encodes object locations into it, forming spatial representations that can be directly read out to support accurate spatial judgments. Internal reasoning transforms it for changing viewpoints. Verbal responses selectively access it, evidenced by causal interventions that alter spatial judgments while largely preserving non-spatial responses. Case studies further show that S-Space assigns locations to unseen entities and the observer, and connects physical directions with abstract linguistic meanings, suggesting both the capabilities and limitations of large-scale language training. Finally, we use S-Space as a diagnostic tool for spatial reasoning failures. Direction-word readouts reveal systematic coupling between cardinal and image-relative reference frames. More importantly, a perception-computation decomposition exposes a key bottleneck: MLLMs can form capable spatial representations, yet fall short in the spatial transformations required to reason reliably across viewpoint changes.

papers.title: Reconstruction and Symmetry of Two-Token Graphs
papers.abstract: We present a proof of the two-token graph reconstruction conjecture. Every finite simple graph $G,H$ of order at least three, $F_2(G) \cong F_2(H)$ if and only if $G \cong H$. We also classify the automorphism groups of two-token graphs whose connected roots have order at least five. Combining these results, we show that, for connected graphs $G,H$ of order at least five, every isomorphism $φ:F_2(G)\to F_2(H)$ admits a factorization $φ=η\circσ^{(2)}$, where $σ^{(2)}$ is induced by a graph isomorphism $σ:G\to H$, and $η\in \operatorname{Aut}(F_2(H))$ is a product of twin-cut switches or Cartesian exchanges.

papers.title: Campana strong approximation on generalized Markoff surfaces
papers.abstract: For every smooth projective generalised Markoff surface $X_m$, every hyperplane section $H$, and every integer $n\ge2$, we establish Campana strong approximation with the Brauer--Manin obstruction for $\bigl(X_m,(1-1/n)H\bigr)$.

papers.title: Teams without teams: a trace-based method for measuring team-like organization
papers.abstract: Digital platforms provide increasingly detailed traces of collaborative activity, yet these traces do not directly reveal whether contributions remain largely independent or whether more structured forms of collective work emerge through interaction. This paper addresses the methodological problem of measuring such organization when the collective being studied is not defined as a team in advance. We propose a trace-based method for measuring teamness, understood as the degree to which collaborative activity expresses properties associated with teamwork. The method translates established dimensions of teamwork into behavioral indicators that can be recovered from digital traces. These indicators can be examined separately and summarized through a composite measure of their joint expression. It does not require predefined team membership and is designed to be adapted across collaborative settings. We illustrate the method using revision histories from 52,437 articles in the English Wikipedia's Medicine WikiProject, comprising more than 10 million human-authored edits. Using article-months as observation units, the application shows that different dimensions of teamlike organization display distinct patterns and that their joint expression can vary within the same articles over time. The contribution is a general measurement framework for examining graded and dynamic forms of collective organization directly from behavioral traces.

papers.title: Quadratic-size Random Permutations are Universal
papers.abstract: A permutation is $n$-universal if it contains every permutation of length $n$ as a pattern. We prove that a uniformly random permutation of length $32n^2$ is $n$-universal with probability at least $1-\exp(-n/25)$ for all sufficiently large $n$. This removes a $\log\log n$ factor from an earlier result of He and Kwan~\cite{He-Kwan} and resolves an open problem of Alon~\cite{Alon2016}. The proof was found by GPT-6 Pro.

papers.title: Zeros of the Spectrogram of White Noise with Hermite Windows
papers.abstract: We study the zeros of the spectrogram of complex white noise analyzed with Hermite windows of order n, extending the classical Gaussian-window correspondence with Gaussian Analytic Functions to the polyanalytic setting. Using the polyanalytic Bargmann transform, these zeros split into two families according to the sign of the local Jacobian, giving rise to a natural notion of charge, and we show that these zeros are almost surely simple, isolated, and form a translation and rotation-invariant point process. We derive closed-form expressions for the one-point intensity, decomposed by charge, and also for the unsigned, signed, and hybrid two-point intensities. Besides, we prove that unlike the total repulsion observed with a Gaussian window, the Hermite window of order n generates a pair correlation function that converges at the origin to a strictly positive constant depending on n. Finally, we propose a numerical method for detecting spectrogram zeros via the winding number around candidate local minima.

papers.title: Hsiang cubics as spherical Chebyshev polynomials: equioscillation and idempotent quadrature
papers.abstract: A Hsiang cubic is a cubic form on $\mathbb{R}^{n}$ whose zero set is a minimal cone; equivalently, it is the cubic form of a commutative nonassociative metrized algebra satisfying a single identity of degree four. We show that the intrinsic geometry of such an algebra, encoded in its idempotents and their Peirce decompositions, is the geometry of a Chebyshev-type extremal problem on the sphere. A Hsiang cubic equioscillates on $S^{n-1}$: its maximum set is the set of normalized idempotents, and on suitable great circles through an idempotent it restricts to the Chebyshev polynomial $T_3$. For the spherical analogue of the problem of least deviation, the minimization of $\|p\|_\infty^2/\|p\|_2^2$ over harmonic cubics, a sharp lower bound based on Kellogg's inequality shows that Cartan's isoparametric cubics are the global minimizers in dimensions $5$, $8$, $14$ and $26$. In general, we compute the ratio of every Hsiang cubic in terms of the Killing form and characterize stationarity by a Kolmogorov criterion: it amounts to a positive measure on the idempotent variety. Such measures are given explicitly in several cases which together cover every Hsiang cubic known to exist; in particular, all of them are stationary. These measures give quadrature identities on the idempotent variety whose moments are invariants of the algebra; they are spherical designs exactly in the Einstein (Killing metrized) case, i.e.\ when the Killing form is proportional to the inner product. Distinguished low-dimensional Hsiang cubics are strict local minimizers, whereas a polar Hsiang cubic is a stationary non-minimizer.

papers.title: Re-emergence of fingering in solidifying liquid-metal drops
papers.abstract: Solidification is expected to suppress fingering by removing mobile liquid. Here we report an unexpected re-emergence of fingering in impacting molten-tin drops: cooling first weakens peripheral fingers, but stronger undercooling restores them. At weak undercooling, fingers originate from a decelerating liquid rim and solidification reduces the effective acceleration that drives Rayleigh--Taylor-like amplification. At strong undercooling, solidification structures develop while liquid is still spreading, creating lateral mobility contrasts that redirect the residual flow. Comparison between the kinematically estimated solidification time and the experimentally measured fingering-onset and growth-termination times reveals a reversal in temporal ordering across the temperature range. A physics-based reduced-order model combines solidification-modified rim deceleration with mobility-gradient growth, captures the characteristic onset dynamics and accounts for the final finger length within the same physical framework.These findings establish solidification as an active means of regulating interfacial flow and morphology, with broad implications spanning metal-based additive manufacturing and debris mitigation in semiconducting industry.

papers.title: MAGMA-Bench: Evaluating Long-Horizon Embodied Agents under Dynamic Tasks and Execution Failures
papers.abstract: Long-horizon embodied agents must maintain task-relevant information, coordinate heterogeneous robots, and adapt their decisions as execution unfolds. Existing benchmarks investigate dynamic task execution and embodied multi-agent coordination, but provide limited evaluation of their intersection. We introduce MAGMA-Bench, an architecture-agnostic benchmark for persistent task reasoning in dynamic multi-robot environments. MAGMA-Bench evaluates agents across increasing task horizons and controlled online perturbations, including execution failures, task interruptions, and mission updates, with scenarios requiring coordination across robots with heterogeneous capabilities. It uses a structured skill-level interface to separate task-level reasoning from perception and low-level control. We evaluate locally deployable open-weight planners, multi-agent state-tracking strategies, and frontier models. Even the strongest evaluated models fail on a substantial fraction of clean episodes, and their success rates decrease further under online perturbations. Supervised adaptation greatly improves a small model, but performance remains substantially lower on longer and multi-robot missions. We release the benchmark, 261,646 task-level training examples, and an architecture-agnostic expert-trace generation pipeline.

papers.title: Knowing Whether, Not Just Where: Anchor-Probing Distillation for Open-Set Remote Sensing Visual Grounding
papers.abstract: Open-set visual grounding in remote sensing requires models to determine not only where a queried object is located, but also whether the image provides sufficient evidence for the query at all. Existing closed-set grounding models, however, tend to return plausible boxes even for absent objects, blurring localization confidence with genuine Visual Support. We introduce AnchorProbe-Distill (APD), a teacher-student framework that recasts open-set grounding as Visual Support learning. APD builds on the insight that supported queries should induce coherent spatial anchors, whereas unsupported or mismatched queries tend to produce unstable or misleading localization patterns. APD-T therefore uses the Original Query as a Reference Anchor to interpret query perturbations: Semantic-Preserving Queries retain the annotated target, Near-Category Ambiguous Queries are resolved according to whether they form a reliable alternative anchor or collapse onto the Reference Anchor, and Far-Category Counterfactual Queries provide rejection supervision. This reference-aware reasoning is distilled into APD-S, enabling unified localization and rejection from a single image--query pair. Experiments show that APD enables the resulting model to reject absent targets while also improving its localization of present targets.

papers.title: Defence against the dark arts of distillation: Unsupervised discovery of subliminal learning
papers.abstract: When a language model is distilled from a teacher that shares its base parameters, the student can inherit behavioural traits of the teacher---including misalignment---even from data that is semantically unrelated to the trait (Cloud et al., 2026). All existing defences require knowing the trait. We remove this requirement and prove that a subliminally transferred trait can be recovered from the parameter updates alone, without supervision, by exploiting a single asymmetry: the trait is expressed consistently across diverse datasets generated by the teacher, whereas task-specific and shared capabilities vary. The resulting estimator returns a weight-space direction that can be amplified to discover and interpret the trait or projected out to suppress it. Applied to the subliminal-learning benchmarks of (Cloud et al., 2026), our method recovers the transmitted animal-preference traits without any trait labels and suppresses their expression with almost no impact to task performance.

papers.title: First Experimental Results of Space Object Detection Using the InteRFeX Array
papers.abstract: This paper presents the first experimental validation of InteRFeX, a non-uniform receive only (passive) array located at the Nova Systems Space Precinct in Peterborough, Australia, designed for space domain awareness applications. It operates over a frequency range of 70 to 300 MHz and is capable of functioning in a range of observational modes, including as a coherent passive bistatic radar for space surveillance, which is the focus of this work. InteRFeX exploits commercial broadcast transmissions as illuminators of opportunity, combining cross-ambiguity function processing for bistatic range and range-rate retrieval with MUSIC-based direction-of-arrival (DoA) estimation for angular localization. The International Space Station (ISS) serves as the experimental target, with measurements evaluated against Two-Line Element (TLE) orbit predictions. Taking advantage of the dual-polarized array, all four reference--surveillance polarization combinations are evaluated, revealing differences in detection rate and mean signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) over the observation pass, with bistatic-range RMSEs of approximately 1 km relative to the TLE-derived reference. Independently, the MUSIC-based DoA estimates exhibit a mean angular separation of approximately $0.45^\circ$ from the TLE-derived reference directions. The angular deviations are further decomposed into along-track and cross-track components, enabling a more detailed characterization of the DoA offsets relative to the TLE-derived reference trajectory. The processing framework also includes a first-order bistatic link-budget analysis to estimate the expected SNR over the observation geometry. These results demonstrate the feasibility of passive-radar space domain awareness using radio-interferometric array technology and establish the proposed signal-processing pipeline as a basis for a dedicated coherent passive-radar mode within InteRFeX.

papers.title: Aubry-André transition in photonic time quasicrystals
papers.abstract: In one dimension, Anderson localization by a disordered potential sets in at any strength, whereas localization by a quasiperiodic potential in the Aubry-André model occurs through a transition at a critical strength. Disordered photonic time crystals exhibit a temporal counterpart of this Anderson localization, in which light, instead of decaying in space, stops propagating and grows in time. Whether a counterpart of the Aubry-André transition exists in photonic time quasicrystals remains an open question. Here we show that it does, and that the transition occurs at mobility edges in momentum rather than in energy. These edges arise even under impulsive modulation, where the field obeys the self-dual almost-Mathieu equation exactly, and for general analytic modulations Avila's global theory reveals the condition under which they form. The Aubry-André transition thus extends from spatial lattices to the time domain, where it sorts light by wave number into components that propagate and components that stop and grow.

papers.title: Hölder regularity of solutions to parabolic equations associated with fractional $p$-Laplacian type operators
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study Hölder regularity of local weak super-solutions to the parabolic equation associated with fractional $p$-Laplacian type operators $$ \partial_t u(t,x)-\text{p.v.}\int_{\R^d}|u(t,y)-u(t,x)|^{p-2}(u(t,y)-u(t,x))J(t;x,y)\,dy=0,\quad (t,x)\in \R\times \R^d, $$ where $\text{p.v.}$ denotes the principal value, $p\in(1,\infty)$ and the kernel $J(t;x,y)$ is comparable (uniformly with respect to $(t;x,y)\in\R\times\R^d\times\R^d$) to the fractional $p$-Laplacian kernel $|x-y|^{-d-sp}$ with $s\in(0,1)$. Our contribution extends the fundamental work of Kassmann and Weidner to the nonlinear case $p\ne 2$. In particular, we provide an explicit nonlocal parabolic tail condition in terms of an $L^{1+\varepsilon}$-norm in the time variable (for a suitable $\varepsilon>0$) for all $p\in(1,\infty)$, under which Hölder regularity holds. Our proof is based on the method of expansion of positivity, which is the key ingredient in the reduction-of-oscillation argument.

papers.title: On a maximum principle in discretization with spherical harmonics
papers.abstract: Spherical harmonics have been studied extensively and are used in many fields of application. We consider the probably earliest application of spherical harmonics, namely for a representation of the solution of the Laplace equation on the $d$-dimensional unit sphere where the boundary data are represented in a spherical harmonics basis. We consider general $d \geq 2$. For the solution $u$ of the Laplace equation the fundamental maximum principle holds. If one approximates the boundary data in the finite dimensional space spanned by all spherical harmonics of degree at most $N$, the resulting discrete solution, denoted by $u_N$, does in general not satisfy the maximum principle. In this paper we derive sharp estimates for $r_N^{\rm max}$ such that the maximum principle holds for $u_N(x)$ for all $x \in \Bbb{R}^d$ with $\|x\| \leq r_N^{\rm max}$. We show that for $d=3$ one has $r_N^{\rm max} \gtrsim 1- 3 N^{-1} \ln\big( 2^\frac13 N \big) $. Similar estimates are derived for $d \neq 3$. We also study the sharpness of these estimates.

papers.title: Efficient Confidence-Aware Densification for 3DGS
papers.abstract: 3DGS-MCMC has replaced the gradient-driven density control of 3D Gaussian Splatting with opacity-based sampling and relocation, and is now the de facto standard for prior-free densification under a fixed primitive budget. Because opacity stays high where the scene is already well reconstructed, this sampling sends most new primitives to the foreground and leaves the background under-reconstructed. At low budgets, prior-based methods such as ConeGS and EDGS outperform it, at the cost of a pre-trained radiance field or dense image matches and a separate initialization stage. We argue for a comeback of error-driven densification within the fixed-budget MCMC framework. Our confidence-aware densification keeps the fixed budget and gradual growth of 3DGS-MCMC, but places primitives by the image error instead of the opacity. New primitives are drawn mostly where screen-space gradients are large. We favor primitives with a low learned confidence, which marks regions the reconstruction still explains poorly, and relocate the primitives that contribute least to the rendered images to these places. Averaged over 24 scenes, our method outperforms 3DGS-MCMC in PSNR, SSIM and LPIPS at every budget from 100k to 2M primitives. At 100k, without a prior or an initialization stage, it recovers 0.84dB of the 1.05dB PSNR by which ConeGS leads 3DGS-MCMC, and from 500k on, it has the highest PSNR and SSIM of all fixed-budget methods we compare with, including ConeGS and EDGS. While inherently prior-free, our densification can also exploit priors: from the ConeGS or EDGS initialization, it matches ConeGS in PSNR and SSIM at 100k and is best in all three metrics at 500k.

papers.title: Giant geometric nonlinear transport in inhomogeneously strained Bi$_2$Se$_3$ single crystalline slabs
papers.abstract: Electrical transport in non-centrosymmetric materials exhibits a nonlinear conductivity tensor component that generates second-harmonic voltages in response to applied electric fields. Harnessing this effect is essential for developing zero-threshold electromagnetic energy harvesters and broadband frequency upconverters, both of which require maximizing the nonlinear responsivity. Here, we demonstrate that inhomogeneously strained macroscopic slabs of the topological insulator Bi$_2$Se$_3$ achieve a record-high nonlinear responsivity of $10^4\,μ$m/V: a six orders of magnitude boost compared to its thin-film counterparts. We attribute this giant enhancement to a classical geometric nonlinear transport effect, which is driven by complex strain gradients within the bulk material. Notably, a similar geometric mechanism known as geometric nonlinear Hall was previously observed only in microscale-patterned structures. Our findings establish macroscopic strain engineering as a powerful route to enhance nonlinear transport, with immediate relevance to a broad class of layered systems, including transition metal dichalcogenides and moiré heterostructures.

papers.title: Three options are roughly enough - Variance-optimal semi-static hedging in the rough Heston model
papers.abstract: This paper studies semi-static variance-optimal hedging of variance swaps in the rough Heston model under a risk-neutral measure. We combine dynamic trading in the underlying asset with static positions in a finite basket of European options, with the aim of minimizing the variance of the residual hedging error. Exploiting the Markovian lift provided by the forward variance curve, the Fourier representations of the claims and the Laplace transform characterization of the log-price, we derive semi-explicit formulas for the optimal strategies and the hedging error. We then study the optimal claim selection problem, investigating numerically how the choice of static instruments depends on the Hurst index. Under standard parametrization, we discover that "three options are roughly enough", i.e. adding three static vanilla options reduces the hedging error by more than 95% relative to the purely dynamic hedge for all considered roughness regimes H= 0.1, 0.3, 0.5.

papers.title: Stationary Ergodic Mean-field Games of Constrained Singular Controls
papers.abstract: We study a stationary ergodic mean-field game of scalar type where the representative player controls a diffusion through two-sided singular controls exerted only at the jump times of an independent Poisson process. For each mean-field parameter, we solve the novel constrained ergodic singular control problem, proving that the optimal policy is of threshold type: the diffusion is reset at Poisson arrival times to the nearest boundary point of an interval. Our explicit probabilistic derivation of the stationary distributions induced by Poissonian threshold singular controls is a key contribution of independent interest. This distribution is used to construct the mean-field fixed-point map. We prove existence and uniqueness of the stationary mean-field equilibrium by combining the stationary density with the monotonicity and continuity of the optimal thresholds in the mean-field parameter. The model provides a tractable framework for a case study of partially reversible investment with singular adjustments under exogenous intervention constraints.

papers.title: Formalisation of information processing and intelligence in proteinoid networks
papers.abstract: Proteinoid microspheres are electrically active assemblies of thermally polymerised amino acids that exhibit spontaneous oscillations, spike-like events, stimulus-dependent responses, adaptation and collective dynamics. We formulate these observations as an applied-mathematical problem and develop a unified dynamical framework for information processing in proteinoid networks. Individual microspheres are represented by nonlinear excitable or oscillatory systems, whereas interactions are described by weighted adaptive graphs and, in the spatial limit, reaction--diffusion dynamics. The framework combines signal propagation, attenuation, fading memory, adaptive coupling, synchronisation, information transfer, reservoir readout, robustness and energetic constraints. We define a task-relative proteinoid intelligence functional from normalised measures of stimulus information, memory, adaptation, directed information transfer, task performance and robustness, penalised by energetic and structural costs. Analytical results establish a joint-response information bound, an upper bound on linear memory for stable linear networks, and existence of an optimal admissible coupling matrix under compact constraints. Dimensionless groups identify the relative time scales and coupling regimes governing the problem in nonlinear and adaptive network dynamics.

papers.title: AI and humanity's long conversation
papers.abstract: These are notes to accompany my public lecture at the International Congress of Mathematicians, in Philadelphia in July, 2026. The goal is to discuss some developments at the interface of AI and mathematics in the context of the long conversation of mathematics.

papers.title: MOSAIC: Multi-Scale Object-Centric Slot Adaptation with Image-Guided Prototype Conditioning for Remote Sensing Image Super-Resolution
papers.abstract: Pretrained diffusion Transformers provide powerful generative priors for image restoration, yet adapting them to structure-sensitive tasks remains challenging. Existing methods mainly rely on dense low-resolution features as conditions, which often entangle salient objects with dominant backgrounds and provide limited abstraction for recurring structures across scales and samples. We propose MOSAIC, an object-centric representation learning framework that learns compact structural conditions for generative model adaptation. MOSAIC organizes degraded observations into structural slots that capture complementary object-level and layout-level evidence, integrates them across resolutions, and retrieves recurring priors from a shared prototype memory to complement incomplete image-specific information. The resulting representations are injected into selected layers of a frozen diffusion Transformer through lightweight residual modulation, preserving its pretrained generative prior. We instantiate MOSAIC for remote sensing image super-resolution, where small objects, repetitive structures, and large-scale variation provide a challenging testbed. Experiments on UCMerced, AID, and RSSCN7 show consistent PSNR improvements across $\times 2$ and $\times 4$ settings and favorable LPIPS results at $\times 4$. Qualitative results further demonstrate improved preservation of small objects, structural boundaries, and repetitive spatial patterns.

papers.title: Auditing VLM Benchmarks from Existing Evaluation Runs
papers.abstract: Every evaluation run of a vision-language model (VLM) already produces per-question artifacts (predictions, judged correctness, metadata) that leaderboards reduce to a single score and then discard. We reuse those artifacts to audit the benchmark itself, and add an audit layer to VLMEvalKit: six detectors that run as post-processing over saved outputs, plus one additional text-only rerun with visual inputs removed, emitting a per-question report. The layer reports per-question findings together with aggregate audit statistics; for the headline quantities, it attaches permutation-null excess where applicable, interval estimates for proportions, and sensitivity to the model pool. Auditing MMStar, a benchmark curated specifically so that the image is indispensable, with three models, we find zero aggregate accuracy gain from the image on 20.2% of its questions. An item-matched permutation null accounts for 17.0%, leaving a +3.2 pp excess (corrected permutation p = 0.001). This excess is concentrated in the mathematics and science categories and is absent from coarse perception, a localization consistent with knowledge substituting for visual evidence; confirming that mechanism would require item-level review. A second detector flags 134 questions on which every model that answered in parseable form picked the same non-gold option, and these candidates peak in the perception categories, whereas the zero-gain excess is largest in mathematics and science & technology. Replacing the LLM judge with exact string matching changes no conclusion, and every scoring discrepancy between the two traces to one model whose free-form answers a parser cannot read. On a binary yes/no benchmark the detectors measurably fall out of calibration, a scope boundary that we measure and report. The audit layer, the prediction artifacts and the generated reports accompany this submission.

papers.title: ELMA: Benchmarking Anaphoric Compositions for Long-Term Text-to-Motion Generation
papers.abstract: Text-guided long-term human motion generation is essential for applications such as continuously operating digital avatars.
