papers.abstract: We propose a rational comparison between several well-known machine-learning interatomic potentials (linear atomic cluster expansion, the Behler-Parrinello high-dimensional neural network potential, and the graph neural network-based MACE potential) by testing their performance for fitting classical potentials such as the Lennard-Jones and Stillinger-Weber potential. With this we assess their advantages and limitations regarding several aspects: varying training dataset size, robustness to noise, carbon footprint, as well as the ability to reproduce the radial distribution function as an example observable. Overall the MACE models are shown to most accurately reproduce the potential energy surface, with little sign of overfitting, but at a significant computational cost, highlighting important questions regarding the choice of models in computational materials science.

papers.title: An Introduction to the $p$-Differential Forms in Spinor Variables on the Minkowskian Manifold
papers.abstract: This article presents an introductory study of $p$-differential forms in spinor variables defined on the Minkowskian (or Lorentzian) manifold. Starting from the algebraic and geometric foundations of spinor spaces and Clifford algebras, we establish the correspondence between Minkowski spacetime and Hermitian matrices in spinor coordinates. Within this framework, we construct differential 1-forms and 2-forms expressed in spinor notation, and formulate the Dirac operator in terms of exterior calculus. Furthermore, we extend this approach to the case of non-monogenic functions, following the method proposed in~\cite{Jaramillo2024}. The results illustrate the consistency of the spinorial exterior calculus and its potential applications in the study of relativistic field equations and geometric formulations of quantum theory.

papers.title: Restricting Odd Antiholes in Critical Graphs via List Coloring
papers.abstract: By the Strong Perfect Graph Theorem, every graph whose chromatic number exceeds its clique number contains an odd hole or an odd antihole. We investigate the structure of odd antiholes in critical graphs with fixed maximum degree. We prove that if $G$ is a $k$-critical graph with maximum degree $Δ$ then every odd antihole in $G$ has length at most $2(Δ-k)+7$, and conjecture that, in the odd-hole-free setting, equality forces the graph itself to be the corresponding odd antihole. We verify this extremal characterization when $Δ\geq 2k-5$, extending recent results for $Δ=k$, and construct $k$-critical odd-hole-free graphs showing that the next possible odd antihole length $2(Δ-k)+5$ below the extremal bound can occur. Our proofs use a list-coloring theorem for graphs on $2\ell-1$ vertices whose complements are hypomatchable. This motivates the conjecture that every odd antihole $\overline{C_{2\ell-1}}$ is strongly $\ell$-chromatic-choosable; we show that this conjecture would imply the full extremal characterization. We also obtain degree and attachment restrictions for odd antiholes in critical graphs.

papers.title: Perturbative Renormalization of Noether Currents in SYM with Improved Discretizations
papers.abstract: We investigate the perturbative renormalization of Noether currents associated with chiral symmetry and supersymmetry transformations in $\mathcal{N}=1$ supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory, regularized on the lattice using improved discretizations. In particular, we study the chiral current and the supercurrent operator for a broad class of lattice actions: Wilson fermions with one-step stout-smeared links and a clover term, together with a family of Symanzik-improved gluon actions. Since the supercurrent mixes with both gauge-invariant and gauge-noninvariant operators, we compute the corresponding renormalization factors and mixing coefficients at one-loop order. We analyze the impact of improved gluon and gluino actions on this mixing pattern and investigate whether suitable choices of lattice parameters, such as the clover and stout coefficients, can reduce unwanted lattice artifacts at one loop. Our results provide perturbative input for the implementation of Ward identities and for matching lattice observables to their continuum counterparts, while also offering guidance for simulations aimed at restoring supersymmetry in the continuum limit.

papers.title: Dynamical degrees of automorphisms of non-projective hyperkähler manifolds
papers.abstract: We determine the dynamical degrees of bimeromorphic automorphisms of hyperkähler manifolds of all known deformation types with irreducible characteristic polynomial.

papers.title: Understanding the Power Consumption of Modern High Bandwidth Memory: Experimental Analysis and Modeling Using Real HBM2 DRAM Chips
papers.abstract: We perform the first comprehensive experimental characterization of power consumed by real HBM2 DRAM chips. Our extensive characterization yields 1) the empirical basis for developing new, accurate HBM power models or validating existing power models and 2) key insights into structural and data-pattern-dependent variation of power in HBM2 chips. Out of our 13 new findings and 6 key takeaway messages, we highlight: 1) a read operation consumes significantly higher current than any other operation and 2) the toggled data bus signals in a data transfer burst significantly affect current draw where toggling all HBM2-internal bank group bus signals causes 29.4% higher power consumption than keeping them constant. Leveraging our empirical insights into HBM2 power consumption, we engineer an access pattern that yields 23.6% higher power consumption on average across 36 tested HBM2 chips than the highest-power-consuming JEDEC-specified current measurement loop. Our results have important implications for HBM-based system design and validation. Relying solely on JEDEC- or vendor-specified test loops to bound HBM power could cause system failures and/or thermal throttling in real-world high-power AI/ML workloads. To improve 3D-stacked DRAM power modeling in open source architectural simulation infrastructures, we develop a new HBM power model. Our model predicts the power of 36 real HBM2 chips across diverse workloads (including a real LLM decode workload) with 7.6 -- 8.1% mean absolute percentage error, substantially more accurately than state-of-the-art HBM power models. The power consumption predicted by our model for a power-intensive microbenchmark closely matches (with 2.4% to 5.3% error across HBM3E's specified supply voltage range) the average HBM3E memory power consumed by three tested NVIDIA H200 GPUs. We publicly release our power model at https://github.com/CMU-SAFARI/HBM-Power.

papers.title: From LLM Plans to Authorized Motion: Execution-Bound Authorization for Excavators
papers.abstract: An LLM-directed excavator can execute mechanically feasible motion whose destination or authority no longer matches the operator's approval. We propose execution-bound authorization for the approval--dispatch--execution interval. A one-use lease binds the action, generated motion, mission contract and admission tolerance; atomic dispatch rechecks current authority and measured joint drift. Periodic supervision detects revocation and requests a quintic stop with a carry-pitch endpoint, selected through sampled joint, stroke, flow and reference-acceleration checks. The framework connects exact motion identity to dispatch integrity and load-aware interruption. Evaluation combines a 672-case interface suite, four loaded digging cases in synchronous simulation, unloaded MuJoCo/Pinocchio transfers and two command-level LLM planners. The gateway admitted all 120 benign interface cases and produced zero unauthorized dispatches in the attack suite. Loaded dispatch-window tests produced zero unauthorized deposition. During simulated dump-phase revocation, maximum closed-site deposition decreased from 1.23 to 0.33\,m$^3$; loaded-slew stops used less than 75\% of nominal swing torque. These results demonstrate motion-bound authorization and quantify the retention and stopping behavior of supervised excavation skills.

papers.title: Learning Non-Gaussian SEMs with Conditional Risk, and Why the Direction of Recursion Matters
papers.abstract: Variance-based methods recover a Gaussian linear structural equation model (SEM) with equal or suitably constrained error variances, either by recursively identifying the source nodes with smallest conditional variance (top-down method) or sink nodes with highest conditional variance (bottom-up method). We show that the use of conditional variance is incidental: replacing it with the conditional risk, i.e., the minimal expected loss of linear prediction under the negative log-likelihood of the noise distribution, extends both methods to non-Gaussian noise. Existing methods are the least-squares special case. This yields two main results. First, exploiting the noise distribution improves structure recovery: the matched-loss procedures recover the SEM more accurately than their least-squares counterparts and the LiNGAM methods, which are designed for non-Gaussianity. Second, the two methods, interchangeable in the Gaussian setting, separate under non-Gaussian noise: the top-down method is correct for every noise density with finite differential entropy, whereas the bottom-up method requires a regularity condition and can fail without it, for instance under mean-zero exponential or Cauchy noise. Simulations confirm both results.

papers.title: Partitioning the magnetization raises the stability limit of ferromagnetic colloids
papers.abstract: Magnetic actuation scales with a particle's magnetic moment, yet practical colloidal suspensions remain superparamagnetic or weakly magnetized, a permanent dipole drives a near contact attraction growing as the square of the moment, binding particles irreversibly. Here we show that this constraint depends not only on how much magnetic material a particle carries, but on where it sits. Partitioning a fixed moment M into N internal elements leaves the far field interaction, and every actuation force, unchanged while suppressing the near-field pair energy by 1/N. As we show in our experiments across 57 samples and three geometries, stability collapses onto a single $\sim M^{2}/N$ boundary, raising the accessible dipolar energy scale nearly 150-fold. A liquid-phase analogue of magnetic force microscopy images the engineered energy landscape directly. The resulting colloids outrun size-matched superparamagnetic beads in weak fields far from a magnetic source, suggesting their applicability in hard to reach places. Together, these results open a new operating regime for colloidal manipulation, with impactful implications in microfluidics and drug delivery.

papers.title: Akule: Fast and Scalable Multi-Robot Motion Planning via Sparse Interaction Diffusion
papers.abstract: Diffusion models provide expressive trajectory priors for multi-robot motion planning (MRMP), but scaling them to large teams requires coordinating individual motions without expensive joint computation. We introduce Akule, a sparse interaction diffusion framework that augments a frozen single-robot prior with three learned modules: a reusable pairwise correction model $R_φ$, a contextual selector $U_ψ$ that determines which corrections to evaluate, and a composer $G_ω$ that combines their effects through context-dependent signed weights. This decomposition separates which interactions merit computation from how their effects should be combined into coordinated denoising updates. We train $R_φ$ using matched pairwise trajectory optimizations, then learn $G_ω$ and $U_ψ$ from physically optimized joint trajectories without requiring a prescribed ground-truth interaction graph. The resulting joint proposals are passed to a downstream search-based planner for validation and repair. Across diverse MRMP benchmarks, Akule achieves competitive planning success, complete-planner speedups of up to $25\times$, zero-shot population transfer, and successful planning with up to $256$ robots. Ablations further demonstrate that learned selection and composition reduce pre-repair conflicts and downstream repair effort relative to heuristic selection and uniform summation.

papers.title: On the calculation of an integral introduced by Hubert Delange
papers.abstract: In his paper, ''Sur la distribution des fractions irréductibles de dénominateur $n$ ou de dénominateur au plus égal à $x$'', Hubert Delange considers the family integrals defined by \begin{equation*} \int_0^1\left(\frac{N(n,t)}{φ(n)}-t\right)^{2q}dt, \end{equation*} where $n>1$ and $q>0$ are positive integers, $φ$ is the Euler totient function, and for any real number $t>0$, $N(n,t)$ counts the number reduced fractions whith denominator $n$ that belong to the interval $]0,t]$. He was able to evaluate the integral for $q=1$ but stated that ''Malheureusement, nous n'avons pas su jusqu'à présent faire cette évaluation pour $q>1$''. In addition to its intrinsic interest, this calculation would help understand the asymptotic distribution of the $φ(n)$ totatives of $n$ relative to $φ(n)$ equidistributed numbers in $[0,n]$. In this paper, we first provide some general properties of the integral for any $q>1$ and reduce the problem to its calculation for odd square-free integers with at least two distinct prime factors. We then analyse into more detail the case $q=2$ for which we provide a formula that reduces the problem to the evaluation of the fourfold Möbius sum, of integer valued modular sums related to generalized Dedekind sums.

papers.title: Harvesting-Aware Routing for Low-Latency Reliable Transmission in Interference-Powered Networks
papers.abstract: We consider a multi-hop wireless network where energy-harvesting nodes rely solely on ambient radio-frequency interference as their power source. The goal is to deliver a packet from source to destination with minimum latency while guaranteeing a target end-to-end outage probability under Rayleigh fading. This gives rise to a joint routing and power allocation problem in which interference plays a dual role: it provides harvestable energy, but also impairs link reliability. We first transform the intricate, multiplicative end-to-end outage constraint into an additive form. Then, we propose two optimal algorithms. The first, HOPE, minimizes the bottleneck harvesting latency, i.e., the longest energy-accumulation time along the path, by reducing the problem to a least-cost path computation on a graph with interference-aware link weights. The second, THOPE, extends the objective to total end-to-end latency, adding the cumulative transmission delay, and likewise admits a closed-form least-cost path solution. Both algorithms are solved in polynomial time via Dijkstra's algorithm and yield explicit expressions for the optimal transmit powers. Extensive simulations reveal that HOPE and THOPE reduce the average total latency by up to an order of magnitude compared with shortest-path and minimum-energy benchmarks, while exhibiting sharply concentrated delay distributions that are largely insensitive to interferer density.

papers.title: A series with a Cantorval set of subsums and ratio of consecutive terms tending to $1/2$ (the second Jones problem)
papers.abstract: The second Jones problem (2011) consists in determining whether there exists a convergent positive series for which the ratio of consecutive terms has a limit and the set of subsums is a Cantorval; in the survey by Gł{\k a}b and Prus-Wiśniowski (2026) this problem is included in the list of open problems. In this paper, a family of such series is constructed explicitly as combinations of blocks of the form $\frac{2^k-1}{2^t} + \frac{2^{k-1}}{2^t} + \frac{2^{k-2}}{2^t} + \cdots + \frac{2}{2^t}$, where $t$ is the index of the last term of the block in the series and $k\ge2$ is the length of the block. For each series of the family it is proved that its set of subsums contains an interval and is not a finite union of closed intervals, and hence is a Cantorval. The proof relies on mixed-radix numerical systems with a redundant alphabet and uses an idea of Guthrie and Nymann (1988). If the lengths of the blocks tend to infinity, then the limit of the ratio of consecutive terms of such series is $\tfrac{1}{2}$, which, by a result of Jones, is the only possible value of the limit for which the set of subsums of a series can be a Cantorval. Thus, an affirmative answer to the second Jones problem is obtained.

papers.title: Adaptive-Depth Is a Finishing Stage
papers.abstract: Looped transformers reuse the same layer multiple times, allowing inference compute to be adjusted without changing the model. Recent adaptive-depth methods train the model across multiple loop depths from the beginning of training. We introduce fixed-first training, which varies model depth only during a short final phase of training. At 200M parameters, training a model of fixed-depth 2 for the first 67% of the run reduces modeled training compute by 45% while keeping mean negative log-likelihood (NLL) across inference depths within 0.5% of training across depths throughout. At 1B parameters, training initially at depth 4 reduces modeled compute by 31% to 37% and wall-clock time by 32% to 39%, while keeping final NLL within 0.8% and downstream differences within the observed seed variation. These results show that training over the full range of depths can be reserved for a short finishing phase with only small changes in performance.

papers.title: SliderEdit++: Improved Slider Trajectories in Instruction-Based Image Editing
papers.abstract: Slider-based control aims to give users continuous, fine-grained control over the intensity of individual edits in instruction-based image editing. However, existing approaches fail to deliver reliable continuous controllability: traversing a slider can produce abrupt visual jumps and non-monotonic changes, while jointly controlled sliders can interfere with one another. To systematically study these limitations, we introduce SlideBench, a comprehensive benchmark for continuous image editing spanning diverse editing categories and equipped with a unified suite of metrics quantifying monotonic progression, perceptual continuity, and inter-slider disentanglement. Building on these observations, we propose SliderEdit++, which explicitly regularizes the intermediate editing trajectory rather than supervising only its endpoints. Our method combines velocity- and semantic-space trajectory regularization with spectral control to encourage smooth, predictable slider traversal, together with a disentanglement objective that reduces interference between independently controlled edits. On SlideBench, SliderEdit++ achieves state-of-the-art performance, improving the overall score by 18.5% relative to the strongest baseline. At the same time, using a few-step editing backbone makes our method approximately 3x to 20x faster than existing slider-based approaches, enabling substantially more responsive interactive editing.

papers.title: Image Diffusion Models Are Good 3D Human Motion Generators
papers.abstract: Text-to-motion generation typically relies on dataset-specific skeletal representations, with models trained separately for benchmarks with different joint layouts. We investigate whether image diffusion architectures can model 3D human motion through a common image-compatible representation that accommodates heterogeneous skeletal layouts while preserving motion-specific kinematic structure. To this end, we organize root-centered joint trajectories into topology-informed joint--time images and model global root dynamics through a complementary latent stream. A motion autoencoder conditions local-motion decoding on the root latent, while a text-conditioned Scalable Interpolant Transformer (SiT) jointly generates both latent streams, with supervision on decoded 3D joint positions further constraining generation in motion space. In addition to dataset-specific models, we train a single motion autoencoder on HumanML3D and KIT-ML, followed by a single text-conditioned SiT shared across both datasets, preserving their respective skeletal definitions without skeleton retargeting to a common joint layout. Experiments on HumanML3D and KIT-ML show that our dataset-specific models achieve state-of-the-art performance, while shared training yields further gains on both benchmarks, demonstrating the benefits of shared modeling across heterogeneous skeletal layouts.

papers.title: Simulate Before You Scale: High-Fidelity LLM Inference Planning Without GPUs
papers.abstract: Deploying large language model (LLM) inference at scale requires jointly selecting hardware layout, parallelism strategy, scheduling policy, admission control, and request routing to meet latency and throughput targets. These choices interact: a routing decision that improves cache locality can concentrate load, and an admission threshold that triggers only at saturation allows queues to grow deep enough to degrade critical-tier traffic. Evaluating candidates on GPU clusters is too expensive for iterative exploration, yet existing predictive tools either ignore batching and queueing dynamics or model only fragments of the pipeline. In this paper, we present BLIS, a deterministic, CPU-only discrete-event simulator that models the full inference serving pipeline (admission, routing, scheduling, prefill/decode execution, KV-cache management, and preemption). BLIS pairs analytical basis functions with learned scaling coefficients and overhead terms, fit once globally, to predict step latency without per-model or per-GPU profiling. Across 36 experiments spanning six models and three GPU types, BLIS achieves 6.7% median end-to-end error while running around 200 times faster than real execution. In a configuration search over 420 serving configurations for Llama-2-70B, BLIS identifies a 4-GPU deployment that meets a 300ms mean TTFT service-level objective (SLO), whereas competing tools either require double the GPUs or recommend configurations that fail under load. Two policies evolved entirely in simulation were validated on real hardware and merged into llm-d, a widely adopted open-source platform for distributed LLM serving: an admission policy that reduces critical-tier TTFT P90 by up to 82%, and a flow-control policy that reduces E2E P50 latency by 32-48% on overloaded workloads.

papers.title: Explicit Solutions in a Probabilistic Cellular Automaton Model for Self-Assembled Monolayer Degradation
papers.abstract: Self-assembled monolayers (SAMs), formed by the adsorption of a monomolecular layer of adsorbate onto a surface, have emerged as leading candidates for plat- forms for electrochemical biosensors. In order to characterize the working age of a SAM-based biosensor, it is necessary to understand the long-term degradation of the monolayer, with particular emphasis on the intermolecular forces present in the self-assembly process. In this work, discrete- and continuous-time proba- bilistic cellular automaton (PCA) models for the degradation of SAMs involving adsorbate-adsorbate interactions are proposed in which adsorbate molecules desorb at a rate dependent only on the number of adsorbed neighbors. Impor- tantly, we make no assumptions on the relationship between degradation rate and adsorbed neighbors. Using techniques from generating function theory and complex analysis, the expected degradation curve is solved for explicitly in one dimension and shown to be a sigmoid curve related to the Gompertz function.

papers.title: Bounds for the residue of Dedekind zeta functions under GRH and applications
papers.abstract: Let $κ_{\mathbb{K}}$ be the residue at $1$ of the Dedekind zeta function of a number field $\mathbb{K}$. We prove explicit upper and lower bounds for $κ_{\mathbb{K}}$ under the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis (GRH). Previous explicit bounds of comparable generality are weaker and require a weak form of Artin's holomorphy conjecture: our bounds improve the constants while assuming only GRH for the relevant Dedekind zeta functions. The new lower bound enables all imaginary quadratic fields with class number $\leq 2000$ to be detected (assuming GRH). Furthermore, we demonstrate that the upper bound can be significantly reduced when considering extensions of any fixed, nontrivial field.

papers.title: Do Artificial Neural Networks Need Dendritic Nanotubes? Two Reasons for Shrinking Importance Estimates in Continual Learning
papers.abstract: Regularization-based continual learning protects each parameter in proportion to an estimate of its importance, yet these estimates come from finite samples and heuristics and are used as if they were exact. We report four studies that start from a biologically inspired mechanism and end with a statistical explanation of it. Motivated by dendritic nanotubes, we let transient lateral links diffuse importance tags between hidden units. Links between co-active units gave no significant gain, but random links with lifetimes of 25 or 200 steps raised final accuracy on 20-task Permuted MNIST by 1.5 to 2.6 points. We show that random diffusion implements linear shrinkage of importance toward the layer mean in expectation. A simulation of the link process alone predicts shrinkage weights of 0.23 and 0.52 for these lifetimes, and graph-free shrinkage at 0.25 and 0.5 reproduces both the accuracy and the dispersion of the consolidated importance, while every activity-dependent rule did worse than random links. A five-seed screen across EWC, SI, and MAS found nominal gains for SI and MAS on Permuted MNIST and losses on task-incremental Split CIFAR-100, where forgetting was small and shrinkage cost plasticity. Varying the number of importance samples then separates two mechanisms on Permuted MNIST. For EWC, the gain fell by about ten points per tenfold increase in samples, from 19.6 points with 10 samples to -0.4 with 1000, a variance effect. For MAS, a gain of about one point persisted at 1000 samples, consistent with a bias in the importance measure rather than noise. Shrinkage had no detectable effect for MAS on a domain-incremental CIFAR-100 benchmark. Finally, we show that a standard heteroscedastic empirical Bayes rule shrinks the largest Fisher-type estimates most, which may explain its poor results, and point to a log-scale alternative.

papers.title: Quantum Signal Processing Phase Factorization via Logarithmic Derivatives
papers.abstract: Quantum signal processing (QSP) requires the efficient computation of phase factors associated with a polynomial transformation. One existing stable factorization method avoids direct root finding but relies on Prony's method to recover a polynomial from weighted power sums of its roots (arXiv:2202.02671). We present a modification of this approach that eliminates Prony's method by using the logarithmic derivative of an associated polynomial. Because the logarithmic derivative has the same residue at every root after accounting for multiplicity, its Fourier coefficients directly yield the unweighted power sums of the roots inside the unit disk. The Newton--Girard identities then recover the coefficients of the corresponding polynomial without computing its roots. The resulting algorithm has $O(d\log^2 d)$ computational complexity and simplifies the factorization procedure of the original method. In numerical experiments on Hamiltonian simulation, eigenstate filtering, matrix inversion, and the Fermi--Dirac operator, our implementation computes phase factors in seconds with maximum errors on the order of $10^{-12}$.

papers.title: Variance Fingerprints: Component-Wise Identification of Content Factors by Augmentation Design
papers.abstract: Augmentation-based self-supervised learning can recover the content shared across views without separating its underlying factors into individual coordinates. We ask whether augmentations can be designed to make those factors identifiable. Our approach allows content factors to fluctuate across augmented views while preserving their mean for each source instance. Each instance receives a fixed, recorded set of augmentation strengths that controls how much its factors fluctuate. When factors respond differently to changes in these strengths, their patterns of variation provide information that distinguishes them. Under suitable decoder and support assumptions, we prove that these differences identify individual factors in a conditional Gaussian model, up to permutation, scaling, and translation. We then develop a learner that uses the recorded strengths to estimate these patterns jointly across instances, enabling learning from few views per instance. Synthetic experiments demonstrate near-perfect factor recovery through nonlinear mixing. Controlled dSprites experiments show improved coordinate alignment using augmentations that target known factors, even without telling the learner which augmentation corresponds to which representation coordinate. These results suggest a route to component identification in self-supervised learning: augmentation design can supply identifying information beyond shared content alone.

papers.title: BigCell: Generating Gigapixel Whole-Slide Images
papers.abstract: Whole-slide images (WSIs) are gigapixel-scale digital scans of histopathology tissue and serve as the primary basis for cancer diagnosis. Existing histopathology generative models operate at the patch scale, producing fixed-size tiles of at most 1024$\times$1024 pixels which encompass only a small fraction of the WSI. In contrast, text reports for clinical diagnoses and slide-level diagnostic labels -- the supervision that exists at scale -- operate at the whole-slide level. We present BigCell, the first approach to generate coherent whole-slide histopathology images at native gigapixel resolution. BigCell trains a flow-matching transformer at 2048$\times$2048 pixels on over 120,000 publicly available WSIs spanning multiple organ types. Conditioning on embeddings from pathology foundation models and using an inference-time sliding-window pipeline, BigCell generates coherent images of up to 32,768$\times$32,768 pixels, outperforming prior tile generators on both tile-level and slide-level fidelity metrics. To make gigapixel synthesis practical, we introduce an adaptive scheduling strategy that prioritizes important slide regions, speeding up image generation by over 3\ttimes with minimal quality degradation. Furthermore, we propose the first text-to-image synthesis at 8k resolution by training a separate model that produces dense conditioning grids directly from pathology text reports. We demonstrate that augmenting with synthetic samples improves slide-level few-shot classification performance by up to $18 \%$ over baselines trained on real data.

papers.title: Mn--Cr dopant association in dilute co-doped $\mathrm{ZnAl_2O_4}$ revealed by combined EPR and optical spectroscopy
papers.abstract: Efficient and durable phosphors made from abundant elements underpin energy-saving solid-state lighting, near-infrared light sources for sensing, and X-ray and biomedical imaging. Co-doping is a standard route to brighter phosphors, yet the fate of the co-dopants is rarely established. We combine quantitative electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spin counting with photoluminescence, photoluminescence excitation, and X-ray-excited spectroscopy across two dilute Mn/Cr co-doping series of hydrothermally grown $\mathrm{ZnAl_2O_4}$ nanoparticles and show that the two ions can form an exchange-coupled, edge-sharing Cr--Mn defect complex, with $\mathrm{Mn^{2+/4+}}$ entering an octahedral site next to $\mathrm{Cr^{3+}}$. The octahedral Mn lifts the inversion symmetry of the $\mathrm{Cr^{3+}}$ site and strengthens its parity-forbidden absorption, enhancing the $\mathrm{Cr^{3+}}$ emission without energy transfer. The population of the defect complex follows the law of mass action, and above a threshold Mn concentration, Mn re-partitions into EPR-silent octahedral configurations that quench both emissions. Concentration optima in co-doped phosphors can thus reflect defect speciation, not only energy-transfer efficiency, which opens a structural design handle for brighter emitters.

papers.title: Bipartite Carrier Compression and Machine-Certified Bounds in Schönhage Trilinear Multiplication Tensors
papers.abstract: Under the conditional framework breaking the longstanding O(n log n) integer multiplication barrier (originating from OpenAI Preprint #109), the asymptotic time complexity exponent T(n) = O(n (log n)^{1-κ}) is governed by bounding the second moment E[X^2] < 1 of recursive branching processes over trilinear tensor carrier graphs. In this work, we present a constructive combinatorial optimization over the alternating carrier bipartite matching graphs of the Schönhage trilinear tensor decomposition at dimensions h=23 and h=25. Through an alternating augmenting path search, we uncover a non-trivial cluster-unlocking cascade that eliminates 185 carrier roles (95 roles in h=23 and 90 roles in h=25), reducing the global physical wire width by 377,890 wires from the reviewed baseline W = 177,284,805 down to W = 176,906,915. Evaluated over the exact 10^{-14} rational grid, this wire reduction certifies an improved second-moment coefficient AB = 5,164,059 / 125,000,000,000 and establishes the sharpened conditional exponent κ= 826,215,307 / 20,000,000,000,000 \approx 4.131076535 \times 10^{-5}, strictly surpassing the preceding record on this architecture (κ\approx 4.123864 \times 10^{-5}). All 47 polynomial constraints and 7 rational security margins are audited in exact Q-arithmetic with zero floating-point error, and the fundamental wire reduction identity is formally verified in the Lean 4 interactive theorem prover without unproven axioms.

papers.title: Large-Scale Data Center Integration in Power Systems: Uncertainty and Multi-Scale Variation
papers.abstract: Hyperscale artificial intelligence (AI) data centers are emerging as a structurally new class of electricity demand. Unlike conventional loads, they materialize as spatially concentrated, transmission-level point loads with rapid deployment timelines and converter-dominated dynamics. Their integration is governed by two defining properties: forecast uncertainty in load realization and multi-scale temporal variation spanning sub-seconds to planning horizons. We develop a unified framework that links reliability and affordability to these dimensions through a four-quadrant structure: (reliability, affordability) $\times$ (uncertainty, variation), which integrates probabilistic resource adequacy, generation and transmission expansion, operational security, and market design. Measured traces from a public generative-AI workload dataset show strongly tonal GPU power spectra rather than smooth broadband behavior: harmonic combs at the training-step cadence, and a distinct sub-second periodicity in inference. Across these traces the dominant variance band shifts with workload type (seconds for training and offline inference; tens of seconds and longer for online inference). We report this as a characterization of the measured workloads rather than a universal signature, and take it to indicate that such loads warrant a spectral description rather than a peak-demand one. These signatures directly affect reserve requirements, ramping products, voltage stability, ride-through performance, and harmonic interactions in converter-rich grids. Taken together, the analytical framework and empirical results establish a system-level basis for assessing the reliability and cost implications of large AI data center integration across planning and operational horizons.

papers.title: Thinking with Images without Coordinates
papers.abstract: Recent advances in multi-modal large language models have shifted toward the "thinking with images" paradigm to improve reasoning faithfulness, yet existing methods rely heavily on explicit coordinate- based grounding. We identify two fundamental limitations in this approach, i.e., a semantic gap where sparse regressions miss high-dimensional latent structures, and a resolution gap due to the granularity mismatch between patch-level tokens and pixel-level coordinates. To address these, we propose TiCO (Thinking with images without COordinates). It reformulates visual reasoning as a semantic evidence discovery process within the latent space, and evidence is injected as token-level regions without pixel coordinates. Specifically, TiCO utilizes a dedicated probe token to estimate similarity distributions and performs importance sampling over spatially connected components to generate diverse, semantically dominant evidence rollouts. Extensive experiments across multiple high-resolution and general visual reasoning benchmarks demonstrate that our TiCO consistently outperforms state-of-the-art coordinate-based methods with significantly improved inference efficiency.

papers.title: Schauder and Riesz Bases for Higher-Dimensional Lebesgue Spaces Inspired by ReLU Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Motivated by the role of piecewise linear functions in ReLU neural networks, we study systems of dilated functions in the Lebesgue spaces $L_q([0,1]^d)$, $q\in(1,\infty)$. For a sequence $τ\in\ell_1$ we consider the operator $T_τg(x)=\sum_{k=1}^\infty τ_k g(kx)$ and the function system $\mathcal Z^τ$ obtained by applying it to the trigonometric system. We show that $τ\mapsto T_τ$ is an isomorphism of algebras from $\ell_1$ with the Dirichlet convolution as multiplication onto an algebra of operators and connect the inverse of $T_τ$ to the inverse of $τ$ with respect to the Dirichlet convolution. We give explicit conditions on $τ$, under which the resulting system $\mathcal Z^τ$ is a Schauder basis of $L_q([0,1]^d)$ and, for $q=2$, a Riesz basis for which we estimate the Riesz constants in terms of $τ$. We characterise the Riesz bases of this type in terms of a sequence space of Dirichlet convolution multipliers, and we treat mixed systems of cosine and sine functions with different sequences. Finally, we apply these results to the system generated by two piecewise linear functions inspired by ReLU networks and improve the known lower Riesz constant to $2/3$, independently of the dimension.

papers.title: Characterizations for quasiconformal weighted Bergman spaces
papers.abstract: We establish characterizations of planar quasiconformal mappings in weighted Bergman spaces $A_α^p(\mathbb D)$. For $p>0$ and $α>-1$, our characterization involves the convergence of certain integrals involving superlevel set areas, the Hausdorff measure of boundary superlevel sets, and the averaged derivative. These include quasiconformal analogues of characterizations established by Karafyllia and Karamanlis for conformal mappings. Moreover, for $-1<α\leq 0$, we obtain an additional equivalent characterization in terms of the Hausdorff measure of level sets. The power $α$ is sharp: for every $α>0$, we construct a bounded $K_α$-quasiconformal mapping for which the weighted level-set length integral with exponent $α+2$ diverges.

papers.title: Learning to Sync at the Edge: Client-Side Adaptive Synchronization for Federated Learning
papers.abstract: The scalability and performance of edge federated learning are fundamentally constrained by synchronization bottlenecks. Clients operate under heterogeneous compute, time-varying communication conditions, and, in some settings, privacy constraints, yet synchronization is often still handled with fixed schedules. However, synchronization decisions are often made outside the client, even though the client directly observes local progress, resource state, and communication conditions. We present a client-side reinforcement learning synchronization framework in which each client decides during training whether to upload, download, synchronize bidirectionally, or defer communication. The framework places a lightweight scheduler alongside the local model and formulates synchronization as a resource-aware control problem driven by local learning and system state. We study this framework on two representative edge workloads, spatiotemporal traffic forecasting and image classification. Across both settings, adaptive client-side synchronization improves the accuracy-cost trade-off, reducing system cost in traffic forecasting while maintaining competitive cost and improving final accuracy in image classification. We also consider privacy-constrained settings, where synchronization must account for not only latency and energy but also privacy expenditure. Overall, our results show that synchronization in edge federated learning is better treated as an adaptive client-side control problem than only as a server-side coordination mechanism.

papers.title: RoboFake: Are Deepfake Detectors Ready for Humanoid Face Robots?
papers.abstract: Humanoid face robots can now move their lips in sync with speech and show detailed facial expressions. Give such a robot the face of a real person and drive it with generated speech, and you get a new kind of presentation attack: a face that talks and reacts in front of the camera, recorded as a real object with no edited pixel. We call this a RoboFake and ask whether current defenses are ready for it. We test three public face presentation attack detection (PAD) models and six public deepfake detectors on video of a physical lip-syncing face robot, on a synthesized video of the same robot, and on rendered robot faces. Thresholds are fixed on human data (BPCER 5% on FaceForensics++), and every result is compared with real human faces processed the same way as the robot videos and turned to the same head angle. A small mobile PAD model detects every physical robot frame (APCER 0%) and is not affected by compression, but its BPCER on processed human video rises to 14%; the two PAD models trained on CelebA-Spoof miss the robot in the direct capture, and one of them also misses most panel frames. Among the deepfake detectors, three flag almost every robot frame and two fewer than 7%; masking shows that the response comes from the face but does not track synthesis, and JPEG compression pushes most robot frames below the threshold for some detectors. Our results suggest that current models catch today's robots because their faces do not look human, not because they recognize the attack. We state three testable hypotheses about realistic, interactive RoboFakes.

papers.title: The Thinking Leakage in Reinforcement Learning for LLMs
papers.abstract: Hybrid reasoning models such as the Qwen3 series switch between a THINK mode and a NO-THINK mode through a few chat-template tokens. A popular recipe trains such models with reinforcement learning in NO-THINK mode and reports improved reasoning performance. We provide evidence that much of this gain can be explained by thinking leakage: the gain comes largely from partially reactivating the reasoning abilities of the original model's THINK mode instead of learning enhanced reasoning behavior. We train Qwen3-1.7B, 4B, and 8B with GRPO in NO-THINK mode. As accuracy improves, responses become longer and more reflective, are increasingly judged by the original model to resemble its own thinking, and the model's internal activations shift toward its THINK mode. We then investigate at the level of weights, activations, and attention heads: scaling the RL update further elicits THINK-mode behavior and approaches THINK-mode accuracy but does not exceed it; in Qwen3-8B, replacing a low-dimensional THINK-related activation subspace of the RL-trained model with its original-model value removes most of the RL gain, and the reverse exchange transfers a considerable fraction of the gain to the original model; and the RL-induced shift passes through the attention heads that read the empty think block. We further identify a possible mechanism in the GRPO training signal: responses favored by the advantage-weighted update are more THINK-like, and a gradient step computed from this signal moves the model toward its THINK state. Thus, gains in NO-THINK mode can largely reflect reactivation of reasoning abilities already present in the original model.

papers.title: Solution of a system of Hamilton-Jacobi equations on a network
papers.abstract: We extend the study of Hamilton-Jacobi equations on networks from a single equation to a weakly coupled system of two equations on a star graph, and we develop a numerical scheme for it. Instead of prescribing the boundary values and imposing a junction condition, we compute the solution on each branch from its outer vertex toward the junction and determine the boundary values for which these branchwise solutions agree at the junction. On each branch, we replace the right-hand sides by their cell averages and solve the resulting problems exactly on every cell. This gives an iteration whose limits we compute in closed form. From these limits, the values of the discrete solution at the junction are affine functions of the boundary values on the branch, with a $2 \times 2$ matrix whose rows sum to one and whose determinant factors into explicit contributions of the cells. We use these formulas to characterize the boundary values that give solutions continuous at the junction and monotone on every branch: when the matrices are nonsingular, the admissible boundary values of one branch form a convex polygon, bounded by conditions on the difference of the two components and by positivity conditions, and the boundary values on the other branches follow from them. We also treat the singular case, and we illustrate the results with numerical experiments.

papers.title: Establishing the role of thickness in LaOBr; an alternative gate dielectric for vdW heterostructures
papers.abstract: In electronic devices, the quality of the dielectric material is determined by figures of merit such as the band gap, leakage onset field, breakdown field and the number of built-in defects, which can all limit device performance. An additional and important metric to consider is the strength of the dielectric constant. Hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) is the benchmark gate dielectric for two-dimensional van der Waals heterostructures, owing to its wide bandgap, and atomically flat interface. At the same time, its dielectric constant (2--4) highlights the opportunity to explore alternative higher-permittivity van der Waals dielectrics that provide stronger electrostatic control. Previous work established lanthanum oxybromide (LaOBr), a layered dielectric with a predicted dielectric constant of 12.5, as a potential dielectric for van der Waals heterostructures. Using graphene field-effect devices with LaOBr, we show that the leakage-onset and breakdown fields decrease systematically with thickness. Dual-gate capacitance measurements combined with a dead-layer model reveal a bulk dielectric constant of $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{bulk}} = 12.2$, in agreement with theory, while interfacial dead-layers cause the effective dielectric constant to vary from 6 to 11 across multiple thicknesses. Benchmarked against established gate dielectrics, LaOBr combines breakdown fields comparable to hBN with dielectric constants 2 to 3 times larger. By establishing the operating regime of devices with various thicknesses, we further confirm the advantage of LaOBr over hBN for high-capacitance gate-dielectric operation. These results validate LaOBr as a promising dielectric for integration into two-dimensional heterostructures, and establish thickness-dependent benchmarking as essential for evaluating emerging layered dielectric materials.

papers.title: Yangian for $\mathfrak{gl}_{2}$ and Gelfand-Tsetlin basis for $\mathfrak{gl}_{n}$
papers.abstract: We construct an explicit realization of finite-dimensional irreducible representations $V_λ$ of $\mathfrak{gl}_{n}$ using the representation theory of $\mathrm{Y}(\mathfrak{gl}_{2})$. We consider $V_λ$ as the evaluation representation of $\mathrm{Y}(\mathfrak{gl}_{n})$ and restrict it to the subalgebras $\mathrm{Y}(\mathfrak{gl}_{2})^{(i)}$. Then $V_λ$ is completely reducible as a representation of $\mathrm{Y}(\mathfrak{gl}_{2})^{(i)}$. It allows us to use the explicit formulas for irreducible representations of $\mathrm{Y}(\mathfrak{gl}_{2})$.

papers.title: Inspect Any Crack: An Automated End-to-End Crack Segmentation and Severity Assessment Framework
papers.abstract: Image-based crack analysis is essential for automated infrastructure inspection to reduce the cost, subjectivity, and safety risks of manual surveys. Despite advances in visual crack detection, methods that translate predictions into physically meaningful and engineering-interpretable crack condition information remain limited. To bridge this gap, this study proposes Inspect Any Crack (IAC), an innovative end-to-end crack recognition and condition assessment framework that automatically derives physical geometric measurements and continuous severity scores from concrete-crack imagery. At its core, IAC introduces SACv2-Tiny, an efficient crack segmentation model adapted from a vision foundation model. Trained on the challenging OmniCrack30K dataset, SACv2-Tiny achieved a $62.49\%$ F1-score and $45.45\%$ IoU on the test set and a mean zero-shot F1-score of $69.89\%$ across three unseen datasets, demonstrating robust segmentation that enables downstream analysis with limited post-processing. IAC further processes the predicted masks to quantify physical crack width and affected area using ground-sampling-distance calibration. Validation at 41 caliper-referenced locations yielded a mean relative width error of $7.33\%$. Beyond geometric quantification, IAC introduces a novel continuous crack-condition metric, the Crack Severity Index (CSI), bounded on $[0,100]$, which combines maximum crack width and affected-area ratio into a unified, standards-informed severity measure. Through these developments, IAC advances crack inspection beyond pixel-level recognition toward interpretable and automated infrastructure condition assessment.

papers.title: Polytopal invariance for Lusztig's $q$-weight multiplicities
papers.abstract: Let $Φ$ be an irreducible root system normalized so that long roots have length $\sqrt{2}$, and let $μ\leqλ$ be dominant weights. We associate to $(Φ,μ,λ)$ the convex polytope $$P^Φ_{μ,λ} = (μ+C)\cap(λ-C)\cap(\overline{D}-ρ),$$ where $C=\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}Φ^+$ and $\overline{D}$ is the closed dominant Weyl chamber. We prove that if $P^Φ_{μ,λ}$ and $P^{Φ'}_{μ',λ'}$ are isometric, then $$K^Φ_{λμ}(q)=K^{Φ'}_{λ'μ'}(q),$$ where $K^Φ_{λμ}(q)$ is Lusztig's $q$-analogue of the $μ$-weight multiplicity in the irreducible highest-weight representation $V(λ)$, often called the generalized Kostka-Foulkes polynomial. Moreover, we construct the polynomial directly from the metric shape of the polytope, and we classify when two such polytopes are isometric. Such coincidences are abundant and can occur in different Dynkin types, and in different Dynkin families. By the Lusztig-Kato theorem, the main theorem gives a metric analogue, in the spherical setting, of the combinatorial invariance conjecture for Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials.

papers.title: Stability of vector bundles and reduction mod $p$
papers.abstract: Let $E$ be a vector bundle on a normal complex projective variety. We prove that slope stability of $\mathop{Sym}^2E$ and Zariski density of the reductions of $E$ modulo $p$ that are not strongly geometrically stable imply that the bundle $E$ is projectively unitary flat. This generalizes Shepherd--Barron's result from rank $2$ to arbitrary rank. We also show that if $E$ has rank $\le 3$ we can replace stability of $\mathop{Sym}^2E$ by stability of $E$ but we cannot do so if $E$ has rank $4$. We also generalize these results to reflexive sheaves on some mildly singular normal complex projective varieties.

papers.title: Echo: Error-Compensated 4-Bit Tensor-Parallel Communication for LLM Training and Inference
papers.abstract: Tensor parallelism ends every layer with an all-reduce that sits between two dependent matrix multiplications, so its cost cannot be hidden and grows as compute outpaces interconnect bandwidth. Sending 4-bit instead of 16-bit values would cut this cost by nearly 4x, but the all-reduce must add the values it carries, and rounding the sum injects an error at every call. Model quality depends on how these errors accumulate over layers, yet existing methods treat each call on its own. We present Echo, a 4-bit all-reduce for training and inference that controls the accumulated error. Echo moves data in 4 bits and sums in high precision, so each value is quantized at most twice per call for any number of GPUs. The summation reveals each injected error, and Echo feeds it back into later calls, so old errors cancel instead of accumulating. We prove that the accumulated error stays bounded independently of depth. On A100 GPUs, Echo is 2.09x faster than the 16-bit NCCL all-reduce on 1 GB messages. It speeds up the time to first token by up to 1.16x and the training step by up to 1.09x on an idle interconnect, and by up to 1.44x and 1.38x as background traffic grows. It keeps the average accuracy over seven benchmarks within 0.4 points of 16-bit inference on Qwen3-8B. In 10B-token pretraining, its final loss is less than 0.9% above that of 16-bit training. Echo needs no FP8 or FP4 hardware.

papers.title: Representation homology of involutive algebras and hyperoctaherdral homology
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce and study the (involutive) representation homology of involutive algebras, following the development of representation homology of associative algebra in our earlier papers. Our main motivation is to understand the hyperoctahedral homology of involutive algebras. We show that over a field of characteristic $0$, the hyperoctahedral homology of an involutive algebra is isomorphic (as a graded commutative algebra) to its one dimensional involutive representation homology. This result enables the explicit computation of the hyperoctahedral homology of the universal enveloping algebras of involutive (DG) Lie algebras. For group algebras $k[Γ]$ equipped with the involution $g \mapsto g^{-1}$, we relate the involutive representation homology of $k[Γ]$ to the representation homology of the group $Γ$ with coefficients in $μ_2$, and we show that the latter is the homology of the loop space of the mod $2$ Dold-Thom space of $BΓ$; more generally, we compute the representation homology of $Γ$ with coefficients in an arbitrary diagonalizable group scheme. As a consequence, the hyperoctahedral homology of $k[Γ]$ is concentrated in degree $0$ in characteristic $0$, for every $Γ$.

papers.title: The RNN Homunculus: Learning to Gate Long-Term Memory
papers.abstract: Learning long-range dependencies with recurrent neural networks (RNNs) is difficult because of the vanishing gradient problem. Gated recurrent neural networks like GRUs and LSTMs address this problem and are commonly explained by their ability to create additive copy paths through time. This explanation is correct, but incomplete: useful RNN gate values must themselves be learned, which is typically done with another RNN. We study this gate-learning problem through carefully controlled sequence classification tasks. Our analysis shows that gated architectures struggle when all training samples require long-range memory and thus equally suffer from the vanishing gradient problem. We intervene by adding short-dependency samples which let gated models learn solutions that capture long-dependency samples, but also generalize across different class labels. When properly learned, gated RNNs match or even exceed the test accuracy of modern architectures like Mamba and xLSTM. Overall, our results highlight gate learning as a central part of learning long-range memory and show how training data can support this process by exposing the same task over shorter dependencies.

papers.title: DFIT: A Framework for Building Instrumentation Tools Across Heterogeneous Dataflow Accelerators
papers.abstract: Emerging dataflow accelerators offer exceptional energy efficiency and throughput for machine learning workloads, yet remain largely opaque to developers for performance analysis. Unlike CPUs and GPUs, where instrumentation frameworks enable fine-grained introspection, dataflow hardware exposes little information. This lack of transparency limits the ability of compiler engineers, system designers, and application developers to analyze, tune, or debug accelerator behavior. In this paper, we introduce DFIT (DataFlow Accelerator Instrumentation Tool), an instrumentation framework designed specifically for dataflow architectures. DFIT directly instruments operations, regions, and compiler transformations at the graph IR and backend-lowering stages using semantic program representation. DFIT captures high-level, semantically meaningful data that reflect the true dataflow of computation. These data can be exported for visualization and analysis. Our approach demonstrates how instrumentation can be generalized beyond traditional hardware to support heterogeneous architectures, providing portability without modifying tool logic. By opening the black box of dataflow execution, DFIT establishes a foundation for new classes of performance analysis tools for AI accelerators. It provides a practical path toward reproducible, architecture-aware introspection across heterogeneous systems, bridging the long-standing visibility gap between compiler design, runtime scheduling, and hardware realization. Evaluation across Cerebras, SambaNova, and TPU shows practical overhead of 3.53%-13.62% across instrumentation modes with robust cross-platform portability.

papers.title: TGSR: Text-Grounded Diffusion for Faithful Image Super-Resolution
papers.abstract: Diffusion models have achieved remarkable success in image super-resolution (SR) by leveraging strong generative priors to enhance perceptual quality. However, for textual content, these priors often produce text hallucinations: non-existent or distorted text, which alter scene semantics and compromise model reliability. While recent methods focus on enhancing text generation, they do so indiscriminately, leaving hallucinations fundamentally unresolved. We argue the core problem is a lack of selective control. Therefore, we reformulate text SR as a selective generation problem: text is resolved only when reliable generation is expected, while other scene content is fully super-resolved. We introduce TGSR (Text-Grounded Super-Resolution), a test-time framework that progressively identifies and suppresses likely hallucinated text regions during generation. To enable this, we train dedicated detectors on a large-scale dataset curated from diverse diffusion-based SR outputs. TGSR consistently improves text fidelity across multiple backbones, increasing recognition precision by up to 17.68 points without degrading perceptual quality, underscoring the value of selective control in generative SR.

papers.title: Example of exponential many collisions of identical hard disks in the plane
papers.abstract: We show that the maximal number of nonsimultaneous elastic collisions among $n$ identical hard disks moving freely on the plane is at least exponential in $n$.

papers.title: What does self-supervision add to engineered features for stellar light curves?
papers.abstract: TESS light curves encode a star's pulsation, rotation, binarity and oscillations, among other physical properties, but the survey produces far more light curves than can be labelled by hand. Astronomers have engineered a few dozen physically motivated features from them, which together remain a strong baseline. Previous work has trained encoders on light curves and judged them by their own downstream scores, but has not asked what they add to the engineered features. We pre-train a convolutional encoder on unlabelled TESS light curves to predict each window's latent representation from those of its neighbours. We then freeze it, add its features to the 25 engineered features, and read the combination out with one fixed linear probe on ten tasks: five variability classes, four asteroseismic targets and rotation period. Adding the learned features improves the readout on 7 of 10 tasks over the engineered features alone, where an untrained encoder does not. The combination also outperforms two networks trained end-to-end on the same labelled stars on most tasks. An encoder trained without labels therefore gives astronomers new features that complement the ones they already use rather than replace them.

papers.title: The dimensional reduction of the spin-3 and spin-4 partially broken Fronsdal models
papers.abstract: Here we perform a Kaluza-Klein dimensional reduction from $D+1$ to $D$ dimensions of a partially broken Fronsdal model for spin-3 and spin-4. The reduced models describe massive spin-3 and spin-4 particles without extra propagating modes. They differ from Singh-Hagen models by quadratic terms which vanish on shell, similarly to their higher dimensional massless parents. A covariant description of the reduced models in terms of gauge invariant field combinations naturally leads to higher derivative models, contrary to lower spin cases ($s\le 2$). For both $s=3$ and $s=4$ we have a rather peculiar massless limit. Although their particle content corresponds to the $\pm j$ helicities with $j=0,1, \cdots s$, as expected, they appear intertwined in a non trivial way preventing diagonalization through any local field redefinition.

papers.title: Zero-Crossing Time Lower Bounds for the Homogeneous Super-Twisting Algorithm
papers.abstract: High-frequency switching and chattering are well-known problems in sliding-mode control. Although the super-twisting algorithm produces a continuous control input, the sliding variable may still cross zero repeatedly near the sliding manifold. This paper studies how fast these crossings can occur and whether they can accumulate in finite time for the scalar homogeneous super-twisting algorithm. Two lower bounds on the time required to return to zero are derived, together with a bound on the time needed to complete a full excursion. These results give minimum separation times and upper bounds on the number of crossings associated with excursions above a prescribed amplitude. Although zero crossings may accumulate in finite time, the amplitudes of the complete excursions considered here must vanish and satisfy a summability condition. Thus, crossings associated with excursions above any prescribed nonzero amplitude cannot accumulate in finite time. When the perturbation-rate bound is zero, the estimates recover the scaling imposed by homogeneity. For the classical super-twisting algorithm, the square-root scaling also holds for nonzero perturbation-rate bounds. Numerical simulations illustrate the results.

papers.title: Definition of Multi-Parameter Super-Resolution for Optical Telescopes
papers.abstract: Super-resolution techniques in microscopy are opening new frontiers in biology, and super-resolution for telescope imaging may provide similar benefits for astronomy and space domain awareness. Telescope super-resolution techniques such as multi-plane light conversion and photonic lanterns have been inspired by the ability of mode sorting measurements to extract classical Fisher information closer to the quantum bound than standard telescope imaging. Fisher information analyses for super-resolution imaging systems commonly consider the case of imaging point sources, but often only consider estimating a small subset of the parameters. Furthermore, there has been no demonstration of an estimation algorithm with performance that follows the limit set by the Fisher information when all point source parameters are considered. We provide a framework for defining and analyzing super-resolution using the classical and quantum Fisher information for the multi-parameter estimation problem and demonstrate an algorithm that can achieve the classical Fisher information bound for all the parameters simultaneously.

papers.title: Parametric Families of Minimal Positive Cubature Formulas of Degrees 4 and 6 on the 2-Sphere
papers.abstract: We study minimal positive cubature formulas on the two-dimensional sphere of degrees four and six, with ten and eighteen nodes, respectively. We prove the regularity of Popov's symmetric formulas and establish that their local families of deformations are two-dimensional, up to rotations. We obtain algebraic relations between the weights and pairwise inner products of the nodes. For degree four, we construct a one-parameter family with half-turn symmetry connecting the formulas of Popov and Heo--Xu. We also give a self-contained proof that eighteen nodes are minimal for degree six.

papers.title: cvxoptdes: convex optimal experiment design in R
papers.abstract: The cvxoptdes R-package provides a unified framework to perform convex optimal experiment design and online response optimization for linear, generalized linear and additive, nonlinear, and random intercept mixed models, using exclusively open-source solvers. It supports optimization and augmentation of weighted, penalized and convex constrained continuous designs across a discrete grid of candidate points and rounding to integer-valued designs using point-exchange algorithms or mixed-integer programming for orthogonally constrained designs, including the class of orthogonal minimally aliased response surface (OMARS) designs. Models and design constraints are defined and updated in an object-oriented context with the aim to facilitate the process of sequential (penalized) design augmentation analogous to online design procedures known from active learning and Bayesian optimization.

papers.title: Harmonic numbers and Lerch functions behind falling factorial generating functions
papers.abstract: We study a family of special numbers and polynomials introduced by Simsek whose exponential generating function has as denominator a falling factorial in the exponential variable. Using the partial fraction decomposition of this denominator, each member of the family is expressed by a single finite sum involving Bernoulli polynomials, Apostol Bernoulli polynomials and two variable Fubini polynomials evaluated at reciprocals of integers. A second expansion, around the point where the denominator vanishes, expresses the same numbers through Stirling numbers of the second kind and generalized harmonic numbers, and yields closed formulas for the first few members. We construct a function, built from the Hurwitz zeta function and Lerch s transcendent, which interpolates the polynomials at the negative integers and gives a closed form of a multiple series recently introduced by Pokaz, Ribicic Penava and Simsek, we give an Euler type integral representation for it, and show that the numbers are signed combinations of moments of geometric random variables. Recurrence relations, asymptotics and an extension to arbitrary distinct nodes are also given.

papers.title: Watermarking for Byzantine Robust LLM Training
papers.abstract: LLM watermarking has emerged as a promising approach for detecting downstream model misuse in centralized settings, but extending it to federated learning (FL) presents unique challenges. In particular, FL systems often rely on strong robust aggregators to defend against poisoning attacks. We empirically show that a malicious server can exploit these same aggregators as effective watermark-removal mechanisms during training, causing representative existing LLM watermarking methods to fail detection in the final model. To address this limitation, we formalize the problem as a constrained optimization task and propose CamoMark, an aggregator-agnostic watermarking scheme for embedding robust watermarks in FL. CamoMark optimizes watermarked updates to become inliers, maintaining bounded deviation from the distribution of clean updates, while preserving sufficient watermark signal for reliable detection. Evaluated on Qwen fine-tuned on the Alpaca dataset, CamoMark achieves a detection confidence of $p$-value $= 1.82\times10^{-2}$ using only 3.3% watermarked data. The watermark also remains robust to a range of post-training removal attacks, including continued fine-tuning on clean data, pruning, and model distillation. At higher watermark ratios, detection confidence improves substantially, reaching $p$-value $= 5.11\times10^{-11}$ at a 13.3% watermark ratio.

papers.title: Layer-wise Input Recoverability in Deep Neural Networks
papers.abstract: The inner workings of deep neural networks are still not well understood. The information bottleneck framework, which characterizes deep networks by the mutual information between their hidden representations and the network's input, has been used to identify compression of input information with respect to an input image and output labels. We instead study how much of a layer's own input is recoverable from the layer's output in convolutional neural networks (CNNs). A convolutional layer applies its filters to one input patch at a time, so we evaluate recoverability on sampled input patches with a reconstruction-based probe and not on the entire feature map. The probe's size thus depends on channels and kernel size and not on feature map size, which lets our method scale to deep CNNs with wide feature maps. For each layer, we compare pretrained, random, and reconstruction-optimized encoders, using linear and linear-plus-residual-MLP decoders. We measure recoverability as $R^2$ between input patches and their reconstructions on a held-out set. Across nine ImageNet CNNs, recoverability generally decreases with depth but is more consistently predicted by the compression of the layer. Learning-attributed recoverability, the difference between pretrained and random encoders, is not uniform across architectures. We introduce single-property random controls, which transfer one pretrained property onto a random encoder, and find that each control changes recoverability with a consistent sign across models: copying pretrained singular vectors tends to raise recoverability, while copying the pretrained singular-value spectrum or activation sparsity lowers it.

papers.title: Inner and outer isometries of graphs of polynomials
papers.abstract: We classify graphs of complex polynomials in one variable up to isometry, both for the inner (length) distance and for the outer (Euclidean) distance of $\mathbb{C}^2\cong\mathbb{R}^4$. For polynomials $p,q$ with $°p\ge 2$ we show that the graphs of $p$ and $q$ are inner isometric if and only if they are outer isometric, if and only if $p(z)=α\,q(βz+h)+k$ or $p(z)=α\,\bar q(βz+h)+k$ for some $α,β,h,k\in\mathbb{C}$ with $|α|=|β|=1$, where $\bar q$ denotes the polynomial with conjugate coefficients. Moreover, every inner isometry between such graphs is the restriction of an isometry of $\mathbb{C}^2$; in this sense graphs of complex polynomials are isometrically rigid. We contrast this with the real case, where the two distances behave very differently: the graphs of any two real polynomials are inner isometric, whereas, for degree at least $2$, outer isometries are generated by translations, reflections in horizontal and vertical lines and half-turns.

papers.title: The Exact Degree Threshold for Complement Connectivity
papers.abstract: For a graph $G$, we investigate sufficient degree conditions under which either $G$ or its complement $\overline{G}$ is $k$-connected. Motivated by a theorem of Hellwig and Volkmann, we introduce the notion of complement connectivity admissible pairs and define the parameter $\mathcal{C}(k)$ as the minimum degree threshold guaranteeing that either $G$ or $\overline{G}$ is $k$-connected whenever $δ(G)\ge\mathcal{C}(k)$ and $Δ(G)\le |V(G)|-1-\mathcal{C}(k)$. We prove that $\mathcal{C}(k)=2k-2$ for every $k\ge2$, thereby determining the exact degree threshold. As an application, we derive a Nordhaus--Gaddum type product condition, showing that for $n\ge4k-5$, the condition $δ(G)δ(\overline{G}) \ge (2k-3)(n-2k+2)$ guarantees that either $G$ or $\overline{G}$ is $k$-connected. Finally, we show that no analogous product condition depending only on $k$ can exist.

papers.title: GeoFix: Geometry Fixing for 4D Consistent Generation
papers.abstract: Video diffusion models increasingly serve as priors for 4D generation, but the generated videos often lack geometric consistency. Recent approaches address this through post-training by designing geometric rewards, yet this can degrade texture and fine detail, requiring auxiliary appearance rewards and careful reward balancing. To address this challenge, we propose GeoFix, a unified framework that improves geometric consistency and visual quality with a single geometric reward, applicable to both training and inference-time reward alignment. Our reward measures cross-view depth consistency in static scene regions, targeting structural inconsistencies without directly constraining appearance or penalizing valid object motion. Crucially, depth agreement increases with camera field-of-view overlap even in real videos and 4D datasets, allowing a smaller camera movement to be mistaken for better geometry. We account for this effect by calibrating the reward against the overlap-dependent trend. GeoFix achieves a 39% improvement in WorldScore 3D consistency and a 4% increase in VBench Quality Score.

papers.title: Controllable Diverse Sampling through Pullback Directions
papers.abstract: Conditional diffusion models can generate high-quality images that align closely with a given prompt. However, samples generated from different random seeds may remain visually similar, limiting creative exploration. Existing approaches can increase variation, but often require additional optimization or sampling overhead, while stronger perturbations may introduce distortions that degrade image quality or prompt alignment. We propose a training-free method that leverages the local pullback geometry induced by the mapping from the conditioning-embedding space to the image space to identify directions of maximal output sensitivity. By steering different sampling trajectories along these directions, we encourage distinct generations while maintaining consistency with the conditioning signal. Experiments on MS-COCO and BrushNet show the efficacy of the method in improving diversity on prompt-conditioned image generation and inpainting.

papers.title: Cost-Aware Iteration Allocation for Sequential Multi-Fidelity First-Order Optimization
papers.abstract: Optimization can be expensive when evaluating the objective and its gradient requires a large dataset or a costly simulation. A cheaper approximation (i.e., a surrogate) can provide a useful initial point, but the work spent on that surrogate must be justified by the saving on the original problem. We study how many iterations to perform on each surrogate before switching to a more accurate objective. For a given sequence of smooth, strongly convex objectives, we use convergence bounds and distances between minimizers to construct a model of the total iteration cost. We derive closed-form two-level budgets for Nesterov's accelerated gradient method and a convex reformulation for multiple levels. We also develop an online switching rule that updates the cost comparison using the gradient at the current point. We test the techniques on a logistic-regression problem using HIGGS data. The online rule reduces weighted iteration cost in all 27 tested configurations, with a median cost of 52.8% of direct optimization. The results illustrate why updating the switching decision can be more effective than fixing the budget from an initial convergence bound.

papers.title: Diagnosing Generalization Boundaries in AI-Based Vulnerability Detection via Calibrated Embedding Distances
papers.abstract: High benchmark scores in learning-based vulnerability detection mask severe degradation under distribution shifts. This paper demonstrates that calibrated embedding geometry exposes these hidden generalization boundaries on syntactically similar vulnerable and patched code pairs. An evaluation of CodeBERT and Qwen2.5-Coder across pattern, project, and temporal shifts on a strictly paired dataset reveals three main findings. First, whitened intermediate-layer embeddings with local nearest-neighbour scoring separate unfamiliar samples with a mean out-of-distribution AUROC of 0.739 (RQ1). Second, distance scores reveal a shift-specific reliability gradient where accuracy drops by over 35 percentage points and cross-project shifts cause the sharpest degradation, even though temporal shifts drift geometrically farthest (RQ2). Third, false positives on patched code systematically correlate with geometric proximity to vulnerable training neighbourhoods, increasing from 9.4% in the lowest-risk decile to 58.8% in the highest (RQ3). These calibrated distances establish a diagnostic signal that maps representation geometry directly to model degradation without requiring auxiliary models.

papers.title: Adaptive Utility Optimization for Stochastic Renewal Systems
papers.abstract: This paper treats a system that performs back-to-back tasks. Each new task has a random matrix of parameters and can be processed in various processing modes. The processing mode determines the task duration and a vector of rewards (penalties are viewed as negative rewards). The reward vector can include quality, profit, or $-1$ times a penalty such as cost or energy. In wireless applications, tasks correspond to data transmissions and rewards/penalties correspond to throughput and distortion. Prior work treats the problem of maximizing the time average of a reward process subject to constraints. This paper seeks to maximize a concave function of the time average reward vector. This is difficult because it involves a multi-variable function of ratios of averages. We develop a single algorithm that does not know the probability distribution of the random task matrices. The algorithm is adaptive, meaning it responds efficiently (with optimal adaptation time) when probabilities change.

papers.title: Revealing New Leakage Paths in GAAFETs using Predictive First-Principles Simulations
papers.abstract: Gate-All-Around Field-Effect Transistors (GAAFETs) are emerging as successors to Fin Field-Effect Transistors (FinFETs) and are central to continued scaling at advanced semiconductor nodes. Despite their improved electrostatic control, recent measurements show that the drain current in GAAFETs deviates strongly from thermionic behavior at negative gate voltages, increasing as the gate voltage becomes more negative. This leakage has been attributed to direct gate-drain tunneling through the high-$k$ dielectric, enhanced by drain-induced dielectric barrier lowering (DIDBL). Here, we use predictive, charge-self-consistent Non-Equilibrium Green Function (NEGF) simulations based on the Contact Block Reduction (CBR) method to spatially resolve this leakage pathway in GAAFETs. Unlike approaches based primarily on phenomenological leakage models, our first-principles, multi-terminal quantum-transport framework treats the source, drain, and gate as current-carrying quantum-mechanical contacts and resolves the local current density throughout the device.
